544513|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue INR 53.8 crore; standalone revenue up 7.8% YoY to INR 42 crore, Ind AS EBITDA margin 56.3% consolidated.
544513|2026-06.overview: Standalone workspace revenue rose 7.8% YoY to INR 42 crore, with consolidated revenue at INR 53.8 crore and Ind AS consolidated EBITDA up 14.7% to INR 30.3 crore. Operational portfolio grew to 1.13 million sq ft (17,294 seats, 27 centers, 12 cities) with occupancy at 91.93%. Post-quarter, the company raised INR 100 crore of 11.75% secured NCDs (36 months) and encumbered about 19.65% of equity, with promoter holding stated at 36.81%. Management highlighted a pipeline of 2.31 million sq ft signed for future consumption, though analyst questions on Ahmedabad per-sq-ft economics, lease-inclusive leverage and Q4 margin drop were answered only partially.

segments.name: Managed workspace (standalone)
segments.commentary: INR 42 crore revenue, recurring; occupied seats 15,899 vs 12,534 YoY; occupancy 91.93% vs 88.6%. Enterprise clients ~70% of revenue vs 52% a year ago; revenue-to-rent 2.63x.

segments.name: Needle & Thread (design and build)
segments.commentary: Balance of consolidated revenue (about INR 11.8 crore implied), one-time in nature and booked on project completion/milestone under Ind AS. FY26 one-time revenue was INR 57 crore per management.

segments.name: Tier 2 cities
segments.commentary: About 80% of operational SBA in Tier 2 cities, contributing ~74% of standalone revenue in the quarter.

guidance_outlook: Management expects revenue from signed capacity to progressively show up as centers move into operation; no numerical revenue guidance given.

Ahmedabad development-management project (~8.6 lakh sq ft, Ambli Bopal Road): fit-out capex ~INR 100 crore, expected ~8,500 seats and ~INR 120 crore revenue potential once handed over; no timeline stated.
Total identified portfolio ~3.63 million sq ft across 40 centers with 52,000+ operational seats; FY27 framed as year of executing signed assets and expanding into new territories.
INR 100 crore NCD to reflect in financials from Q2 onwards; ~INR 55 crore of existing debt repaid.
Global tokenization platform being set up outside India; entity incorporation commenced, no timeline given.
capex_capacity: Operational 1.13 million sq ft; 0.19 million sq ft under fit-out; 2.31 million sq ft signed for future consumption (total identified ~3.63 million sq ft, 40 centers).

Management said ~12 lakh sq ft operational area of which ~75% is company-built, roughly 9 lakh sq ft at ~INR 1,300/sq ft, i.e., ~INR 118 crore of fit-out investment to date (excluding refurbishment and deposits on future sites).
Development-management model covers ~1.4 million sq ft across Ahmedabad and Jaipur.
New-center ramp: 75-90 days from handover to client fit-out; ~6-9 months to maturity, per management.
Management said unspent IPO proceeds are still with the company and will be deployed as properties under construction are handed over.
demand_pricing: Ahmedabad realisations management cited at INR 100-125 per sq ft per month for a full operating year; Capital One (~3.15 lakh sq ft, 95% pre-leased) became operational toward end FY26.
Analyst's implied Capital One figure of ~INR 1,044/sq ft/yr was reconciled by management to ~INR 87/sq ft/month in year one, reflecting rent-free and fit-out periods; 8-9 billable months assumed.
Enterprise/GCC demand: management said it is in talks with clients for full-spectrum GCC solutions in Bangalore and Hyderabad.
Scalex Advisory (GCC full-service JV, ~12% stake held by DevX) to focus on GIFT City; managed-office GCC leads to be redirected to DevX.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 145 crore at end FY26
vs INR 89 crore at end FY26; net debt/equity 0.4x vs 0.48x; net debt/EBITDA (IGAAP) 1.04x vs 2.10x

qa_highlights.question: Shubham Padhiyar (Chhattisgarh Investments) asked why Mumbai Central revenue fell from INR 14 crore to INR 11 crore despite Noida revenue rising, given a Noida centre closure.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Noida centre closed at the very end of FY26 after litigation, and that Noida (three centres) did about INR 11.5 crore operational revenue before closure, with roughly INR 4.5 crore now lost from the closed centre. The analyst's figures were disputed (INR 9 crore vs INR 11.5-12 crore), and the reconciliation was deferred to email.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst's implied Capital One revenue of about INR 1,050 per sq ft per year (INR 2.7-3 crore a month on ~3.15 lakh sq ft) versus Ahmedabad portfolio at about INR 2,500 per sq ft per year.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Ahmedabad realisations are INR 100-125 per sq ft per month (about INR 1,200-1,500 a year), and that INR 2,500 a year is not the right figure. The INR 1,044 figure equals about INR 87 per sq ft per month in year one, reflecting rent-free and fit-out periods; management assumed 8-9 billable months. Management declined to confirm the analyst's FY26 Ahmedabad revenue of about INR 78 crore and asked for an email.

qa_highlights.question: What share of revenue is recurring versus one-time, and how much capex has been spent on the 1.13 million sq ft portfolio?
qa_highlights.answer: Of INR 53.8 crore consolidated revenue, INR 42 crore is managed office (recurring) and the balance is Needle & Thread one-time revenue. FY26 Needle & Thread one-time revenue was INR 57 crore. About 75% of the ~12 lakh sq ft is company-built, roughly 9 lakh sq ft at about INR 1,300 per sq ft, i.e. about INR 118 crore of fit-out investment, excluding refurbishment and deposits on future sites.

qa_highlights.question: Mukul Bhushan (Raru Family Office) asked to disclose lease-inclusive leverage each quarter: debt-to-equity ~2x and ROCE ~9% including about INR 226 crore of lease liability, versus the presented 0.78x and 14%.
qa_highlights.answer: Parin Shah did not confirm or refute the lease-inclusive figures. He explained the ROCE/ROE lag: 75-90 days from handover to fit-out and client onboarding, and 6-9 months to maturity. He said ROCE is 14% and ROE 7%, and that unspent IPO funds will be deployed as under-construction properties are handed over.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone EBITDA margin fall to 59.2% in Q4 from 64% a year earlier, and should the FY27 model use 60.5% or 59.2%?
qa_highlights.answer: Parin Shah attributed the Q4 drop to expenses he described as one-time in nature, and said it was not a structural margin decline. He cited standalone Ind AS margin of 66% in Q1 and peer margins of 60-65%. Consolidated margin is lower because Needle & Thread books revenue on project completion or milestone under Ind AS. No FY27 margin figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: How does the Scalex Advisory non-compete work, what is DevX's stake, and can DevX still do GCC business?
qa_highlights.answer: Umesh Uttamchandani said Scalex is a JV of DevX, Savvy (GIFT City developer) and Talati & Talati, with DevX holding about 12%. It targets full-spectrum GCC solutions, limited to GIFT City, and standalone managed-office leads are redirected to DevX. DevX continues GCC business (payroll and facility management) and is in talks for GCC solutions in Bangalore and Hyderabad.

risks_watch: Revenue reconciliation gaps: city-wise and Ahmedabad revenue figures disputed on the call and deferred to email; watch for the written responses and whether they close the gap.

Lease-inclusive leverage: the analyst's estimate of about 2x debt/equity and about 9% ROCE including about INR 226 crore of lease liabilities was not answered. Management asked for quarterly disclosure of this view to be declined; watch whether it is added.

Ramp execution: 2.31 million sq ft signed but not yet operational, with 0.19 million sq ft under fit-out. Revenue conversion timelines (75-90 days to handover-fit-out, 6-9 months to maturity) are long, and no revenue timeline for the Ahmedabad 8.6 lakh sq ft project was given.

Debt and promoter pledge: INR 100 crore 11.75% NCD over 36 months from Q2; about 19.65% of equity encumbered; promoter holding 36.81% (about 37.29% after warrant conversion) against a 19.65% covenant floor. Watch for any changes to covenants or pledge levels.

Margin trajectory: Q4 FY26 standalone margin of 59.2% vs 64% a year earlier was attributed to one-time expenses without quantification. Consolidated Ind AS margin of 56.3% is diluted by Needle & Thread's milestone-based revenue recognition.

Early-stage new ventures: tokenisation platform outside India (no timeline), AI infrastructure launchpad, and Scalex (operations only just starting, GIFT City focus). Monitor incorporation and any capital commitments.
key_quotes: So the operational number although being 1.12 million square feet, there is an additional 0.19 million square feet, which is under fit out.
It is important to note that this is not a borrowed money, there is no bank, no loan, and no repayment schedule attached to it.
Against this requirement, the current promoter shareholding is 36.81%, which is significantly above the prescribed minimum requirement.
I would appreciate if you can reach out to our email address of Investor Relations team and we would be happy to address those questions.
544513|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on portfolio growth, occupancy and the signed pipeline, but defensive and evasive when pressed on city-level revenue, Ahmedabad per-sq-ft economics, lease-inclusive leverage and the Q4 margin fall. Several specific questions were deferred to email follow-up.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Standalone Ind AS margin 66% and consolidated Ind AS EBITDA margin 56.3% vs 47.4%, but Q4 FY26 standalone margin fell to 59.2% from 64% on unquantified one-time expenses and Needle & Thread milestone revenue dilutes consolidated margin; no FY27 margin figure given.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 0.19m sq ft already under fit-out and 2.31m sq ft signed for future consumption (total identified ~3.63m sq ft, 40 centres), with 75-90 days from handover to fit-out; Ahmedabad 8.6 lakh sq ft has no timeline, so its timing stays unclear.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Occupied seats rose to 15,899 from 12,534 YoY and occupancy to 91.93% from 88.6%, with Capital One (~3.15 lakh sq ft, 95% pre-leased) ramping; enterprise share of revenue 70% vs 52%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation at 91.93% is above the 80% threshold, the Ahmedabad project needs ~INR 100 crore of fit-out capex, and the INR 100 crore NCD plus unspent IPO proceeds are earmarked for handovers.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No numerical revenue guidance was given, and management declined to confirm the analyst's Ahmedabad and Capital One figures, so there is no base for an upgrade.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Revenue conversion from signed space is slow (6-9 months to maturity), the Noida closure removed ~INR 4.5 crore of revenue, and city-level figures are disputed; no numerical guidance exists to cut.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Scalex GCC full-service JV is just starting operations (DevX ~12% stake, GIFT City focus), and the tokenisation platform and AI launchpad are at incorporation stage with no timeline.

rows.label: 2.31m sq ft signed for future consumption
rows.when: next 2-4 quarters as centres hand over
rows.why: Signed space of 2.31m sq ft against 1.13m sq ft operational means a large pipeline is still to convert, with 0.19m sq ft already under fit-out.

rows.label: Net debt down to INR 81 crore from INR 89 crore
rows.why: Net debt/EBITDA (IGAAP) fell to 1.04x from 2.10x, and gross debt is INR 135 crore after ~INR 55 crore repayment, though the INR 100 crore 11.75% NCD is added from Q2.

rows.label: Promoter pledge at 19.65% of equity against 36.81% holding
rows.why: About 19.65% of equity is encumbered, and the stated covenant floor equals that level, so any further pledge or covenant change would be a risk to watch.

tone.note: Management was confident on occupancy (91.93%), the 2.31m sq ft signed pipeline and enterprise mix, but deferred city-level revenue, Ahmedabad per-sq-ft economics, lease-inclusive leverage and the Q4 margin drop to email; analysts pressed on each of these.

544513|2026-09.headline: Dev Accelerator Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 54.8% YoY to a record INR 80.2 crores, with PAT tripling to INR 5.5 crores.
544513|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations reached a record INR 80.2 crores in Q2 FY27, up 54.8% YoY and 49.2% QoQ, with consolidated EBITDA of INR 40.8 crores at a 50.8% margin. Profit before tax rose to INR 6.3 crores from INR 1.7 crores and PAT to INR 5.5 crores from INR 1.8 crores. Operational portfolio grew to about 1.16 million sq ft with occupancy of 91%, and the Capital One asset in Ahmedabad became operational. Net debt rose to INR 185 crores from INR 89 crores at the end of last year after a INR 100 crore NCD raise in August 2026. The call had no analyst Q&A; management only presented prepared remarks.

financial_highlights.change: +54.8% YoY vs INR 51.8 crores; +49.2% QoQ vs INR 53.8 crores
+34.4% YoY; margin vs 49.2% in H1 FY26
vs INR 1.9 crores in prior-year period

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated cash EBIT (Q2 FY27, EBITDA less lease rentals)
financial_highlights.change: vs INR 9.1 crores, margin 17.5% last year (+625 bps)
+58.8% YoY; margin vs 66.6% in Q2 FY26
INR 71.6 crores as stated on call
vs INR 89 crores at end of last year

segments.name: Standalone (office space solutions)
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue INR 63 crores (+51.7% YoY) with EBITDA INR 43.9 crores at 69.7% margin. H1 standalone revenue INR 105 crores and H1 EBITDA margin 68.2%.

segments.name: Design and build (Neddle and Thread)
segments.commentary: External-client business generated about INR 30 crores in H1 FY27. This excludes design and build work done for DevX's own centres.

segments.name: Technology (SaaSJoy Solutions Pvt Ltd)
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue about INR 2.8 crores. Management said external revenue has not yet been monetised; the unit mainly builds internal technology capability.

guidance_outlook: Pipeline of 17 new centres covering about 2.8 million sq ft (about 3.5x current size), taking the platform to about 4.16 million sq ft across 49 centres; to be commissioned in phases.

Ahmedabad development-management project of about 8.6 lakh sq ft (about 8,500 seats) expected to generate about INR 120 crores of revenue at scale; intended investment about INR 100 crores over time in fit-outs, furniture and security deposits.
H2 FY27 priorities: bring new centres into operation, deepen enterprise relationships, grow GCC services, and improve cash conversion through faster billing and collection.
Management expects contributions from newly signed capacity to reflect in coming quarters as it becomes operational.
capex_capacity: Operational portfolio about 1.16 million sq ft at end-Sept 2026 vs 0.89 million sq ft a year earlier; 17,400 operational seats across 28 centres in 12 cities and 6 states.
Occupied seats 15,800 vs 12,019 in Q2 FY26; occupancy 91%.
Capital One (Amritabh Bhopal Road, Ahmedabad), about 3.15 lakh sq ft, became operational with about 95% pre-leased.

Development-management model: DevX does not acquire land or fund construction; investment limited to security deposits, fit-outs and operating infrastructure. Assets to be Grade A, IGBC Platinum-targeted.
Management is in talks with larger REIT players about its existing PropCo/OpCo assets; no transaction announced.
demand_pricing: Enterprise clients were about 75% of revenue from operations, vs 70% in Q1 FY27 and 65% in Q2 FY26.
Revenue-to-rent ratio improved significantly from 2.4x a year earlier; brokerage fell to 1.13% of revenue from 1.6%.
About 78% of operational area is in Tier 2 states; target GCC clients have USD 250 million to USD 750 million revenue.
Other expenses fell to 1.7% of revenue from 11%; employee costs largely flat in H1 despite revenue growth.
Industry context cited from CBRE and Colliers reports: GCCs took about 42% of top-9 city leasing; flex operators leased 12.6 million sq ft in top-7 markets (+37%).
risks_watch: Net debt more than doubled to INR 185 crores from INR 89 crores at FY26 end, while the company says it is well below equity.
Cash conversion is a stated H2 priority; faster billing and collection needed as fit-outs and new centres are commissioned.
Execution risk on 17 new centres (2.8 million sq ft) and the Ahmedabad 8.6 lakh sq ft project, including about INR 100 crores of planned spending.
SaaSJoy has not yet monetised external revenue; the GCC services strategy is still early.
Lease liabilities under Ind-AS are large; management asks investors to assess borrowings and lease commitments separately.
Possible REIT transactions on PropCo/OpCo assets are unconfirmed.
544513|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on the quarter's growth, margins and occupancy, with a clear emphasis on execution. Management was more cautious on balance-sheet items, explaining lease liabilities and stressing cash conversion as the next focus.
key_quotes: This quarter, to be very honest, has been very meaningful to us because we have achieved the highest ever quarterly revenue of INR 80.2 crores.
We by no means intend to own the asset, neither do we intend to get into construction activities.
For the second half, one of our clear priorities is cash conversion.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Consolidated EBITDA margin rose to 50.8% in Q2 FY27 from 49.2% in H1 FY26, cash EBIT margin rose 625 bps to 23.8%, and other expenses fell to 1.7% of revenue from 11%, though new centre fit-out costs and lease rentals may dilute it.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Operational area is about 1.16 mn sq ft with Capital One (3.15 lakh sq ft, ~95% pre-leased) already live, and a 17-centre pipeline of about 2.8 mn sq ft (about 3.5x current size) is being commissioned in phases, with timing not dated for most of it.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Occupied seats rose to 15,800 from 12,019 (+31%) at 91% occupancy, and management expects contributions from newly signed capacity to show up as it becomes operational.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is 91%, the Ahmedabad development-management project (about 8.6 lakh sq ft) is approved with about INR 100 crore of intended fit-out, furniture and deposit spend, and REIT talks on PropCo/OpCo assets are ongoing, though no transaction is announced.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: H1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 24.7% but Q2 grew 54.8% YoY, and no numeric revenue guidance was given, so an upgrade is conditional on new centres ramping.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Net debt more than doubled to INR 185 crore from INR 89 crore, cash conversion is an explicit H2 priority, and execution risk on 17 centres and about INR 100 crore of Ahmedabad spend is flagged.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: GCC services are being grown and SaaSJoy has not yet monetised external revenue (H1 FY27 revenue about INR 2.8 crore), so a commercial launch is hinted but not dated.

rows.label: Ahmedabad DM project revenue at scale
rows.why: The approved 8.6 lakh sq ft (about 8,500 seats) project is expected to generate about INR 120 crore of revenue at scale, though no date is given.

rows.label: Cash conversion improvement
rows.why: Net debt rose to INR 185 crore (gross debt INR 222 crore, cash INR 37 crore), and management named faster billing and collection as an H2 FY27 priority.

rows.label: REIT transaction on PropCo/OpCo assets
rows.why: Management is in talks with larger REIT players, but no transaction has been announced, so this is unconfirmed.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth, margins and 91% occupancy and emphasised execution on the 17-centre pipeline, but was cautious on balance-sheet items, lease liabilities and cash conversion; the call had no analyst Q&A, so analyst tone is not observable.

544515|2026-03.headline: Urban Company Q4 FY26 NTV rose 42% YoY to ₹1,148 crore, with Services ex-InstaHelp adjusted EBITDA margin at 3.3% and Q4 PAT of ₹98 crore hit by InstaHelp's ₹119 crore loss.
544515|2026-03.overview: Management reported its highest-ever quarterly NTV, with Q4 NTV up 42% YoY to ₹1,148 crore and FY26 NTV up 33% to ₹4,290 crore. Core Services ex-InstaHelp grew 26% YoY to ₹808 crore with adjusted EBITDA margin expanding to 3.3% of NTV from 1.6% a year earlier. International (UAE and Singapore) turned profitable for FY26 at ₹6 crore, and Native narrowed its loss to ₹31 crore. InstaHelp absorbed ₹119 crore of Q4 losses, which drove reported Q4 profit to ₹98 crore; management is investing heavily in InstaHelp and held its break-even and ₹1,000 crore EBITDA targets.

financial_highlights.value: ₹131 crore (4.1% of NTV) — 3.3% of NTV for Services adjusted EBITDA as per call
financial_highlights.change: Services margin 1.6% of NTV in Q4 FY25
Entirely attributable to InstaHelp's ₹119 crore loss; ex-InstaHelp adjusted profit ₹22 crore

segments.name: Core Services (ex-InstaHelp)
segments.commentary: Q4 NTV ₹808 crore, up 26% YoY; adjusted EBITDA ₹131 crore at 4.1% of NTV (3.3% of NTV in Services overall as stated). Management said the segment was loss-making as recently as FY24.

segments.name: International (UAE + Singapore)
segments.commentary: Q4 NTV ₹211 crore (+84% YoY) despite a March UAE headwind from the Middle East conflict; FY26 NTV ₹700 crore (+75%) with FY26 EBITDA turning positive at ₹6 crore.

segments.name: Native
segments.commentary: Q4 NTV ₹89 crore (+67% YoY); FY26 NTV ₹345 crore (+122%) with loss narrowing to ₹31 crore (-8.9% of NTV) from ₹39 crore (-25.1%) in FY25.

segments.name: InstaHelp
segments.commentary: Q4 loss of ₹119 crore covering acquisition, network subsidies and onboarding; 2.7 million orders and ₹40 crore NTV in Q4, with March alone crossing 1.1 million orders. Targets EBITDA break-even by Q3 FY28.

guidance_outlook: InstaHelp EBITDA break-even target retained at Q3 FY28.
Company-level EBITDA target of ₹1,000 crore by FY31 retained.
Management will not be giving quarterly call commentary on InstaHelp dynamics; detail is in the shareholder letter.
Management expects Services adjusted EBITDA as % of NTV to keep rising, aiming for 10% over a longer horizon; progress to be judged year-on-year rather than quarter-on-quarter.
No timeline given for Native break-even; management said it is fairly confident of the trajectory.
No incremental geography planned for the foreseeable future; focus remains India, UAE, Singapore and the KSA JV.
Native targets quadrupling net revenue with water purifiers and smart electronic door locks; no timeline given.
capex_capacity: Services now covers 60-plus cities across 47 cities' hundreds of micro-markets; densification is the priority over coverage expansion.
UC Instant (30 to 60 minute service) rolled out; management says it improves partner packing efficiency and utilisation rather than reducing it.
AI used to audit 100% of proof-of-work images; 55% of partner support queries handled by AI; about 90% of code shipped with GenAI assistance.
Saudi Arabia JV showing improving margins with visibility towards profitability.
InstaHelp expansion kept calibrated; management leaning towards densifying existing micro-markets.
demand_pricing: Services NTV growth accelerated: 19% in Q2 FY26, 21% in Q3, 26% in Q4 (ex-InstaHelp).
Management said the Middle East dip was visible month-on-month but YoY growth stayed healthy and the business is nearly back to recovery.
No material disruption from the state election-related workplace displacement; handled through pre-onboarding of professionals.
Competitive intensity in InstaHelp described as irrational at times but manageable; management said it will optimise for share rather than unit-economic elegance.
AOV sensitivity described as low in Core; management said AOV can move up or down and it will be managed through tactics and strategy.
Contribution per order declined in Q4 as InstaHelp marketing and subsidies rose; management said the decline was largely due to one cost metric (cost per order).

qa_highlights.question: What is driving Services ex-InstaHelp growth to 25% in top 10 cities, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to densification flywheel effects: higher utilisation, lower travel and faster fulfilment via UC Instant, improving retention. Growth accelerated from 19% to 26% over three quarters; management wants to see more quarters before calling it a structural trend.

qa_highlights.question: Will AOV pressure and elevated competitive intensity hurt steady-state economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated its break-even and ₹1,000 crore EBITDA guardrails but declined to give a steady-state unit-economics range, citing the need to flex tactics on AOV and competition.

qa_highlights.question: What timeline and drivers exist for Native break-even?
qa_highlights.answer: Native's loss narrowed to -8.9% of NTV from -14.7% earlier; management is fairly confident of break-even but gave no timeline, and said it would happen despite new product launches.

qa_highlights.question: What is the new product pipeline for Native to meet its quadrupling target?
qa_highlights.answer: Current launches are water purifiers and smart electronic door locks; no timeline set, and revenue to come from installed-base growth and retention.

qa_highlights.question: Is the InstaHelp versus core structure a concern given competitor fundraising and is there a diversification plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it sees a winner-take-most dynamic in trust-based services, is targeting leadership in InstaHelp, and is not worried about competitor funding; InstaHelp average rating 4.7 and retention claimed as industry-leading.

qa_highlights.question: Are there plans to expand into new geographies or adjacencies?
qa_highlights.answer: No new geography planned in the foreseeable future; no experimentation in adjacencies. Focus is entirely on densifying core micro-markets.

qa_highlights.question: What was the contribution-per-order decline and cause in InstaHelp Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said marketing elevated to acquire users and build the brand, including Cricket World Cup spend; all metrics improved except contribution per order, which declined largely due to one cost line.

risks_watch: InstaHelp losses (₹119 crore in Q4) and break-even target of Q3 FY28; reported profit depends on InstaHelp spend.
Competitive intensity in InstaHelp and rising AOV pressure; management declined to quantify steady-state unit economics.
Middle East conflict effects on UAE business in March and the pace of recovery.
Native break-even has no timeline; new products (water purifiers, smart locks) not yet material.
Seasonal cost spikes in Q1/Q3 marketing ahead of peak quarters, which complicates quarter-on-quarter comparisons.
Whether Services adjusted EBITDA margin can rise from 3.3% toward 10% of NTV over a multi-year horizon.
544515|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on Core and International execution, and defensive on InstaHelp unit economics, where management refused to give steady-state or quarterly guidance. Management repeatedly described competitive irrationality as manageable and said it is prioritising market share over short-term margins.
key_quotes: We are investing to win, and we intend to stay in it.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Services ex-InstaHelp adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 3.3% of NTV from 1.6% a year earlier, and management expects it to keep rising toward 10% over a longer horizon, though quarterly comparisons will be noisy from Q1/Q3 marketing spikes and InstaHelp subsidies.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Management is densifying existing micro-markets across 60-plus cities rather than adding coverage, and InstaHelp expansion is kept calibrated, so new capacity is hinted at only through densification, with no new plant, line or store date given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q4 NTV up 42% YoY to ₹1,148 crore, transacting users up 24% to 8.4 million, InstaHelp crossed 1.1 million orders in March, and Core ex-InstaHelp grew 26%, with management guiding to continued densification-led growth.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No capex plan or utilisation level (utilisation_read gives direction only, no % level) was disclosed; the asset-light model and densification-first stance point away from a discrete capex announcement.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Services ex-InstaHelp NTV growth accelerated from 19% in Q2 FY26 to 21% in Q3 and 26% in Q4, but management wants more quarters before calling it structural and has held rather than raised guidance.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: InstaHelp absorbed ₹119 crore of Q4 losses, competitive intensity is described as irrational at times, and contribution per order declined in Q4, so the InstaHelp break-even by Q3 FY28 could slip if unit economics do not improve.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Native is targeting quadrupling net revenue with water purifiers and smart electronic door locks, but no timeline was given and these products are not yet material (Native FY26 NTV ₹345 crore).

rows.label: Native loss narrowing toward break-even
rows.why: Native loss fell to -8.9% of NTV in FY26 from -25.1% in FY25 (₹31 crore vs ₹39 crore), and management is fairly confident of break-even, but gave no timeline.

rows.label: International (UAE + Singapore) and KSA JV profitability
rows.why: International FY26 NTV grew 75% to ₹700 crore with EBITDA turning positive at ₹6 crore, Q4 NTV rose 84% to ₹211 crore despite the March UAE disruption, and the KSA JV shows improving margins with visibility toward profitability.

rows.label: InstaHelp order scale-up
rows.why: InstaHelp did 2.7 million orders and ₹40 crore NTV in Q4, with March alone above 1.1 million orders, though management is not giving quarterly InstaHelp commentary.

tone.note: Management was confident on Core densification, International profitability and the 26% Services ex-InstaHelp growth, but defensive on InstaHelp unit economics, declining to give steady-state or quarterly guidance; analysts pressed on AOV pressure, competitive intensity and the Native break-even tim

544515|2026-06.headline: Urban Company Q1 FY27 consolidated NTV rose 42% YoY to ₹1,465 crore; Services NTV grew 29% and InstaHelp loss narrowed to ₹(132) crore.
544515|2026-06.overview: Consolidated NTV grew 42% YoY to ₹1,465 crore and revenue rose 44% to ₹528 crore, with orders up 79% YoY to 13.2 million. Core Services NTV accelerated for a fourth straight quarter to 29% growth (₹1,056 crore), and Services adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 6.9% of NTV. Consolidated loss was ₹(65) crore, almost entirely from InstaHelp, while the rest of the business delivered an adjusted EBITDA of ₹67 crore. Management retained its guidance of consolidated adjusted EBITDA breakeven by Q3 FY28 and ₹1,000 crore adjusted EBITDA by FY31, and framed InstaHelp as the main investment area.

financial_highlights.change: +5.2 pp YoY (stated as 170 bps improvement in the margin line in the Q&A)
improved from (11.4)% a year ago (410 bps)
Loss per order ₹(346) vs ₹(447) in Q4
1.2 million new customers added in the quarter

segments.name: Core Services
segments.commentary: NTV ₹1,056 crore, growing 29% YoY, the fourth consecutive quarter of acceleration (10%→19%→21%→26%→29%). Adjusted EBITDA margin 6.9% of NTV, up 5.2 pp YoY per the call; management says the 29% base was muted by unseasonal rains and monsoon in the prior year.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: NTV ₹237 crore, up 76% YoY (58% ex-currency). UAE and Singapore both grew strongly; the Saudi Arabia JV is approaching profitability. UAE and Saudi JV are described as nearing or at profitability, and the company is not planning new international markets.

segments.name: InstaHelp
segments.commentary: NTV ₹119 crore (+51% YoY), net revenue ₹95 crore (+60% YoY); adjusted EBITDA loss ₹(132) crore, or (7.3)% of NTV versus (11.4)% a year ago. Largest investment; management expects it to need 2 or more years of investment and aims for adjusted breakeven within about 18 months.

guidance_outlook: Retains guidance of consolidated adjusted EBITDA breakeven by Q3 FY28.
Retains guidance of ₹1,000 crore adjusted EBITDA by FY31.
Long-term Services adjusted EBITDA margin guidance of 9-10% of NTV; currently at 6.9%. Management said it is not in a rush and sees the target as achievable without trading off growth.
Management said Services will be a cash-generating business going forward and that it intends to keep it profitable; InstaHelp is expected to need 2 years or more of investment.
Management explicitly declined to give growth guidance beyond the 29% trend, saying the company does not want to set the wrong expectations.
Top-15-city TAM for InstaHelp is ₹7,000-12,000 crore NTV annually; management's base case is ₹7,000-8,000 crore and the bull case is ₹10,000-12,000 crore.
capex_capacity: InstaHelp: management said the company is investing aggressively in micro-market density, with the investment level still under evaluation.
Core Services trainer and infrastructure capacity is being scaled up with AI support; management says the company is 'all hands on deck' as supply grows.
Beauty segment: partners are being retrained and retooled, and the company moved to a majority of professionals having access to two-wheelers, with the target of approaching 100%.

Services is expected to consume less capital as InstaHelp is scaled; management said capital allocation will be reviewed once InstaHelp approaches adjusted breakeven (hopefully within about 18 months).
demand_pricing: Management said Q1 was among the best quarters in the company's history, with growth broad-based.

InstaHelp pricing: sustainable professional payout is about ₹130-160 per hour, with ₹150 as the rule of thumb. Management said an AOV of about ₹300 is needed for InstaHelp to break even, with ₹200 per hour required to clear gross breakeven.

Management said competitors in the InstaHelp category have pricing of ₹80-120 per hour for full-month subscriptions and that competitive intensity is high; it said the company has no reason to comment on rival strategies.
Management said the 3 major players have limited their household coverage to about 3.5-4 million households; the company believes most spending goes to subsidised repeat orders.
Management said the company has 'underestimated' the Tier 2 opportunity, with Tier 2 cities performing as well as Tier 1.

Management said it is seeing acceleration in MAUs, DAUs and MTUs, with conversion rates improving; the marketing spend in Services was about ₹25 crore in the quarter versus ₹24 crore a year ago (flat).

qa_highlights.question: Morgan Stanley: is the Cheaper, Faster, Better flywheel now visible enough to call a bold trajectory shift in Services NTV growth, and can growth be guided higher?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the flywheel comes from densifying many micro-markets, which improves partner utilisation, lowers churn and supports trust. It cited UC Instant (30-60 minute service) as a new driver. It declined to give growth guidance, said the 29% was helped by a muted prior-year base from unseasonal rains and monsoon, and said the margin of 6.9% is in line with the 9-10% long-term target, which is not a trade-off against growth.

qa_highlights.question: Morgan Stanley: why should InstaHelp get capital and attention, and how will capital be allocated over two years between Services, new segments and international?
qa_highlights.answer: InstaHelp is strategically relevant because its high frequency keeps users on the app weekly. Services is to be profitable and cash generating; UAE and Singapore are profitable wholly owned subsidiaries; the Saudi JV is nearing profitability. InstaHelp needs two years or more of investment, with capital allocation revisited at adjusted breakeven, hopefully within about 18 months.

qa_highlights.question: Goldman Sachs: why not export the UAE and Saudi model to new international markets, given Core Services is generating cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited bandwidth as the main constraint. It said playbooks need local customisation plus some luck, and that earlier Australia and US launches did not succeed. It will stay focused on UAE, Saudi Arabia and India, with no plans for new international markets for now.

qa_highlights.question: Goldman Sachs: where does Services margin go from 6.9% of NTV versus the 9-10% target, and would the company cap margin around 10% or reinvest?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the goal is to reach the 9-10% range without rushing and without trading growth for margin. Priority one is growing fast, priority two is margin expansion. Once it reaches about 10%, it will decide whether to lift margins further or reinvest for faster growth.

qa_highlights.question: Goldman Sachs: is the InstaHelp TAM structurally lower, and would the company operate at a narrow loss if competition leaves room for only two players?
qa_highlights.answer: The base case is INR 7,000-8,000 crore NTV and the bull case is INR 10,000-12,000 crore, with 3 orders per user per month. Management said the 3 major players have limited coverage to about 3.5-4 million households and that subsidised repeat orders dominate spend. It expects a low single-digit market share outcome and says it will not spend heavily on the category to drive share, while being opinionated about winning micro-markets.

qa_highlights.question: Bank of America: what AOV is needed for InstaHelp to break even, and is there scope for growth above 29%?
qa_highlights.answer: Sustainable professional payout is INR 130-160 per hour, with INR 150 as the rule of thumb. Gross breakeven needs about INR 200 per hour, and an AOV of about INR 300 is needed for InstaHelp to break even. Management said breakeven could take a couple of years or up to 5 years, and it declined to give growth guidance beyond the 29%.

qa_highlights.question: Bank of America: how is AI being used and how much margin benefit is there?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 90-95% of the code is now written by AI, and that support, supply-side onboarding, quality audits and fraud detection are increasingly AI-led. Marketing and Finance/HR run AI end-to-end. It said the margin benefit has started to show but there is a long way to go.

qa_highlights.question: Kotak: is Beauty acceleration sustainable, and are the 30-40 annual transactions per user assumption and consolidation prospects realistic?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Beauty has seen a resurgence after retraining and retooling partners, and that the company had underinvested there a couple of years back. Two-wheeler access for Beauty professionals is now a majority. It expects 3 transactions per month, not 30-40, for the 10-12 lakh household case. It expects private players to keep burning cash and believes it will be the eventual winner in the category.

qa_highlights.question: Bellwether: what is driving the 5 lakh quarter-on-quarter user addition, what marketing spend is involved, and what training and capacity constraints exist in InstaHelp and Core Services?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the user growth is largely from MAU, DAU and MTU growth and better conversion, and that marketing spend in Services was about INR 25 crore versus INR 24 crore a year ago. For Core, it said capacity is comfortable but is being scaled up, with all hands on deck, to match trainer and infrastructure growth. It said InstaHelp supply is also being expanded.

qa_highlights.question: Emkay: is the shift to premium products a sign of a premium customer base, and will the company expand beyond water purifiers and smart locks?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said its products, such as the M3 water purifier with a 3-year no-service, no-filter-change design, are aimed at lowering lifecycle cost. It said it is not building a durables company and will keep its focus on a small number of categories, mainly water purifiers and smart locks, with the aim of serving the top households in India.

risks_watch: InstaHelp losses: the loss was INR (132) crore; management expects 2+ years of investment and an adjusted breakeven target within about 18 months. Track loss per order, which improved from INR (447) in Q4 to INR (346) in Q1.
AOV and payout economics: InstaHelp needs about INR 300 AOV to break even, with pay of INR 130-160 per hour; competitor pricing of INR 80-120 per hour is a pressure point.
Competition and TAM: management said 3 major players have limited coverage to 3.5-4 million households; the TAM base case is INR 7,000-8,000 crore against a bull case of INR 10,000-12,000 crore.
Growth sustainability: Services NTV growth of 29% was helped by a muted prior-year base, and management declined to give forward growth guidance.
Services margin: current 6.9% of NTV against a 9-10% long-term target; the timing of expansion remains unspecified.
Capacity and trainer scaling for Core Services as user additions accelerate.
544515|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the Services growth trend and the balance sheet, but cautious and deliberately non-committal on forward growth, TAM and the timing of InstaHelp breakeven. Management repeatedly declined to set expectations beyond the 29% trend.

rows.why: Total orders rose 79% YoY to 13.2 million, 1.2 million new customers were added, InstaHelp orders grew 43% QoQ to 3.82 million, and Services NTV growth accelerated for a fourth straight quarter to 29%, though management gave no forward growth number.

544515|2026-09.headline: Urban Company's consolidated NTV rose 39.1% to ₹1,432.3 crore in Q2 FY27, with adjusted EBITDA (ex-Native/International investment) at ₹30 crore, up 213% YoY.
544515|2026-09.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 consolidated NTV up 39.1% YoY to ₹1,432.3 crore and revenue from operations up 41.4% to ₹537.3 crore, with adjusted loss of ₹144 crore after a ₹174 crore investment in Native. Core Services adjusted EBITDA was ₹30 crore ex-investments, and management reiterated breakeven for the consolidated business by Q3 FY28 and a ₹1,000 crore EBITDA-type goal for FY31. Management announced a fundraise of up to ₹2,500 crore, framed as flexibility rather than a need to fund losses. Q&A focused on the rationale for the raise, Native's AC launch, professional supply, and pricing/contribution economics.

financial_highlights.change: +213% YoY; ₹119 crore for trailing four quarters, +175%
vs NTV growth of 26%, per management
up 110 bps (from prior level per call)

segments.name: Core Services (India)
segments.commentary: Management said Core Services adjusted EBITDA was ₹30 crore ex-investments and contribution margin rose to 3.5%; NTV growth was attributed to new-customer acquisition, repeat cohorts and densification, with instant service now used in top 7–8 cities.

segments.name: International (UAE, Saudi, Singapore)
segments.commentary: International NTV grew 66.2% YoY per management, with UAE described as a key market; adjusted EBITDA margin was 2% of NTV, improved by 190 bps. Management said war-related concerns are behind it and Q2+Q3 combined growth is expected at 50–55%.

segments.name: Native (water purifiers / AC services)
segments.commentary: Native's loss narrowed by ₹220 crore (per call) with loss per order down 19% QoQ to ₹279; management says Native is being built deliberately with a ₹174 crore investment in Q2 and is in a learning phase for its first AC device.

segments.name: Insta Help (professional/household help)
segments.commentary: Management said Insta Help is in a tougher base with Q2 revenue growth at 26.3% and the festive season falling in Q3; penetration in top 8 cities for largest categories is below 10%.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated breakeven target reiterated for Q3 FY28; management said it is confident, more than ever, of the ₹1,000 crore FY31 goal.
Management expects Q2 plus Q3 combined international growth in the range of 50% to 55%.
Fundraise of up to ₹2,500 crore is for flexibility, mainly for organic build-out of existing businesses and selective M&A; management said nothing imminent.
Native AC device launch: management expects one to two quarters of learning, limited largely to the app, and no material change to Native's trajectory.
Contribution margin target of 9–10% noted as the key lever; management said it is working towards it.
capex_capacity: Orders rose 63% QoQ to 6.23 million; 45% of new orders are reportedly from the Core Services' top categories, per management.
Management is onboarding professionals aggressively in the 3–4 months before the festive season to improve the liquidity coefficient.
Native's offline distribution is in a learning phase; M3 water purifier and Lock Ultra launched in modern retail with pull from offline ecosystem.
Gold premium service rollout: management said results are promising and it intends to scale it out across categories.
demand_pricing: Core Services average spend growth slowed to around 3% (vs historical 6–7%); management attributed this to mix change and season timing, and pass-through of densification benefits in pockets.
Instant service delivered in 30–60 minutes is offered in UAE and Singapore; management said no premium is currently charged.
Professional (partner) supply grew 16% YoY versus NTV growth of 26%; management declined to give forward partner-growth projections.
Hourly pricing roughly ₹200 and net order value roughly ₹300 for an average order of 1.5 hours; partner payout of ₹150 per utilised hour.
Management described the household-help TAM as range-bound with no single winner, and the AC TAM as roughly 10x water purifier TAM.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving Core Services' accelerating new-user acquisition and is it sustainable, with average spend growth slowing to 3%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a stronger product with instant service in top 7–8 cities, AI-led training/QC improving word of mouth, densification, faster growth in Tier-2 markets and higher marketing. Average spend slowed due to mix, seasonality and some densification benefit passed to consumers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the use of proceeds from the ₹2,500 crore fundraise and the M&A framework?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly for flexibility and organic build-out; M&A would be for consolidating existing categories or entering new categories, not new countries, with buy-vs-build tilting to buy if accretive. Nothing imminent.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise capital now given cash on balance sheet?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the raise is for flexibility, to be aggressive, pursue acquisitions and absorb downside in a high-competition scenario; not primarily to fund losses. Targets remain unchanged, and they would have changed short/medium-term targets if funding were insufficient.

qa_highlights.question: Does the Native AC launch and its allocation impact profitability timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Native is on track for profitability, AC will be a disciplined build-up with R&D the bulk of losses, and any new category would take one to two quarters of learning before scale.

qa_highlights.question: Is professional supply or retention a rate limiter, and what is steady-state unit economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the challenge is retaining high-quality professionals, not sourcing. Experts care about net take-home pay; the company frames pricing and payouts as competitive. Steady-state unit economics remain under evaluation with a cited framework of payout ₹150 per hour, with ₹50 covering costs at best utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the acceleration in professional-services growth and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said professional growth of 16% is a leading indicator; drivers are utilisation, targeting, and onboarding. Management declined to give specific projections.

qa_highlights.question: Will Native offline distribution expand pan-India in modern retail?
qa_highlights.answer: Offline share is small and in a learning phase; modern retail response is good; management will expand calibrated and slowly.

risks_watch: Competitive intensity in Core Services and International; management says losses are a deliberate choice.
Average spend growth slowing to 3% versus historical 6–7%.
Professional partner retention and churn as supply expands.
Native profitability and AC device adoption, with a one-to-two-quarter learning phase before scale.
Use and deployment of the ₹2,500 crore fundraise and any M&A execution.

544516|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 66% to Rs.319.6 Crores with PAT margin of 12.2%; FY27 guidance is Rs.500 Crores revenue at 12-13% PAT margin.
544516|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue reached Rs.319.6 Crores (up 66% YoY), with H2 contributing Rs.229.1 Crores (up 114% YoY), and EBITDA of Rs.64.2 Crores at a 20.1% margin (EBITDA margin down from about 25% per analyst question). PAT was Rs.39.1 Crores (up 52%) at a 12.2% margin. Management said the Rs.1,000 Crores revenue milestone timeline may extend modestly because it declined to pursue low-margin re-tenders amid aluminium and stainless steel inflation. Management guided FY27 revenue of about Rs.500 Crores at 12-13% PAT margin, backed by an unexecuted order book of about Rs.469-487 Crores (figure varied in the call) and a Rs.1,200 Crores bid pipeline.

financial_highlights.change: +66% YoY vs Rs.192.4 Crores in FY25
+114% YoY vs Rs.107.3 Crores in H2 FY25
receivable days down 24 days; inventory days down 48 days

financial_highlights.metric: Net debt to equity at 31 Mar 2026

segments.name: Railways
segments.commentary: Largest growth driver; management says about 70% of the pipeline is railway, roughly Rs.900 Crores of the Rs.1,200 Crores bid pipeline, covering Atmanirbhar Bharat, Spark and Kavach coaches, Vande Bharat sleeper and Amrit Bharat turnkey contracts. Refurbishment is cited as a separate opportunity of about Rs.26,000 Crores sanctioned, with hoped-for orders of at least Rs.100 Crores this year.

segments.name: Metro
segments.commentary: About Rs.70 Crores of metro orders held, with another Rs.120 Crores expected within the Rs.1,200 Crores pipeline; Kolkata Metro turnkey contracts are named as a focus.

segments.name: Defence and aerospace
segments.commentary: Rs.29 Crores of current order book to execute this year, plus Rs.60-70 Crores expected from HAL tenders (mainly simulators, not AMCA airframe production). Proposed JV with Big Bang Boom Solutions to be incorporated before 15 June 2026; Airfloa committed about Rs.25 Crores, focused on autonomous drones and electronic warfare.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of approximately Rs.500 Crores with PAT margin of 12-13%; management said PAT would not fall below 12%.
Rs.1,000 Crores revenue milestone timeline may extend modestly; management also said it could be reached in FY28 or earlier if conditions allow.
Management said about 70-75% of the Rs.500 Crores FY27 target is covered by the existing order book, and 30-40% of the Rs.1,200 Crores pipeline is expected to execute in FY27.
R&D spend to rise to about 8-9% of sales this year from about 4% earlier; management later said R&D spend would be capitalised on the balance sheet.
Capex of Rs.30-40 Crores planned for FY27-28, including about Rs.30-35 Crores for a 14-acre facility with 50,000 to 1 lakh sq ft of initial shed space, expanding to 3-4 lakh sq ft.
Debt funding of about Rs.120 Crores at 8.25% from two banks: Rs.60 Crores sanctioned, the other Rs.60 Crores expected by end June 2026. No equity raise planned this year.
capex_capacity: Current capacity utilisation is about 90% of existing facility; two-shift operations in use since around December 2025.
New 14-acre facility planned: initial 50,000 to 1 lakh sq ft, later extending to 3-4 lakh sq ft; land already acquired and term loan discussions with bankers under way.

Machinery purchases, mostly from China, delayed because Chinese OEMs require an end-user certificate from the Government of India; management expected clarity in June 2026 and may switch to different machinery for lightweight rail interiors.
Plans to consolidate seven units into about two, reducing rent of roughly Rs.20-25 lakh per month.
Channel partner model in place to execute zonal railway contracts without building facilities in each region.
demand_pricing: Unexecuted order book about Rs.469-487 Crores (figure cited differently in different answers): Rs.415-420 Crores government and Rs.50-55 Crores non-government.
Bid pipeline about Rs.1,200 Crores with historical bid-win ratio of about 20-25%.

Raw material inflation: aluminium up more than 80% and stainless steel up 60-65% YoY; price variation clauses cover only about 50-60% of the increase, and accessories (30-35% of assembly cost) are not covered.
Competitors named: Kineco, Hindustan Fiberglass Works, DTL Ancillaries, Vibgyor, Universal Engineers; seating competitors Tata (with Fainsa), a Korean firm and firms from Mumbai and Bengaluru.

qa_highlights.question: How will working capital be funded and when will operating cash flow turn positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about Rs.100-110 Crores of receivables collected by June end; receivable and working capital cycles targeted at 60-70 days from 90-95 days within 3-4 months. Debt of Rs.120 Crores is being raised.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Rs.500 Crores FY27 target is covered by orders?
qa_highlights.answer: About 70-75% is covered by the existing order book, and 30-40% of the Rs.1,200 Crores pipeline is expected to execute in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Margin pressure and its causes in H2 FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Aluminium and stainless steel inflation hit margins. Management said price variation covers only about 50-60% of losses, and it used advances, LCs and BGs to block vendor prices, limiting losses to 20-25% of the uncovered amount.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of added debt interest and R&D on the 12-13% PAT target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PAT would stay at or above 12%, citing higher-margin bids and that R&D spend would be deployed only when expected returns are met.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY28 revenue reach Rs.1,000 Crores and PAT Rs.150 Crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Rs.1,000 Crores could be reached even this year if all goes well and that FY28 could exceed Rs.1,000 Crores, without firm numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Does the Rs.500 Crores target hold given 90% utilisation and machinery delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said machinery delays would not affect FY27 turnover; two-shift operation and channel partners could add Rs.400-450 Crores from the Rs.320 Crores base.

risks_watch: Working capital: trade receivables of Rs.214 Crores at year-end; collection of about 70% expected by June, and cash conversion still negative.
Debt servicing: about Rs.120 Crores new debt at 8.25% adds interest cost of roughly Rs.10 Crores per year, per the analyst's calculation.
Raw material and commodity inflation, with price variation clauses covering only part of the increase.

544527|2026-06.headline: Atlanta Electricals Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 48% YoY to INR466.33 crore; record order inflow of INR972.42 crore lifted order book to INR3,116.63 crore.
544527|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 48% YoY to INR466.33 crore, driven mainly by volume from newly commissioned plants, with management saying pricing and product mix were broadly unchanged. Gross margin rose 130 bps to 27.3% and EBITDA margin expanded to 16.5% from 15.5% a year ago, though both moderated from Q4 FY26 seasonally. Order inflow was a record INR972.42 crore, taking the unexecuted order book to about INR3,117 crore, of which about INR2,400 crore is expected to execute in FY27. Management reiterated a 40% revenue CAGR target and a 17-18% margin range, while 400 kV and 765 kV product timelines were pushed out and largely remain conditional.

segments.name: Product mix by voltage class
segments.commentary: 220 kV class was 56% of Q1 revenue, 66 kV class 25%, and 132 kV class about 5.5%. Power transformers were about 79% of revenue, with auto, inverter duty and other products making up the balance.

segments.name: End market
segments.commentary: Transmission and distribution contributed about 66% of revenue and renewable energy about 19%, with thermal power and other industrial making up the rest.

segments.name: Order book by voltage
segments.commentary: 220 kV and above transformers are over 55% of the order book; 400 kV transformers and reactors account for nearly INR275 crore. Management said the entire record Q1 inflow is 220 kV and below.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of 40% YoY growth, applied to FY26 revenue of INR1,851 crore (per CFO); management also cited a 40% CAGR for three years.
EBITDA margin expected around 17-18% for the year, with raw material inflation expected to persist but margins sustainable at the Q1 level.
About INR2,400 crore of the ~INR3,100 crore unexecuted order book is due for execution in FY27.
Inverter duty transformer facility (~5,000 MVA) targeted for commissioning by end-December 2026.
Export target of about 15% of revenue within three years; no export revenue in Q1 FY27 and first export execution expected in FY28.
Management expects meaningful revenue from 400 kV transformers from FY28, with 765 kV tech tie-up targeted by end-Q2 FY27 and first 765 kV product by Q4 FY27.
capex_capacity: Installed manufacturing capacity of 63,060 MVA; Q1 sales-based utilisation of 4,381 MVA, of which Vadod produced 1,520 MVA and Ankhi (Jambusar) 320 MVA.
Inverter duty transformer facility adds ~5,000 MVA; construction on track for commissioning by end-December 2026.
Vadod Unit 4 received Power Grid approval for 400 kV class manufacturing; first 400 kV unit under engineering completion, with short-circuit test planned around quarter-end (Q1 FY27 end or early Q2).
Tank and radiator backward-integration facility adjacent to Vadod: INR15-20 crore spent so far against about INR180 crore planned; tanks and radiators are 4-5% of transformer cost.
765 kV plan: first product to be made at Ankhi once technical tie-up closes; Power Grid revalidation needed in new name. Short-circuit test requirement for 765 kV not yet finalised.
demand_pricing: Record order inflow of INR972.42 crore in Q1 FY27; order book INR3,116.63 crore as of 30 June 2026.
Key orders: INR291.68 crore from RVPNL (160 MVA, 50 MVA, 31.5 MVA power transformers) and INR285.15 crore from PSTCL (23 units of 160 MVA 220/66 kV transformers).
Pricing passed through via price variation clauses in purchase orders; per-MVA realisation described as unchanged across kV classes, with raw material inflation passed on.
Management saw no pricing or bidding-intensity impact from Chinese manufacturers being allowed into PSU tenders; none had participated yet.
No data-centre orders in current order book. Management expects order booking to peak in Q2 and mid-Q3 FY27.
Management said CRGO steel prices and supply are not under pressure in the short term; DGTR anti-dumping verdict expected by end-March 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Will the new 400 kV capacity pressure incremental margins or order inflow?
qa_highlights.answer: Niral Patel said Q1 was the highest order inflow in at least 2-2.5 years, with no visible pricing correction in the market.

qa_highlights.question: Are inventory builds speculative ahead of raw material volatility?
qa_highlights.answer: Anand Sharma said procurement is strictly job-to-job with no speculation on commodity prices; inventory build is for the next quarter's executions.

qa_highlights.question: What are the 765 kV tech tie-up terms?
qa_highlights.answer: Niral Patel said the deal combines a one-time fee of USD3-5 million and royalty of 2-4% for at least three to four years, on 765 kV products only; the partner is not named.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins be sustained at 17-18%?
qa_highlights.answer: Mehul Mehta said FY25 and FY26 margins ended at 15.56% and 18.52%, and that 17-18% is the expected range, with raw material price increases continuing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin differential for 400 kV and 765 kV?
qa_highlights.answer: Anand Sharma said these products should earn better margins than 220 kV or 132 kV, but the exact differential will only be known after first prototypes and commercial production.

qa_highlights.question: How much FY27 revenue is implied?
qa_highlights.answer: Mehul Mehta said a 40% YoY increase on FY26 revenue of INR1,851 crore is the guidance.

risks_watch: Execution timing on 400 kV: short-circuit test for the first 400 kV unit slipped from June-July to around quarter-end; balance order quantity depends on passing it.
765 kV entry depends on closing the technical tie-up (targeted Q2 FY27), government approvals on the partner side, Power Grid revalidation and an unresolved short-circuit test requirement.

Capacity additions by peers (including mention of CG Power and Transformer Rectifiers, about 60,000 MVA in the next 3-4 months per an analyst) could pressure pricing; management expects margin protection through 400/765 kV and exports.
Raw material cost pressure from geopolitics and CRGO steel anti-dumping investigation; Q1 gross margin fell QoQ.
Working capital: inventory days at 105 and inventory build in Q1; monitor cash conversion cycle (~83 days).
Export revenue is zero so far; the 15% export target is three years out.
544527|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on demand and order inflow, with a strong emphasis on structural growth. Noticeably cautious and evasive on specifics: declined to name the technical partner, to quantify 400/765 kV margins, or to comment on competitors and large pending orders.
key_quotes: We have had a record order inflow and order book during quarter one of ‘27.

We believe it is not a cyclical upturn but a multi-year investment cycle supported by expansion in transmission network, renewable energy integration, battery energy storage systems and industrial electrification, railway electrification and rapid growth of data centers.
We are in the business of manufacturing transformers and not speculating on the raw material price.
So we expect the margin somewhere around 17 to 18% as we always convey to our investors.

rows.why: Revenue guided +40% YoY on FY26 base of INR1,851 cr (~INR2,590 cr for FY27) with INR2,400 cr of the INR3,117 cr order book due for execution in FY27; Q1 revenue was INR466 cr, so H2-weighted execution is required to hit it.

rows.why: Utilisation is low at ~7% of installed 63,060 MVA (4,381 MVA sales-based), so capacity-driven capex is not required; however, tank/radiator backward integration is only INR15-20 cr of ~INR180 cr spent, and 765 kV/400 kV tie-ups could bring further capex announcements.

rows.why: Management reiterated (not raised) 40% growth and 17-18% margin; 400 kV short-circuit test slipped to around quarter-end and 765 kV entry is conditional, so no clear upside signal.

rows.why: Q1 revenue of INR466 cr is only ~18% of the INR2,590 cr FY27 implied target, 400 kV short-circuit test slipped from June-July to quarter-end, and 400/765 kV timelines were pushed out with 765 kV largely conditional.

rows.when: Q4 FY27 (first 765 kV product), FY28 for meaningful 400 kV r

rows.label: Export revenue ramp (~15% of revenue target in 3 years)
rows.why: Zero export revenue in Q1 FY27 against a ~15% of revenue target within three years; first export execution expected in FY28.

rows.label: Order booking peak in Q2 and mid-Q3 FY27
rows.why: Record Q1 order inflow of INR972 cr (highest in 2-2.5 years) and management expects booking to peak in Q2 and mid-Q3, though no data-centre orders are yet in the book.

rows.why: Inventory days at 105 and cash conversion cycle ~83 days; inventory build is for next quarter's executions, so working capital could absorb cash if execution slips.

tone.note: Management was confident on record order inflow (INR972 cr), structural growth and 17-18% margin range, but cautious and evasive on 765 kV partner identity, 400/765 kV margin differential and competitor capacity; analysts pushed on peer capacity additions (~60,000 MVA) and margin sustainability.

544527|2026-09.headline: Atlanta Electricals Q2 FY27 revenue rose 23.1% YoY to INR390.1 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 15.3% on firm-price contracts and ~INR180 crore of deferred deliveries.
544527|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations grew 23.1% YoY to INR390.1 crore, while gross margin fell to 26.6% from 30.9% and EBITDA margin to 15.3% from 17.3%. Management attributed the squeeze to elevated transformer oil, copper and steel prices on firm-price orders (about 15% of quarterly revenue) and Gujarat monsoon disruptions that delayed customer acceptance of finished transformers worth about INR180 crore. PAT rose 28% YoY to INR32.1 crore, helped by lower finance costs. Order book reached INR3,197 crore, up 54.5% YoY, but Q2 order inflow was only about INR421 crore as management chose to limit 220 kV and below bookings.

financial_highlights.change: +6.1% YoY vs INR97.8 crore; gross margin 26.6% vs 30.9%
+28% YoY vs INR25.1 crore; margin up from 7.9%

financial_highlights.metric: Basic and diluted EPS Q2 FY27

financial_highlights.change: +32% YoY; margin vs 16.4% in H1 FY26
vs INR7.9 crore in H1 FY26

segments.name: Transformers - 220 kV and below (current book)
segments.commentary: About 47% of the order book is 220 kV class per management. Management said it deliberately limited new 220 kV and below bookings in Q2 given a large Q1 booking base.

segments.name: Transformers - 400 kV class
segments.commentary: About 8.6% of the order book is 400 kV class (INR184 crore per management). First 315 MVA, 400 kV unit commenced manufacturing on 26 Oct 2026; commercial contribution targeted in Q4 FY27 after testing.

segments.name: Export / US
segments.commentary: First US order for a special duty transformer, for a new US transformer plant. US inquiries of about 120 transformers (9,300 MVA). Medium-term aspiration of exports at about 15% of revenue within 2 years.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin for FY27 and FY28 expected in the 16% to 18% range; management said it remains firm on achieving this in both years.
3-year revenue growth aspiration of approximately 40% CAGR reiterated; CEO-level comment that 40% is a minimum, and management said FY28 is covered but would not give FY29 guidance.
About 70% of the INR180 crore deferred orders already dispatched in October; remainder expected in Q3 FY27, subject to customer site readiness.
Remaining firm-price orders (about 10-12% of order book per CFO, 3-4% per COO) expected to be substantially executed in Q3 FY27, with price revisions reportedly obtained from customers.
Management expects H2 to be stronger than H1 seasonally and expects margin correction in Q3 and Q4; target utilisation of 80%.
capex_capacity: Dedicated inverter duty transformer (IDT) plant: about 5,000 MVA capacity, capex INR65 crore, civil work complete, commissioning expected before end-Q3 FY27; 33 kV IDT production moves from Unit 2 to free Unit 2 for 66 and 132 kV classes.

Tank and radiator backward integration via AE Components: capex about INR193 crore (INR196 crore cited later in Q&A, likely the same project), groundbreaking done, commissioning targeted October 2027. Funded mainly through internal accruals, with term loans tied up but undrawn as a backup.
Utilisation as stated in Q&A: Unit 1 at 60%, Unit 2 at 40%, Bangalore at about 90%, Vadod at about 30%, Jambusar (765 kV plant) at about 7-8%.

765 kV: in-house design of first 765 kV reactor started; production targeted in Q4 FY27 with completion and testing between Q4 FY27 and Q1 FY28. International technology partnership not progressed due to sanctions constraints; management says partnership remains open.
Vadod facility has approvals from NTPC Solar, NTPC Renewables, Tata Power, KPTCL and Punjab Transmission Company.
demand_pricing: Order book INR3,196.97 crore at 30 Sep 2026, vs INR3,116.63 crore at end-June and about INR2,069 crore a year ago (+54.5% YoY).
Q2 order inflow about INR421 crore; management called the slowdown a deliberate decision to limit 220 kV and below orders, and cited commodity volatility delaying some L1 tenders.
Inquiry pipeline about INR19,464 crore. Battery energy storage pipeline of about 3,400 MVA worth INR184 crore.

Pricing: majority of orders carry price variation clauses. Since the Middle East conflict began in March 2026, new quotes are mostly on price-variation basis; management said no pressure yet seen on pricing or inquiry pipeline.
LOI worth INR193.92 crore from APTRANSCO for 12 units of 160 MVA, 220 kV class autotransformers. 12 new customers added in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 765 kV plant ramp-up delayed by the lack of a technology partner, and will the designs align with Power Grid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the partner route remains open but it is proceeding in-house; 765 kV is in Unit 5 and 400 kV in Unit 4 in parallel. COO said CEA has standardised 400 and 765 kV specifications, so designs are acceptable to Power Grid and other Indian customers.

qa_highlights.question: Why did order inflow fall about 55% QoQ, and what to expect in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO-level answer: a management decision to cautiously book 220 kV and below orders after a large Q1 booking base covering about 1.5 years; 400 kV and above will be the focus once a 400 kV prototype is ready. Management said the INR3,000 crore-plus book covers visibility.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the order book is firm-price, and will new orders carry price variation clauses?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said firm-price share is 10-12%; COO later said 3-4%. COO said new quotes since March are price-variation based, with at most 1-2% of the last six months' book on firm price.

qa_highlights.question: How will the INR193 crore capex be funded, and is more capex planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Funded mainly from internal accruals, with bank term loans tied up but not drawn. No other major capex planned beyond small staff housing projects.

qa_highlights.question: Will the remaining firm-price orders keep margins down in Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: COO said customers agreed to price revisions bringing 2025 booking prices in line with current levels, so no major negative margin impact is expected in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Can EBITDA margins reach the earlier 18-19% aspiration, and what is the pricing outlook from new capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO reiterated the 16-18% FY27-FY28 range, with H2 expected to lift margins through operating leverage. COO said no pricing pressure seen so far, though some peers are expanding capacity.

risks_watch: Gross margin compression on remaining firm-price orders and commodity volatility (transformer oil, copper, steel) that management says is still a key factor to monitor.
Customer site readiness: about 30% of the INR180 crore deferred orders is still pending dispatch, with completion targeted in Q3 FY27.
Inventory rose to INR632.9 crore from INR364.1 crore in six months, creating working capital pressure. Management expects it to unwind as deferred orders are executed.
Supply chain risk for critical components (bushings, containers) due to typhoons and Middle East conflict; management says the issue is temporary.
Execution risk on 400 kV first unit (commercial contribution Q4 FY27) and 765 kV production (Q4 FY27), with the technology partner route stalled by sanctions.
Order inflow slowdown in Q2 and the low utilisation of Vadod (30%) and Jambusar (7-8%) plants; the IDT and backward integration commissioning dates are key checkpoints.
544527|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term outlook and margin range, but defensive about the Q2 miss, attributing it to weather, commodity costs and deferred deliveries. Management was evasive on FY29 targets and US margin uplift, and gave inconsistent answers on firm-price order share (10-12% vs 3-4%).
key_quotes: Importantly, these represent deferred deliveries and not cancellations and these orders continue to remain part of our order book.
We maintain that our EBITDA margin for FY27 and FY28 would be ranging around 16% to 18%, and we are still firm on the belief that we will be achieving this margin in current year and coming year.
Green Energy Corridors will definitely improve the demand, but, on our side, we will still try and at least commit 40%.

rows.why: Inventory rose to INR632.9 crore from INR364.1 crore (+74%) in six months; management expects it to unwind as ~30% of the INR180 crore deferred orders are executed in Q3 FY27.

544528|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 20.3% QoQ to INR2,267 million but fell 5% YoY on West Bengal atta disruption; EBITDA margin 13%.
544528|2026-09.overview: Revenue from operations was INR2,267 million, up 20.3% QoQ and down 5% YoY, with B2C down 2.5% YoY almost entirely due to atta. Excluding atta, B2C grew 4.9% YoY and 26% QoQ. Operating EBITDA rose 23.6% YoY to INR295 million at a 13% margin (+302 bps YoY), helped mainly by lower other expenses from advertising phasing. PAT rose 68.7% YoY to INR188 million as finance costs fell to INR6 million. Management guided FY27 revenue down about 5% and EBITDA margin up 50-70 bps, with H2 margins structurally lower than H1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the strategy for non-West Bengal regions?

qa_highlights.question: How are spices growing and what is the outlook?

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY28 outlook and margin sustainability?

qa_highlights.question: What are the advertising spend numbers?

qa_highlights.question: Why is H2 margin expected to be lower?

544530|2026-03.headline: Anand Rathi Q4 FY26 consolidated PAT rose 125.7% YoY to ₹416 million on revenue of ₹2,557 million, while the MTF book fell 10.53% QoQ.

Recoveries will be booked only when reasonably certain.
