544530|2026-09.headline: Anand Rathi Q2 FY27 revenue rose 20% YoY to INR2,732 million and PAT rose 50% to INR419 million, a record quarter per management.
544530|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations grew 20% YoY to INR2,732 million, with PAT up 50% YoY to INR419 million at a 15% margin. H1 revenue rose 21% to INR5,193 million; H1 PAT after exceptional items was INR653 million (up 29%), and PAT before exceptional items was INR810 million (up 60%). Broking and related services grew 34% YoY to INR1,551 million, while the MTF book reached INR14,993 million at 30 September, already about 57% of the year-end guidance. Management said market volumes were weak in derivatives but cash volumes were improving, and it discussed the drop in net cash, which it attributed to clients moving margins from FDs into G-Secs.

financial_highlights.metric: Broking and related services revenue (Q2 FY27)
Broking and related services revenue (H1 FY27)

financial_highlights.change: Q2 distribution income up about 4% YoY per analyst question; not confirmed by management

segments.name: Broking and related services
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR1,551 million (+34% YoY); H1 INR2,831 million (+25% YoY). Equity cash is 52% of broking revenue. Digital platform contributed 36% of brokerage income in H1.

segments.name: Margin trading facility (MTF)
segments.commentary: Book INR14,993 million at 30 Sep 2026 against year-end guidance of INR17,500-18,000 million. Q2 MTF book grew 38% YoY to INR1,499 crore; MTF interest income INR496 million in Q2 (+36%) and INR924 million in H1 (+43%). Borrowing cost about 9.5%, NIM about 4.5%, zero NPAs, average book per client below INR17 lakh.

segments.name: Distribution and non-broking
segments.commentary: Distribution AUM INR99,990 million, up 29% YoY. Distribution income INR327 million in Q2 and INR603 million in H1. Trail income now covers about 75% of salary costs, per management.

segments.name: Asset management and custody
segments.commentary: Asset management grew 29% YoY to INR99,990 million. Under custody grew about 13% YoY to about INR1.15 trillion.

guidance_outlook: Year-end MTF book target of INR1,750-1,800 crore, which the MTF figures in the call suggest is a different scale from the INR17,500-18,000 million year-end guidance quoted by the WTD; the two figures are inconsistent and need checking.
Distribution AUM to grow about 40% by end of FY27; management said it had already reached 29% growth by September.
Broking revenue targeted to grow 15-20% and non-broking 30-35% (up to 40% in some cases).
Long-term target: top line growth of about 15-20% and bottom line growth of about 20-25% to 30%.
capex_capacity: Network at 30 Sep 2026: 99 branches and 1,071 authorised persons across 314 cities.
Client base about 10.5 lakh, of which 55% have been with the firm for more than 3 years and 71% of active clients are in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities.
Employee base grew: management said it adds about 150 employees on an ongoing basis; Q2 employee expenses rose about 31% YoY, partly from bringing outsourced staff onto payroll.
New products: insurance is being stabilised, AIF is being added to distribution, and an NRI business is being built.
demand_pricing: Nifty 50 fell 5.22% in the quarter and 1.3% in H1, including a 6% fall in September. IPO activity was strong: 108 IPOs raised about INR90,000 crore in Q2, and H1 raised INR96,585 crore across 154 mainboard IPOs.
Industry MTF book was INR156,261 crore as of 12 Oct 2026, up about 41% YoY. Demat accounts were about 24 crore, with 31.1 lakh added in September.

Management said cash-market volumes were improving while F&O and capital-market volumes were flat to lower. It said Anand Rathi's broking growth outperformed the industry because it has no proprietary trading volumes.
Distribution income growth lagged AUM growth because of upfront commissions in the prior year and the RBI/AMFI ARN transfer cooling period, which was extended from 6 to 12 months.
Around INR300 crore of MTF-related impact from an RBI circular was absorbed, and borrowing costs were held at around 9.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did distribution income grow only 4% when distribution AUM grew 29%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed upfront commissions earned in the prior year that did not repeat, plus a longer 12-month ARN transfer cooling period. It said trail income is rising and now covers about 75% of salaries.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee expenses rise about 31% in the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said outsourced staff were moved onto the payroll, which it called largely one-time. It also said it keeps adding RMs and product staff, about 150 employees on an ongoing basis.

qa_highlights.question: Have trading volumes recovered since Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cash-market volumes were growing consistently while derivatives and capital-market volumes were static or lower. Broking revenue is tracking cash volumes.

qa_highlights.question: How is MTF spread and risk managed?
qa_highlights.answer: Borrowing cost is about 9.5% and NIM about 4.5%. Average book per client is below INR17 lakh, and the company says its MTF NPA has been zero for 8 years. Policy has not changed; the stock list is about 1,000 approved stocks out of about 2,000 permitted.

qa_highlights.question: Why did net cash fall from about INR2,700 crore to about INR900 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said HNI clients moved margin cash from FDs into G-Secs following an RBI circular. Business is intact, and the decline reflects a change in the form of client margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt-market strategy with yields above 7.40%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt is a small allocation for clients. It sees rising rates in the next 3-6 months and recommends short-term G-Sec allocation only, with equity preferred over the long term.

risks_watch: Derivatives and capital-market volumes remain weak, and broking growth depends on cash-market volumes.
Net cash fell sharply (about INR2,700 crore to about INR900 crore) on the client margin shift to G-Secs. Watch whether this affects liquidity and interest income.
Distribution income lagged AUM growth. Track whether trail income catches up as management expects.
Employee costs rose about 31% YoY in Q2, and the company plans ongoing hiring. Watch the operating margin.
Rising interest rates may affect the MTF spread and the borrowing cost, which is about 9.5%.
Inconsistent MTF targets in the transcript (INR1,750-1,800 crore vs INR17,500-18,000 million) need clarification.
544530|2026-09.management_tone: Management was confident on growth and on MTF asset quality, saying the book is at zero NPAs and that guidance is already largely met. It was more defensive on the distribution income gap and the net cash decline, which it attributed to a change in client margin format.
key_quotes: I'm happy to share with all of you that the last quarter, we have achieved our highest ever revenue as well as higher ever profitability.
Considering all those facts, our NPA into MTF book is zero.
Business-wise, business is intact, and cash flow -wise, it's just a change format change in cash flow.

rows.why: H1 PAT before exceptionals rose 60% to INR810 million on revenue up 21%, showing operating leverage, but Q2 employee expenses rose about 31% YoY with about 150 hires planned on an ongoing basis, and MTF NIM is about 4.5% against a 9.5% borrowing cost, so margin gains are not assured.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: MTF book reached INR14,993 million at 30 Sep, about 57% of the INR17,500-18,000 million year-end guidance, and distribution AUM is up 29% against a ~40% FY27 target, though derivatives and capital-market volumes are flat to lower.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management says guidance is already largely met, with MTF at about 57% of target by September and distribution AUM at +29% against ~40% goal, but the MTF target figures in the transcript are inconsistent and the broking outlook depends on cash volumes.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Distribution income rose only about 4% YoY in Q2 against 29% AUM growth, derivatives volumes are weak, and rising rates may pressure the MTF spread on a 9.5% borrowing cost.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management said AIF is being added to distribution and an NRI business is being built, though no launch dates or sizes were given.

rows.label: MTF book growth to year-end target
rows.why: MTF book at INR14,993 million on 30 Sep is about 57% of the INR17,500-18,000 million target, and the industry MTF book grew about 41% YoY to INR156,261 crore, so the target looks reachable.

rows.label: Net cash decline from client margin shift to G-Secs
rows.why: Net cash fell from about INR2,700 crore to about INR900 crore as HNI clients moved margin cash from FDs into G-Secs, a change management called format-only, though it could still affect interest income.

rows.label: Distribution trail income catching up
rows.why: Trail income now covers about 75% of salary costs, and the ARN cooling period went from 6 to 12 months, so distribution income should catch up only if trail income compounds on AUM up 29%.

tone.note: Management was confident on MTF asset quality (zero NPAs for 8 years) and on growth, but defensive on the distribution income gap (4% vs 29% AUM growth) and the net cash decline; analysts pushed on those two points and on employee cost growth.

544531|2026-03.headline: True Colors FY26 revenue rose 29.22% to INR 301.55 crore, with EBITDA margin at 15.58% and PAT at INR 31.16 crore, but operating cash flow was negative.
544531|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue from operations was INR 301.55 crore (up 29.22% YoY), EBITDA INR 46.98 crore (15.58% margin) and PAT INR 31.16 crore (10.33% margin). Recurring revenue from ink, sublimation paper and spares was about 50.25% of revenue. Operating cash flow was negative (about INR 35 crore), which management attributed to MSME payment-term compliance, Konica Minolta advance-payment terms and a rise in receivables to INR 111 crore at March-end, now reported at about INR 93 crore. Management is moving ink from trading to in-house manufacturing under the INKIA brand, with a phased capex plan.

Compared with a figure of about INR 31 crore in the analyst's question (sign and comparison not clarified)

segments.commentary: FY26 reported ink volume was 1,140 tons, with ink revenue about INR 74 crore. Ink is being moved from import/distribution to in-house manufacturing under INKIA; INKIA produced about 80 tons per month last year and 80 tons was added via the merger.

segments.commentary: Digital fabric printing capacity is 75,000 meters per day. Revenue split is about 50:50 between customer-supplied fabric (job work) and company-bought fabric. About 6% of fabric revenue is direct export.

segments.name: Commercial printing (new)
segments.commentary: Early-stage entry into label, mica and packaging printing, starting as a trading/distribution business with no additional capex planned. No service team has been added yet.

qa_highlights.question: Why enter commercial printing (labels, mica, packaging)?
qa_highlights.answer: The company says the same ink formulation capability can serve commercial printers; it is a first step via trading, with aggressive expansion only if market feedback is strong.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall from about 18% last year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a mix effect: paper revenue was concentrated in H2 last year, and about 45-50 tons of ink bundled with machines this year was not reported as ink revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Will the INKIA ink be accepted by customers versus imported ink?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INKIA has supplied about 2-2.5 years, with 2,000-2,500 tons of white-label ink consumed, and that compatibility testing is a 4-5 year journey that is already complete.

qa_highlights.question: How is the ink capex funded and what working capital days are targeted?

qa_highlights.answer: Management said machine realization varies widely by model and declined to give a current average; the bundled ink revenue is expected to show up in future ink revenue.

544532|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 235% YoY to INR591 crore, but EBITDA margin was 12.1% and FY26 PAT margin 8.5%, below the 11% promised earlier.
544532|2026-03.overview: Solarworld reported Q4 FY26 revenue from operations of INR591 crore (up 235% YoY), EBITDA of INR73 crore (12.1% margin) and PAT of INR49 crore (8.1% net margin). For FY26, total income was INR1,416 crore (up 1.57% YoY), EBITDA INR187.9 crore (13.3%) and PAT INR120.4 crore (8.5%). Management blamed a loss-making initial module ramp after ALMM approval in December 2025 and sharp raw material cost increases in Q4 linked to the West Asia conflict. The company is pivoting toward BESS, with a 582 MWac / 1.2 GWh DC BESS project pipeline and a 3.4 GW BESS line in trials.

segments.name: Solar EPC
segments.commentary: FY26 EPC revenue about INR1,250 crore; management cites EPC PAT margin close to 10.5%. EPC margin guided at 9-11% through the cycle and 8-11% overall for FY27. Solar EPC order book about INR1,674 crore.

segments.name: BESS EPC
segments.commentary: FY26 BESS revenue was nil; management guides INR800-1,000 crore in FY27. BESS order book about INR1,136 crore. Q4 orders from NTPC at Solapur and Unchahar aggregate about 514 MWh, order value about INR5 billion incl. O&M. BESS margin guided at 14-15% PBT.

segments.name: Solar module manufacturing
segments.commentary: 1.5 GW Roorkee module line began operations after ALMM approval in December 2025; about two to two-and-a-half months of run-time in FY26 produced a slight loss. Breakeven at about 30-35% utilisation; FY26-27 utilisation expected at 40-45% on about 600 MW captive NTPC REL orders, rising to 60-65% with more orders. Line capex about INR146 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 order book conversion target at least 70% of about INR2,800 crore, i.e. about INR2,000 crore revenue; EPC about INR2,000 crore including BESS INR800-1,000 crore.
Management expects 40-45% revenue growth in FY27 and says it will not sustain FY26's 200-250% growth.
Overall EBITDA/PAT margin guided at 8-11%; sustaining current margins if the West Asia conflict eases, with slight downside if raw material prices keep rising.
BESS margin guided at 14-15% PBT; 3.4 GW BESS line capex about INR55-60 crore, potential revenue about INR3,000 crore at full capacity (740 containers at INR4.5 crore each).
Q1 and Q2 seasonally weak; Q3 and Q4 strong. Management declined to give a half-yearly split.
1.2 GW solar cell line at Pandhurna targeted for commercial operation by June 2027; cell-line funds to be deployed from Q3 FY27.
No near-term plans to add module or cell capacity until about 75-80% captive utilisation is visible.
capex_capacity: Module: 1.5 GW Roorkee facility (7.5 acres, automated ATW and Horad lines) operational; output 600-750 W TOPCon-type panels across M10R, G12R and G12 configurations.
BESS: 3.4 GW fully automated line (KUKA robotics) ready, trials underway; capex about INR55-60 crore already spent.
Solar cell: 1.2 GW line at Pandhurna, approvals mostly received, construction to start around June 2026, commercial operation targeted by June 2027.
Junction box: 5 GW line being set up in a joint venture; site ready for trials.

Operational capacity to be added on commissioning: a 272 MW project and a 70 MW project expected to complete in June 2026; management expects about 600 MW near term, about 700 MW next quarter and about 1.5 GW by year-end.
demand_pricing: PSU tenders were about 40 GW last year; the company executes about 1-1.5 GW a year, so it sees limited impact from a slower tendering market.
Raw material costs up sharply since Oct 2025: copper about +40%, aluminium about +50%, steel higher; INR depreciated from about 85-86 to about 96 per USD, affecting BESS imported inputs.
ALMM List-II (cells) applies from June 2026; management expects 90-95% of projects to shift to DCR cells, with a possible 6-12 month cell shortage.
Current order book has no ALMM-2 cell requirement, giving a headway of about a year. Lithium cells for BESS are sourced from China as no Indian supplier exists.
PPA signing delays after L1 bids and grid connectivity constraints are slowing the solar tender market; management expects connectivity to take 10-12 more months to resolve.
Claims filed with SJVN for about INR219 crore; only INR52 crore recognised as receivable. Ind AS allows recognition only after dispute-board award.

qa_highlights.question: PAT margin is 8-8.5% versus the 11% promised earlier, and top line is short of the INR1,500 crore target. What is the guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EPC PAT margin is about 10.5%, with the module loss from a short ramp and Q4 raw material headwinds dragging the total. Guidance is INR1,900-2,000 crore revenue and 8-11% overall margins.

qa_highlights.question: Battery cell unit timeline, and when will it contribute?
qa_highlights.answer: The 1.2 GW cell line at Pandhurna is now targeted for commercial start by June 2027, with construction starting around June 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expense rise, and what is the BESS capex and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Other expense rose to INR83 million from INR74 million; last year's base included a INR140 million write-off that was recovered this year. The 3.4 GW BESS line capex is INR55-60 crore; margin 14-15% PBT.

qa_highlights.question: How will the module line utilisation ramp, and what is breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: Breakeven is around 30-35% utilisation. Utilisation should reach 40-45% on existing NTPC REL orders (about 600 MW), rising to 60-65% with new orders. All existing EPC orders can be serviced in-house.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company expand module or cell capacity, and why are PPAs being rescinded?
qa_highlights.answer: No expansion planned until 75-80% captive use is visible. PPA delays stem from DISCOM absorption and transmission constraints; management expects resolution by around end-FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for ROW, labour and the EPC tender pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: ROW compensation is moving to market rates, which helps, but management does not see it as the biggest hurdle; no major labour issues. Tender activity is slower, but the company's order book is full.

risks_watch: Margin pressure from copper, aluminium, steel and INR depreciation; management guides 8-11% overall margin range.
Execution risk on the 60-40 BESS to EPC mix, with BESS revenue ramp from nil to INR800-1,000 crore and most BESS projects due by June 2027.

Customer concentration in PSU and NTPC REL orders; PPA rescissions and slower PSU tendering.

segments.commentary: Contributed 24.55% of FY26 revenue. Management called it one of the fastest-growing verticals and among the highest-margin, and said it expects revenue to at least double in the coming period, without giving a percentage target.

segments.name: International (Chtr International / Dubai subsidiary)
segments.commentary: About 18% of FY26 revenue. Dubai subsidiary is the gateway to the Middle East; priority markets are MENA, with APAC and LATAM evaluated selectively. Management said it will expand in a lean way.

544547|2026-03.headline: Jinkushal Q4 FY26 standalone revenue rose 89% YoY to INR133 crore, a record quarter, but full-year PAT was only INR12.44 crore as logistics and HexL brand costs weighed.
544547|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 delivered the highest quarterly standalone and consolidated revenue in company history, with standalone revenue up 89% YoY to INR133 crore and consolidated at INR192 crore. Full-year standalone revenue grew 48% to INR313 crore, but standalone PAT was INR12.44 crore and consolidated PAT was INR12.76 crore, with management attributing the margin pressure to freight and geopolitical logistics costs, HexL brand investment and higher employee costs. Consolidated net worth rose from INR86 crore to INR194 crore after the IPO, while working capital increased on higher volumes and overseas inventory. Management declined to give FY27 revenue guidance, citing the Middle East conflict, and reiterated a medium-term target of INR600-700 crore revenue in 2.5-3 years.

segments.commentary: Customised machines of other brands contributed about 62%, refurbished used construction equipment about 35%, and HexL own-brand about 5% (4.9-5% consolidated; about 7% standalone).

segments.name: Geography FY26
segments.commentary: Mexico about 46%, UAE about 19%, South Africa and Australia about 10% each (per management's approximate figures), with the rest in single digits. Management said exports are about 97-98% of revenue.

segments.name: HexL brand
segments.commentary: Own brand in early build-out with lower margins; management targets 11-12% of FY27 revenue and about 150 units in FY27.

guidance_outlook: No FY27 revenue growth guidance given, citing geopolitical uncertainty around the Middle East conflict and the Strait of Hormuz.
Medium-term vision of INR600-700 crore revenue in 2.5-3 years, reiterated from the prior call.
Medium-term targets: revenue of INR600-800 crore at about 5-7% consolidated PAT margin before focusing on cash conversion cycle.
Management expects FY27 profitability to improve faster than revenue if Middle East logistics normalise.
Long-run margin targets: 12-14% PAT for HexL and refurbished used equipment; 2-4% for new equipment of other brands.
HexL unit milestones to track: 100, 250 and 500 units; FY27 target about 150 units.
Cash conversion cycle expected to improve next year, not in the near term.
capex_capacity: Overseas inventory held above INR50 crore as at 31 March 2026; about 70% available for retail opportunities and 30% allocated to customers pending order confirmation.
Offices in Dubai and Kissimmee, Florida, USA.
Management said capital, not market size, is the main constraint on growth; refurbishment expertise is cited as the operating base.
No immediate plans for new overseas geographies or inventory hubs, though 80-100 countries are cited as the long-term addressable base.
Management did not disclose a new manufacturing unit or specific capex plan.
demand_pricing: Management said demand for construction and mining equipment stayed resilient, supported by infrastructure, industrial capex and replacement demand in emerging markets.
West Asia crisis raised logistics costs, freight, insurance and currency volatility; management said freight costs were absorbed in P&L and were the main reason for profit decline.
Mexico Q4 performance was better than Q3, but management did not quantify FY26 Mexico decline.

No order pipeline; inventory-led sales model with working capital churn of 2-2.5 times.

qa_highlights.question: How will HexL affect working capital?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory positioning and customer credit for HexL keep the cash conversion cycle higher; management expects it to ease after the brand is established, next year at the earliest.

qa_highlights.question: What is the geographic mix and how is Mexico trending?
qa_highlights.answer: Mexico about 46%, UAE about 19%, South Africa and Australia about 10% each; management said Mexico Q4 was stronger than Q3.

qa_highlights.answer: Working capital is INR300-350 crore; management said each INR100 crore of additional working capital could support roughly INR200-300 crore of revenue after the INR600-700 crore milestone.

544547|2026-06.headline: Jinkushal Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 37.4% to INR51.29 crores, but consolidated PAT fell to INR2.2 crores from INR6.51 crores.
544547|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue grew 37.4% YoY to INR51.29 crores and consolidated revenue grew 15.9% to INR56.57 crores. Profitability fell sharply on a consolidated basis, with PBT at INR3.04 crores versus INR7.26 crores, as shipping costs and employee expenses rose. Africa contributed about 32% of revenue against about 4.47% a year earlier, partly replacing Middle East business disrupted by geopolitics. Management said inventory of about INR96.8 crores, mostly overseas, is being built as part of the international strategy, and that investments in people and systems will weigh on margins for several quarters.

segments.name: Africa (geography)
segments.commentary: Contributed about 32% of Q1 FY27 revenue versus about 4.47% in Q1 FY26, offsetting lost Middle East revenue. Management said it sees the shipping and business cycle as established.

segments.name: HexL (proprietary construction equipment brand)
segments.commentary: Management said it is in early stages, with heavy spending on marketing, discounting and dealer development. Management cited a long-term PAT target of 12% to 14% (also 12% to 15% in an earlier call) and a 20% to 40% retail price advantage versus global brands.

segments.name: New/customised equipment, used and refurbished equipment
segments.commentary: No segment revenue split was disclosed. Management said new customised equipment demand is strongest near term, and that used equipment and HexL should each grow to a larger share over 2 to 3 years.

guidance_outlook: Long-term revenue target of INR600 crores to INR700 crores, to be reached in 2 to 3 years; management declined to give a FY27 growth figure.
Management expects healthier profitability in 2 to 3 years once shipping, interest and manpower costs settle; near-term profit is being sacrificed for long-term build-out.
Inventory expected to stay at similar levels, plus or minus a few percentage points, in lower double digits, with conversion over about 2 quarters.
Expects to see results from strategic investments in 3 to 6 quarters.
Expects operational manpower costs to keep rising over the next few quarters.
capex_capacity: Consolidated inventory of about INR96.8 crores at June 30, 2026, of which about INR84.4 crores sits at overseas subsidiaries.
Inventory is positioned overseas to shorten delivery times for used and refurbished construction equipment.
Management says the investments are transient (inventory, working capital, manpower) rather than fixed capex or plant machinery.
Post-IPO capital base and enhanced banking facilities cited as capacity to support higher volumes.
demand_pricing: Africa is now a major market; management said the Middle East revenue gap was partly filled by Africa.
Freight and shipping costs rose on geopolitical route closures and longer shipping times, which also lengthened debtor cycles.
Commodity inflation is not expected to be fully passed through; costs are partly absorbed and partly passed to suppliers and customers.
Management said new customised equipment is in highest demand, driven by faster availability and lower breakdown times for end users.
Management said customer collections have generally met commercial timelines, but geopolitical disruptions have led to some customer payment delays.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving Africa's growth and can it be sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Africa replaced Middle East revenue hit by geopolitics and board capital allocation decisions. Management expects the shipping and business cycle there to be sustainable, and it sees Africa, Latin America and the Middle East as equally important.

qa_highlights.question: Will the INR97 crore inventory convert to sales, and how fast?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the business cycle runs at least 2 quarters, so inventory should convert over the next 1.5 to 2 quarters, with inventory levels fluctuating by a few percentage points over the last 2 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and debtors rise: what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called the debtor rise a planned overseas penetration strategy, with longer shipping times keeping receivables high until machines reach customers. It expects working capital cycles to stay elevated for now.

qa_highlights.question: Will freight costs ease and can they be passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is taking a substantial hit on shipping costs, partly passing them to suppliers at purchase and to customers at sale. Management said it cannot forecast oil prices.

qa_highlights.question: Will employee costs yield operating leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it plans to add sales and purchase staff and to move from SME to mid-corporate or large-corporate operations, and will keep investing even at the cost of near-term reported margins.

qa_highlights.question: When will returns on these investments become visible, and what will the business look like in 3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects results in 3 to 6 quarters. In 2 to 3 years it targets INR600 crores to INR700 crores revenue with healthier profitability, a dominant international business, and roughly equal revenue from the three verticals.

risks_watch: Consolidated PAT fell about 66% YoY, and management is absorbing shipping, interest and manpower costs without a date for recovery.
Inventory of about INR96.8 crores with about INR84.4 crores overseas ties up working capital and raises conversion risk.
Africa accounts for about 32% of revenue; management said it is not viewing any single geography in isolation.
Freight costs depend on oil prices, which management said it cannot forecast; geopolitical route closures are extending shipping times.
Management declined to give FY27 revenue guidance and gave no segment-level margin or revenue numbers.

Management said the company manufactures backhoe loaders under contract in China, and an analyst raised natural calamities there as a supply risk; management said the locations it uses are unaffected.
544547|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on long-term targets and the Africa shift, but cautious and evasive on near-term profitability, FY27 growth and HexL economics. Management repeatedly deferred forward-looking questions because of geopolitical uncertainty.

544550|2026-06.headline: Pace Digitek Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 51.3% YoY to Rs.555 crore; FY27 guidance of Rs.3,200-3,400 crore reiterated on Rs.10,803 crore executable order book.

EBITDA was Rs.86.1 crore (15.5% margin vs 14.9% in Q4) and PAT was Rs.63 crore (11.3% margin vs Rs.55 crore in Q1 FY26). Order inflow in the quarter was about Rs.1,677 crore, with two energy EPC wins (NLC, DVC, ~Rs.1,412 crore) and a BSNL OFC project (~Rs.265 crore). Management said the 5 GWh BESS line is operational, with a further 5 GWh line due to be commissioned by December 2026, and reiterated the FY27 revenue guidance.

segments.name: Energy (BESS, renewable EPC, BOO)
segments.commentary: Contributed 79.5% of Q1 revenue and is the main growth driver; energy executable order book Rs.8,453 crore, split Rs.4,074 crore BOO and Rs.4,367 crore EPC. Management expects energy to be about 65-70% of the order book by year end.

segments.name: Telecom & ICT (BharatNet, Railway Kavach, BSNL OFC)
segments.commentary: Contributed 20.5% of Q1 revenue; executable order book Rs.2,350 crore. Kavach about 30% complete; BSNL OFC (~Rs.265 crore) to execute over about 2.5 years. Management said telecom has better margins but lower volume.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue guidance of Rs.3,200-3,400 crore reiterated; management said it sees no concern in achieving it, with most revenue expected from the existing order book.
H1 FY27 targeted at 40-45% of full-year revenue vs 35% in H1 FY26.
Q2 container supply planned at 210 units; management expects about 125+ containers per month in the next calendar year.
FY27 PAT margin guidance of 10.5-11% for BESS, with the lithium-ion cell cost increase said to be factored in.
Cash flow from operations expected to turn positive by March 2027; inventory and receivables expected to stabilise between December and March.
Energy-to-telecom order book mix expected to move to about 65:35 or 70:30 by year end.
capex_capacity: BESS capacity is 5 GWh operational (two 2.5 GWh lines); a third 5 GWh line is due for installation in October 2026, targeting 10 GWh by early December 2026 as India's largest operational BESS facility.
Total capex of about Rs.300 crore for the 5 GWh expansion phase, the container fabrication unit, and related setup, mainly land cost, funded from the earlier private placement.
In-house container manufacturing started with trials this month; batch production from next month. Over 300 containers supplied to date.

BOO projects: 975 MWh commissioned to date (MSEDCL standalone BESS, about Rs.900 crore recognised in P&L); four BOO projects expected to add about Rs.750 crore annual revenue once all are commissioned.
Pune R&D centre inaugurated about three weeks ago; cell manufacturing planning under way. Applying for 4 GWh under the government cell PLI scheme (10 GWh total scheme).
demand_pricing: Bidding for about 27 GWh of tenders; NTPC Renewable Energy and NTPC Green tenders noted, with NTPC Green tenders drawing only 7-8 bidders versus 32-51 in earlier state tenders.
Management said bidding aggression has eased after a 4 GWh Maharashtra project was cancelled and a Punjab tender saw a single bid at higher prices.
Management said cell cost is about 60% of total BESS cost, unchanged; recent tenders include price variation clauses while older tenders do not. Stock was built in March to lower Q1 cell costs.

C&I BESS (below 5 MWh) received product approval from large Indian customers; first trial order of about 25 units, with management referring to potential for thousands per year. Management guided C&I EBITDA margin about 4-5 points above grid-scale product margin of 13-15%.
Container unit value about Rs.4-4.5 crore; about 70 containers per month currently.
Early exports: small container supply to a Saudi company in Q1 and an MoU signed in Saudi Arabia.
MEGMEET tie-up for AI data-centre power solutions in India; demo equipment planned; management said a concrete revenue plan could come in about one quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Telecom & ICT order inflow break-up and execution timeline for the Rs.2,350 crore telecom book?
qa_highlights.answer: Of Rs.1,677 crore inflow, NLC and DVC EPC wins were about Rs.1,412 crore and BSNL OFC about Rs.265 crore. EPC projects run about one year; OFC about 2.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY27 guidance not higher given the energy order book visibility?
qa_highlights.answer: BOO solar-plus-BESS capex is capitalised as a fixed asset and not recognised as revenue, so physical execution will exceed reported revenue. Revenue recognition comes from EPC and standalone BESS in BOO.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cash flow and working-capital profile by segment?

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue path needed from Q2 onwards?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most of the remaining Rs.2,700 crore should come from the existing order book, with Q1 seasonally low due to government funding and approval cycles.

qa_highlights.question: How will rising lithium-ion cell prices affect EPC and BOO margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance of 10.5-11% margin already includes anticipated cell price increases; price variation clauses in new tenders and stock built in March mitigate impact.

544550|2026-09.headline: Pace Digitek Q2 FY27 revenue rose 51.5% YoY to Rs 808 crore and FY27 revenue guidance was raised to Rs 3,300-3,500 crore.
544550|2026-09.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue was Rs 808 crore (+51.5% YoY, +45.5% QoQ) and H1 revenue was Rs 1,364 crore (+51.4%), with energy about 80% and telecom about 20%. Q2 EBITDA rose 68.5% YoY to Rs 159 crore and PAT rose 43.3% to Rs 97 crore, though management said margins were flattered by a higher telecom services mix. Borrowings rose to Rs 1,371 crore from Rs 961 crore in March 2026, driven by build-to-operate (BOT) assets, and net debt-to-equity moved to 0.35x. Management raised FY27 revenue guidance but kept FY28 at Rs 4,000-4,200 crore, and said it has paused new BOT projects without external investment.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 10,735 crore (energy Rs 8,528 crore; telecom Rs 2,208 crore)
financial_highlights.change: H1 inflows Rs 2,437 crore (energy Rs 2,173 crore; telecom Rs 265 crore)

segments.commentary: Energy contributed about 80% of H1 revenue; energy EBITDA margin is 12-13% per management, and the combined EBITDA margin was flattered by telecom services. H1 BESS commissioning was about 875 MWh, with 1.8 GWh delivered to customers to date.

segments.commentary: Telecom contributed about 20% of revenue, with EBITDA margin around 20% (20-23% on projects, about 25% on O&M). More than 8,000 BSNL sites were commissioned and entered a 5-year O&M phase.

FY28 PAT margin guided at about 10% (management later said 10-11%), down from the 11-12% level seen in H1 FY27, which was helped by telecom turnkey projects.
Blended EBITDA margin expected at 16-17% as energy mix rises; container in-house fabrication expected to cut BESS cost by 4-5% gross and add about 1.5-2% at EBITDA level.
Build-to-operate revenue expected at Rs 325-375 crore in FY28, after Rs 197 crore from the current project and about Rs 200 crore from two projects commissioning by March 2027.
Peak debt expected at around Rs 1,100 crore of additional borrowing by March 2027, with about Rs 1,600 crore of back-to-back BOT assets.
C&I to target about 30% of energy revenue in the next financial year (FY28); C&I margins expected to lift blended EBITDA by at least 1-2%.
capex_capacity: BESS manufacturing capacity expanded from 2.5 GWh to 5 GWh in August 2026; production currently running at full 5 GWh. About 844 MWh produced in H1 FY27, equal to 94% of FY26 output.
Expansion to 10 GWh: an additional 5 GWh setup to be completed in Q3 FY27, with production starting in Q4 and about one quarter needed to reach full utilisation.
In-house BESS container facility: trial production from November 2026 and full-scale production from January 2027, expected to meet about 50% of container requirements.
BESS volume target of about 200 containers per quarter; Q2 sold about 91 containers plus 10 in stock (about 100), and Q3 target is slightly below 200.

Build-to-operate asset stood at Rs 1,311 crore at 30 Sep 2026; about 60% commissioned, with completion expected December 2026 or January 2027. Management has paused new BOT projects absent external investment.
4 GWh cell manufacturing (PLI) tendering expected to complete by mid-November 2026; cell plant to start in the next financial year, with technology transfer still under study at the R&D centre.
demand_pricing: Management sees BESS demand of about 30-35 GWh in FY27, rising to about 236 GWh by FY32.
Bidding competition has eased: about 6-8 participants per tender now versus 25-30 earlier; management said margin pressure persists but is smaller.
Lithium-ion cell prices rose about 20% in the prior quarter, hurting energy project margins; prices are now falling and expected to stabilise. Tenders bid over the last 3-4 months use the new prices.
Landed Chinese BESS price is roughly in line with Pace's manufacturing cost plus margin.
From January 2027, about 6% export rebate cut on Chinese cell imports; management expects lower cell prices to offset it.
Standalone EBITDA margin fell due to early-stage MAHAGENCO solar supply-and-erection and Bondada balance-of-systems projects with higher initial mobilisation costs.
Receivable days were about 286 at March 2026; management expects receivable cycle near 150 days and payables of 60-90 days, for a net working capital cycle of 90-120 days.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp EBITDA margin improvement and how should margins trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it targets 17-19% EBITDA margin and that H1 was lifted by a larger telecom services share; energy margins are 12-13% and telecom about 20%. Blended margin is expected to fall to 16-17% as energy grows.

qa_highlights.question: Q2 container volumes and Q3-Q4 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: About 100 containers in Q2 (91 sold, 10 stocked) on an unchanged 2.5 GWh base, because the expanded capacity only started commercial production in September. Q3 is targeted at slightly below 200 containers.

qa_highlights.question: Benefit from in-house container fabrication?
qa_highlights.answer: Container cost expected to fall about 25%, BESS overall cost 4-5% at gross level, and about 1.5-2% at EBITDA level.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the Q2 standalone and energy margins decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Two new solar projects (MAHAGENCO and Bondada) carry high initial mobilisation costs, plus a 20% rise in lithium-ion cell prices last quarter and early-stage costs at the new BESS capacity. Management expects a slight recovery in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 10 GWh capacity supported by enough BESS demand, and how is FY28 guidance framed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said demand of 30-35 GWh in FY27 and 236 GWh by FY32 supports capacity; the 10 GWh is to reach full utilisation one quarter after Q4 start. FY28 guidance was not revised but management expects better. Revenue realisation is spread over about 2 years because most product goes into EPC and BOT projects.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working-capital outlook for receivables and payables?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivables are falling as telecom retentions are collected, and management expects receivable days near 150 and payables of 60-90 days. Consolidated payables fell from about Rs 1,800 crore to Rs 1,500 crore, with a target of Rs 800-900 crore.

544557|2026-03.headline: Glottis Q4 FY26 revenue rose to INR 1,959 mn (from INR 1,439 mn in Q3) but PAT margin was 5.5%; FY26 revenue fell to INR 7,226 mn with TEUs down to 89,098.
544557|2026-03.overview: Glottis reported Q4 FY26 revenue of INR 1,959 mn, up sequentially from INR 1,439 mn in Q3 but lower year-on-year, with EBITDA of INR 105 mn (5.4% margin) and PAT of INR 107 mn (5.5% margin). For FY26, revenue was INR 7,226 mn, EBITDA INR 495 mn (6.9% margin) and PAT INR 377 mn (5.2% margin), with management attributing the decline to softer freight rates and lower container volumes. Sea import remained the dominant vertical at about 78% of FY26 revenue, while air and export lines grew from small bases. The balance sheet moved to net cash of INR 510 mn after the IPO. Management was broadly upbeat on FY27 but gave no numerical guidance, and analysts pressed on receivables and falling revenue.

segments.name: Road transportation
segments.commentary: Contribution improved to about 5% of FY26 revenue.

segments.commentary: Renewable energy was the largest contributor at 40.9% of FY26 revenue; automobile share rose to 4.2% from 1.5% (more than doubled); agro products grew 58.7% YoY to 5.7% of revenue.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said receivable days rose because credit days were extended to customers to retain them amid global volatility and to support expansion; many new customers were added. Other current assets rose due to advances to suppliers and prepaid expenses, since shipping lines and agents are paid early while invoices go out 15-20 days later. No specific receivable or other-asset figures were given.

qa_highlights.answer: Crude and bunker cost changes are passed to exporters or importers through the bunker adjustment factor, so there is no impact as of now.

qa_highlights.answer: Management cited softer freight levels during the year and slower demand as the two main reasons for the revenue decline.

544558|2026-03.headline: Fabtech FY26 total income rose 28.4% to ₹431.33 crore, but margins compressed; management guides ~25% growth and 9.9–10.5% PAT margin.
544558|2026-03.overview: FY26 total income grew 28.4% YoY to ₹431.33 crore and EBITDA rose 18.29% to ₹55.56 crore, while reported net profit fell to ₹38.36 crore from ₹46.45 crore (FY25 included ₹17.85 crore exceptional item). Q4 total income rose 22% YoY to ₹168.24 crore and quarterly net profit rebounded to ₹22.06 crore. Margin pressure was attributed to remobilisation, a 33% rise in RMC cost and a 43% rise in execution cost, amid Middle East disruption. Cash and bank balance rose to ₹208.57 crore after a ~₹230 crore equity infusion (IPO), while receivables rose to ₹204.34 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why have margins shrunk despite revenue growth, and how will investor confidence be regained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited project and geography mix (Africa margin pressure), remobilisation, a ~33% RMC cost increase and ~43% execution cost increase; non-contribution margin at 43.8% vs 45.9% last year. Margins expected to improve as internal margin development progresses.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of Middle East conflict on Q4 and expected impact going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: No material financial impact per management; freight is the main cost pressure while RMC is sourced in India and revenue is in USD. Delivery delays are possible; no cancellations so far, and clients are discussing variation clauses.

qa_highlights.question: How are raw-material and freight increases reflected in customer contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Contracts contain variation clauses, with post-detailed-engineering items priced at net present value; management says clients accept variations to avoid project delays. It is not a pass-through, but a negotiated outcome that also affects future awards.

qa_highlights.question: What is the breakdown of the ₹900 crore order book by geography and the timeline for conversion?
qa_highlights.answer: Split across UAE, Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Kenya, other Africa and North Africa; to be executed over 18–24 months. Billing depends on client readiness to accept materials and complete installation.

qa_highlights.answer: Management called it an active decision: the JBN acquisition in the West is under due diligence and talent acquisition is ongoing. Current borrowings are USD PCFC lines at about SOFR-linked rates plus 200 bps.

544558|2026-06.headline: Fabtech Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 10% YoY to Rs 74.98 crore and PAT turned to Rs 4.21 crore from a Rs 6.13 crore loss.
544558|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 10.3% YoY to Rs 74.98 crore, with EBITDA of Rs 7.41 crore (9% margin) versus negative Rs 5.27 crore a year ago. Contribution margin expanded about 910 bps to 46.7%, which management attributes to geography mix (Saudi Arabia, Africa) and project mix, with reduced dependence on UAE. UAE FTS faced war-related headwinds, and several large orders slipped (not cancelled) into later quarters. Management reiterated 20-25% organic growth for FY27, with Q2 steady and Q3-Q4 stronger, and guided PAT margin of 9-11%.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said UAE demand is focused on high-tech facilities, cell and gene therapy labs and compounding pharmacies, with some projects delayed by geopolitics. It gave no timeline for normalisation.

qa_highlights.question: Does the West Asia war affect execution and working capital?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said on-site teams kept executing, but conversions slowed as customers delayed decisions. Management said working capital has not been impacted much, and the company is using outsourced labour selectively.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company move to percentage-of-completion accounting to smooth quarterly results?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is reworking contracts with auditors to define billable milestones tied to percentage completion. Existing contracts stay on shipment/milestone basis, and changes are expected over the next few years.

qa_highlights.answer: The Saudi acquisition (SACE, 51%) is complete. The European acquisition is in due diligence and management expects it in the next two to three quarters, with no value disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Where does the margin expansion come from: gross margin or operating leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited both: evaluating procurement from China to lift gross margin, and fixed-cost control with operating leverage visible in Q1.

544567|2026-09.headline: Infinity Infoway H1 FY27 revenue rose 106.22% to Rs 16.81 crore, with EBITDA margin at 50.68% and PAT margin at 29.89%.

qa_highlights.question: How will Rivet design-and-build differentiate and how large is the opportunity?

qa_highlights.question: What occupancy should the 14,000 Q1 FY27 desks reach?

qa_highlights.question: How will the portfolio mix change over the next six to eight quarters?

qa_highlights.question: What drove the occupancy jump, and how durable is GCC and BFSI demand?

qa_highlights.question: Will margins hold in FY27 with capacity coming in?

qa_highlights.question: What is the rent escalation exposure on renewals, and how is it passed to clients?

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR500-600 crore capex guidance being kept?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, guidance is held; any change depends on large managed-office deals, with visibility by the next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20%+ growth guidance intact on a quarterly basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reaffirmed FY27 revenue and EBITDA growth above 20%, citing about 70% YoY EBITDA growth; it expects EBITDA to rise each quarter from the Rs138 crore base.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the decline in mature and growth-cohort occupancy and the seat exits?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said mature-cohort capacity rose about 8,000 seats as a result of cohort migration. Growth-cohort occupancy fell from 73% to 65% because about 7,000 new seats opened, and mature-cohort EBITDA margin is holding at about 28%.

qa_highlights.question: How does the managed-office customization model work and could REITs compete?
qa_highlights.answer: Customization is billed upfront when clients ask for changes beyond the contract price and is now amortised over the term. Management argues clients prefer one operator across formats, and REITs typically require longer commitments.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Rivet and Member Services economics?

544570|2026-09.headline: WeWork India Q2 FY27 revenue rose 31.6% YoY to INR768.7 crore and EBITDA margin reached 21.2%, with PAT up 67.4% to INR65.8 crore.
544570|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 was a strong quarter: revenue grew 31.6% YoY and 10.1% QoQ to about INR768.7 crore, and EBITDA rose 37.6% YoY to INR162.9 crore at a 21.2% margin. The company added a record ~11,700 desks in the quarter, taking capacity to 145,300 desks across 85 centres, while occupancy rose 357 bps YoY to 83.7%. Net debt of INR310 crore a year ago turned into net cash of INR23 crore, and ROCE reached 34.5%. Management guided to 150,000-155,000 desks by March 2027, and the company is laying out a 190,000-200,000 seat path. All figures are on an IGAAP-equivalent basis.

segments.name: Value-added services (VAS)
segments.commentary: VAS revenue INR79.6 crore, up 35% YoY; management says VAS is margin accretive. Customization revenue about INR18 crore in Q2 and about INR30 crore in H1, with flow-through to EBITDA.

segments.name: Digital
segments.commentary: Digital revenue INR29.2 crore, up 46% YoY, operating at close to 80% EBITDA margin.

qa_highlights.question: How has underwriting changed for new centres (payback, revenue-to-rent) given rising competition and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is taking larger positions in Grade A assets, underwriting buildings under development, and doing multi-property deals; it says underwriting is smarter but not drastically changed versus two years ago. Payback periods are improving and capex control is driving better returns.

qa_highlights.question: Renewal trends and pricing on renewals versus new contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Renewal rate 80%-85% in H1; renewal escalations are lower than contracted escalations and pricing on fill-up, as management trades price for loyalty and scale. Around 50% of customer growth comes from existing members expanding.

qa_highlights.question: Capital allocation between expansion and FCF, and use of cash?
qa_highlights.answer: More FY28 expansion is planned with additional capex; the company is also looking at buybacks or dividends once book losses are cleared, and at investing in adjacent businesses that help Indian companies scale.

qa_highlights.question: Customization revenue in Q2 and EBITDA flow-through; GCC hiring outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Customization was about INR18 crore in Q2 and about INR30 crore in H1, with flow-through to EBITDA; management says large lumpiness is normalised. Management sees GCCs continuing to set up in India and expects demand to grow, with premium managed offices and more amenities.

qa_highlights.question: Will March 2027 desk target of 155,000 be met, and what H2 margin uplift to expect?
qa_highlights.answer: Already at about 150,000 desks; 155,000 visibility by March, though some deliveries may slip into early April. Margins to expand further in Q3 and Q4, with the larger step-up in Q4 as rent freezes expire. Q4 YoY margin change expected to be modest given a strong Q4 last year.

544572|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 sales rose 9.8% QoQ to INR 9.5 billion; reported PBT margin 9.5%, or 11.5% excluding demerger one-offs.
544572|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 (Jan–Mar 2026) revenue grew 9.8% QoQ to INR 9.5 billion, led by OEM orders from wind, metals and rail. Reported PBT margin recovered to 9.5% from negative 7.8% in Q3, but this includes demerger-related one-offs; excluding them, margin was 11.5% versus 13.1% in Q3. Net working capital fell 2.8% QoQ to 18.7% of sales on lower inventory. Management guided margins back to around 13% after demerger costs end and about 15% by FY29-30, with capex of around INR 800 crore planned through FY30 for a new Pune plant. YoY comparisons were not presented because prior-period figures were extracted from SKF India Limited.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY26 segment-wise mix across general machinery, heavy industries, metals, railway, wind, OEM, aftermarket and exports?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26: distribution about 35%, OEM about 51%, exports about 6%, SKF India sales about 4%, other income about 3%. Within OEM: railway 11%, general machinery 7%, wind and defence 7%, heavy industries 7%, metals 6%.

qa_highlights.question: How is raw material inflation trending, how much price has been taken, and how will margins evolve with capacity additions and demerger costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin to return to about 13% by end of calendar 2026; about 15% by FY29-30. Cost escalation projected at 3-4%, with FX as the bigger headwind. Pricing actions already taken with distributors; OEM price escalation being negotiated and expected to be harder.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the gap between current margins and the 13-15% historical range, and what drives the path to 16-18%?
qa_highlights.answer: Drags are extra investments in Pune including the new plant, intense OEM competition, higher railway mix, and higher depreciation. Management targets around 15% through 2030 and says 16-18% is an aspiration that cannot yet be committed.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company prioritise growth over margin, given exits and re-entries in wind, rail and tractors?
qa_highlights.answer: Strategy is growth while maintaining margin, with a target of about 15%. Re-entering wind, freight rail and tractor segments through localization means winning share at lower OEM margins, which management expects to improve through efficiency and pricing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex timeline and when will new capacity be commissioned?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex of around INR 800 crore plus over FY26 to FY30. New Pune plant expected to be operational mid-2028, with full ramp-up and channel transfers complete by end of 2028.

qa_highlights.question: What is the INR 350-400 crore channel expansion investment and how will growth be delivered until the new plant is ready?
qa_highlights.answer: The investment is plant and machinery for DGBB and TRB channels at the new Pune plant, not warehouses. Growth is guided at about 8% in the interim, supported by job-work from SKF India and sourcing from Ahmedabad and Nilai.

544572|2026-06.headline: SKF India (Industrial) Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18.3% YoY to INR 9,708 mn, but PBT margin fell to ~9% on FX losses and demerger IT costs.

PBT was INR 869 million, a margin of about 9%, hit by roughly INR 147 million of forex loss and about INR 150 million of demerger-related IT separation cost. Operating cash conversion was 63%, with a one-time outflow for name change and land transfer. Management reiterated a long-term PBT margin path of 14-16% through 2028, with a 17-19% aspiration, and a new Pune plant with INR 850-950 crore capex targeted for 2028.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the margin moderation from the 16-19% guidance to 14-16%, and how much is FX and demerger impact?

qa_highlights.question: What is the supply and recurrence profile of the INR 140 crore wind and INR 35 crore agri orders?

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin difference across distribution, OE and exports?
qa_highlights.answer: Distribution is the higher-margin channel at high double-digit margins; OE is high single-digit. OE supports aftermarket share growth.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the solutions business and what is the doubling timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Solutions are around 6-7% of India business, below 10% in aspiration. Doubling the business is an aspiration within five years at the outside, with no committed timeline.

544574|2026-06.headline: Tata Capital Q1 FY27 PAT rose 56% YoY to INR1,547 crore, with consolidated AUM up 22% YoY to INR2.91 lakh crore and credit cost at 1%.
544574|2026-06.overview: Consolidated PAT of INR1,547 crore grew 56% YoY and 3% QoQ, with ROA at 2.3% (2.5% ex-Motor Finance) and ROE at 13.7%. AUM reached INR2.91 lakh crore, up 22% YoY and 5% QoQ, or 28% YoY excluding Motor Finance. Disbursements rose 33% YoY to INR46,212 crore, while the book grew about 10% YoY on a legacy run-off drag. Management announced the acquisition of Yogloans (gold loans), with RBI approval expected by calendar year-end, and raised USD400 million of international bonds, 4x oversubscribed.

segments.name: Motor Finance
segments.commentary: Book moderated to INR24,445 crore as of June 2026 after a sequential decline; legacy net AUM run-off reduced to INR945 crore from INR3,139 crore a year earlier. Business remained profitable in Q1 FY27 despite seasonal credit cost rise.

segments.name: Unsecured Retail
segments.commentary: Unsecured retail disbursements up 50% YoY; unsecured retail AUM up 17% YoY. Management says the unsecured book will grow faster than overall book in FY27.

segments.name: Corporate and SME
segments.commentary: Retail plus SME is 85.4% of the portfolio, within the 85-88% target band; Corporate is the balance. Management says Corporate has 'maxed out' and will be syndicated down if originated above target.

Micro Housing ticket size about INR9 lakh versus INR15-16 lakh for Affordable Housing (per Q&A).

qa_highlights.question: Why does Corporate loan growth look fast and is Corporate maxed out?

qa_highlights.question: What drove the rise in PCR across segments?
qa_highlights.answer: Rakesh Bhatia said it reflects Stage-3 ageing mix, moving PCR about 30-40 bps quarter to quarter; ECL grades refreshed quarterly with no material change in TTC PD or LGD.

qa_highlights.question: Capital comfort level and need to raise capital?

qa_highlights.question: Operating expense growth of 21% YoY: what is underlying?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex growth is distorted by the appraisal-cycle change; normalised growth is about 16%. Cost-to-income guided to 33-34% by FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Cost of funds outlook and margin trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost of funds expected up about 8-10 bps for FY27 on a daily-average basis; NIMs targeted up about 10 bps for the year. Floating-rate book is about 70%, with rate changes passed through.

qa_highlights.question: Gold loan strategy and state expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Approval expected by year-end; about 500+ branches over 2.5-3 years and INR4,000-5,000 crore portfolio; target states identified but not disclosed, with some in northern India. Acquired entity to be renamed under Tata Capital once a subsidiary.

qa_highlights.question: Monsoon and El Nino impact on rural and vehicle books?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has seen no impact on the portfolio so far and sees no early signs of stress.

544574|2026-09.headline: Tata Capital Q2 FY27 consolidated AUM rose 26% YoY to INR3,08,030 crore and PAT grew 51% YoY to INR1,660 crore.
544574|2026-09.overview: Consolidated AUM crossed INR3 lakh crore, growing 26% YoY and 6% QoQ, with 32% YoY growth excluding Motor Finance. PAT rose 51% YoY to INR1,660 crore, ROA was 2.3% (2.5% ex-Motor Finance) and ROE exceeded 14%. Credit cost eased to 0.9% from 1.0% in Q1 and Stage 3 was stable at 1.9%, while NIM plus fee fell about 10 bps QoQ. Management guided to a 25 bps repo hike in October and a 20-25 bps PLR increase effective 1 November, and said it expects no further NIM plus fee drag in Q3 and a distinct improvement in Q4. Revolving credit and insurance commission regulations remain open risks, with no quantification given.

segments.name: Tata Capital Housing Finance
segments.commentary: AUM INR95,098 crore (+26% YoY, +6% QoQ), PAT INR552 crore, ROA 2.5%, ROE 18%. Affordable and micro housing AUM grew 22% YoY and 5% QoQ; 23 new locations added in the quarter.

segments.name: Retail and SME
segments.commentary: Retail and SME make up 85.4% of consolidated AUM. Supply chain has diversified, with auto now about 35% of supply chain versus about two-thirds four years ago.

segments.name: High-margin businesses
segments.commentary: Disbursements grew 40% YoY while AUM growth rose to 14% from 10% in Q1; management expects AUM growth to reach overall portfolio levels by Q4.

segments.name: Motor Finance (TMFL)
segments.commentary: Portfolio is still running down, with the Q2 rundown below Q1 and Q1 below Q4 FY26. Management expects stabilisation in Q3 and growth from Q4. Share of the book fell from 14.5% in March 2025 to about 7.7%. Gross NPA rise is attributed to seasonality and a shrinking denominator; absolute Q2 slippages were lower YoY. A macro provision of about INR30 crore was created in CV.

segments.name: Microfinance and flexi loans
segments.commentary: Microfinance is under 1% of the book, with improving asset quality and growth. Retail flexi loans are about 2-2.5% of the book. Management estimates the revolving credit impact at 3-4% of AUM if products cannot be converted.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth guided at 23-25% for FY27 and over FY25-FY28; management says it will land within this range and is not looking to revise guidance down.
Management is not revising FY28 ROA and ROE guidance and says it may revise upward at year-end; it is confident of meeting cost-to-income, credit cost and PAT growth guidance.
PLR increase of 25 bps (standalone ALCO) and 20 bps (Housing Finance) effective 1 November 2026, to protect NIM plus fee.
NIM plus fee expected stable in Q3 FY27 and improving distinctly in Q4 FY27.
Management expects about 2 further repo hikes in FY27 (market talk of around 50 bps more).
Income growth expected around 25% and cost growth around 15% for the year.
Capital raise expected in H2 FY28, more towards Q3-Q4, based on the current growth plan.
capex_capacity: Branch network at about 1,515 branches across 1,094 locations in 26 states and UTs; net addition of 24 branches in Q2.
Q3 and Q4 location expansion in affordable and micro housing planned to be stronger than Q2.
Gold loan business is not yet live; launch expected in the coming month.
On-roll employee strength 31,655, with over 80% in frontline sales and collections; headcount up 6% against AUM up 26%.
Over 180 digital partnerships; 9.2 million customers served.
demand_pricing: Management described festive demand as strong across two-wheeler, passenger vehicle and commercial vehicle segments, with dealer supply-chain demand also rising.
Rural growth is slower than urban, but Tata Capital's rural exposure is limited to microfinance; it has no tractor or agri farm loans and hardly any microfinance in Maharashtra.
Housing NIM fell about 5 bps QoQ from competitive pressure in prime home loans; the other 5 bps came from higher cost of funds.
Fee income rose 30% YoY, driven by assignment income (DA income up 58% YoY); non-assignment fee income held at Q1 level as a percentage of AUM.
Management is declining some deals that do not meet margin requirements, prioritising margins over growth.
Floating-rate liabilities are 48% of total liabilities and floating-rate assets 66% of assets.

qa_highlights.question: Path if revolving credit draft norms are adopted, and whether exposure is being cut before final norms.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has not cut exposure and is piloting alternate products, with more to start in November; it estimates the impact at 3-4% of AUM and believes more than half of flexi can be converted to modified products at similar pricing.

qa_highlights.question: Insurance distribution norms impact and alternative fee sources.
qa_highlights.answer: Management has not quantified the impact, which depends on final regulations. Options include selling retail insurance, growing NIM plus fee, and reducing costs if insurance is not sold.

qa_highlights.question: Motor Finance NPA rise and the timing of book growth.
qa_highlights.answer: The rise reflects seasonality (Q2 typically has the highest NPA growth) and a shrinking denominator; absolute slippages were lower YoY. Portfolio growth is expected to stabilise in Q3 and resume in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: NIM trajectory for H2 FY27 and FY28.
qa_highlights.answer: NIM fell about 10 bps QoQ in Q2 (about 5 bps from cost of funds and 5 bps from prime home loan competition). Management expects stability in Q3 and a distinct improvement in Q4, and says a rate increase should be neutral to accretive.

qa_highlights.question: Whether the SME growth is channel finance and whether supply-chain growth will shift to retail.
qa_highlights.answer: Growth came from both term loans and supply chain, with supply chain having a particularly strong quarter. Auto is about 35% of supply chain, down from about two-thirds four years ago.

qa_highlights.question: Capital raise timing.
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects to need capital in H2 FY28, more towards Q3-Q4, and will also consider sub-debt; it did not give a precise size.

qa_highlights.question: Why yields are not rising despite high-margin growth.
qa_highlights.answer: Balance transfer pressure eases in a rising-rate environment, and high-margin AUM growth (14%) is expected to reach overall portfolio growth by Q4. Business-level yield plans are expected to show output from end-Q3 or Q4.

Motor Finance: Q3 stabilisation and Q4 growth are not yet demonstrated; NPA trend is seasonal.

544576|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record INR80.54 bn (+8.1% YoY) but EBITDA margin fell ~250 bps YoY to 11.7%, with FY27 targeting early double-digit margins.
544576|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was LG Electronics India's highest-ever quarterly revenue at INR80.54 bn, up 8.1% YoY, with EBITDA of INR9.45 bn (11.7% margin) and PAT of INR6.93 bn (8.5%). Year-on-year margin compression was attributed to channel promotion spend (~1.1 pp), rupee depreciation (~5.6% YoY, ~1 pp impact), and e-waste compliance cost (~0.2 pp). For FY26, revenue grew 1.0% to INR246.05 bn, EBITDA was INR24.08 bn (9.8%) and PAT INR16.85 bn (6.8%). Management guided FY27 to mid-teen revenue growth and early double-digit EBITDA margins, citing April-May sell-through and recent price hikes.

guidance_outlook: FY27 AUM growth guidance of 25% (given at start of year); medium-term AUM target of about INR1.5 lakh crores by FY28 (doubling every 3 years).
FY27 profit growth guidance of about 50% YoY reiterated; management says it is confident of meeting it.
Exit Q4 FY27 Growth RoAUM target of about 2.5% reiterated, even if cost of borrowing does not fall further; management expects further opex reduction of 30-35 bps over the next 6 quarters.
Long-term RoAUM ambition above 3%; FY28 exit target now being recalibrated for the insurance commission headwind, with specific guidance to be given in Q4.
Leverage expected to rise towards 4.5x-5x in the medium term.
Overall cost of borrowing on a stock basis expected at similar or lower levels over the next 12 months despite RBI tightening.
capex_capacity: Branch network 838; no full-service urban branches added in Q2. Rural branches rose from 178 to 203.
Gold loan branches rose from 67 to 100 in Q2; target of 200 by end-March 2027.
Gold loans are a high-yield product that management is growing, partly at the expense of low-yield mortgages.
Non-dilutive regulatory capital release possible over the next 12 to 24 months; management says this plus the QIP gives runway for growth capital for some years.
Capital raise in Q2 structured to limit leverage hit; QIP added ~200 bps to CAR and 5 bps to RoAUM.
demand_pricing: Disbursements up 34% YoY in Q2, with momentum stronger than Q1.
Unsecured AUM mix at 21% (20% two quarters ago); target 25-26% over coming years. Cross-sell share of unsecured disbursements at 30%.
Mass-affluent housing loans and larger-ticket LAP showing higher growth after rating upgrade.

Incremental borrowing cost: 9.36% (H1 FY26), 8.67% (H2 FY26), 8.46% (H1 FY27). Retiring debt about 9.1% vs new borrowing about 8.4%. About INR37,500 crores of long-term borrowings mature in next 18 months (about INR29,000 crores next year per analyst).

Pricing: NBFC lending rates move with PLR; management said it will not pass on rate increases until its own cost of borrowing rises, with roughly a one-year lag and a further three-month lag to customers.
Market-linked borrowings under one-third of total; almost no repo-linked debt. Q2 raised almost nothing from capital markets, shifting mix to MCLR-linked funding.

qa_highlights.question: Which segments will pass on higher rates to customers, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Pass-through follows PLR changes, which lag cost of borrowing by about one year; management expects no pass-through yet. Around 50% of assets (HL and LAP) are the main repricing book.

qa_highlights.question: Will yields rise as the legacy book runs off?
qa_highlights.answer: Partly. Q2 had one extra day, which cut retail yield by about 11 bps; management called this optical. Growth NIM should converge towards company NIM as legacy runs off.

qa_highlights.question: Is the housing loan vintage uptick real?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, driven largely by one INR4 crore fraud case from Q2 FY26; management expects it to fall in Q3. Concentration in South India IT-sector home loans persists but has not spread.

qa_highlights.question: Gold loan exposure and risk strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Industry data shows 15-23% of gross gold disbursements went to customers 90+ days past due. Piramal's October gold disbursements to such customers are under 1%, and it will not disburse to them.

qa_highlights.question: Why is consolidated provisioning lower than Growth credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Legacy book write-backs (about INR90 crores profit from recovery) offset Growth credit cost, which is used to build other buffers.

qa_highlights.question: Path from 2% to 3% RoAUM?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex 30-35 bps further reduction over 6 quarters, funding cost reduction and mix shift to unsecured and gold; exit FY27 target 2.5%. FY28 outlook recalibrated for insurance headwind.

qa_highlights.question: How much RoAUM headwind from the insurance commission rules?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross 18-24 bps FY28 RoAUM impact if the IRDAI draft is implemented from 1 April 2027; partly offset by Pramerica Life profit share and sales-incentive rationalisation. Management says mitigating half would still be meaningful.

qa_highlights.question: Does the rising rate cycle hurt NIM?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says rate-cycle positioning is favourable: variable-rate assets INR56,000 crores exceed variable-rate liabilities INR51,000 crores; spreads down 40-45 bps; retiring debt about 60 bps above current borrowing rates.

risks_watch: IRDAI draft on insurance commissions: 18-24 bps FY28 RoAUM gross impact if effective 1 April 2027; formal feedback to regulator planned via FIDC.
RBI tightening in H2 FY27 and rising global yields may raise borrowing costs; management expects offsets from maturing debt and rating-driven spread compression.
Gold loan industry risk: high share of customers with active gold loans (above 35%) and industry disbursements to 90+ DPD customers.
Wholesale growth headwind from high prepayments (72% of disbursements repaid in Q2).
Housing loan 90+ uptick (one fraud case) and IT-sector delinquencies in South India; management expects Q3 improvement.
544597|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, profitability and funding tailwinds, with a notably cautious stance on FY28 RoAUM and the insurance commission draft, which management said it would recalibrate for once rules are final.
key_quotes: Our incremental cost of borrowing at Piramal Finance continues to decline steadily.
We don't take macro calls. We don't take decisions on everyday credit choices because of how the macro looks.
Growth is an outcome of our framework. It is not an input to our framework.
There is a INR4 crores case from Q2 of FY26, which turned out to be fraudulent, which is there in that number.
