rows.why: Gold loan branches rose from 67 to 100 in Q2 with a target of 200 by end-March 2027 and rural branches went 178 to 203, but no full-service urban branches were added in Q2 and total branches stand at 838, so capacity adds are small and incremental.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Total AUM up 24% YoY to INR1,13,112 crores with Growth AUM up 30%, disbursements up 34% YoY in Q2 and momentum stronger than Q1, and FY27 AUM growth guidance of 25% held; wholesale is a headwind with 72% of disbursements prepaid in Q2.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No capex or plant utilisation discussed; capital needs are met by the INR3,850 crores equity raise (QIP INR2,100 crores plus INR1,750 crores warrants) lifting CAR to 20.1%, with non-dilutive regulatory capital release possible over 12-24 months.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reiterated FY27 profit growth of about 50% and 25% AUM growth without raising either, and flagged RBI tightening and rising borrowing costs as offsets.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: RBI tightening in H2 FY27 and rising global yields may raise borrowing costs, and the IRDAI draft insurance commission rule could cut FY28 RoAUM by 18-24 bps if effective 1 April 2027, though management is confident on FY27 profit growth of 50%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Unsecured AUM is 21% of total (up from 20% two quarters ago) with target of 25-26% over coming years, and gold loan branches are being scaled from 100 toward 200 by March 2027; no specific new product named.

rows.label: Gold loan branch rollout to 200 by March 2027
rows.why: Gold branches rose from 67 to 100 in Q2 and the target is 200 by end-March 2027, with gold a high-yield product management is growing partly at the expense of mortgages.

rows.label: Further opex reduction 30-35 bps over 6 quarters
rows.why: Management expects another 30-35 bps of opex to AUM reduction, with cost-to-income already down to 52% from 61% in Q2 FY26 and retail opex to AUM down 5 bps QoQ to 3.48%.

rows.label: IRDAI insurance commission draft headwind
rows.why: Gross 18-24 bps FY28 RoAUM impact if the draft is implemented from 1 April 2027, partly offset by Pramerica Life profit share and sales-incentive rationalisation.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY27 profit growth of about 50%, 2.5% exit Q4 FY27 RoAUM and funding tailwinds, but cautious on FY28 RoAUM and the IRDAI insurance commission draft, which it will recalibrate for once rules are final; analysts probed gold loan 90+ DPD exposure, housing loan vintage uptick

544599|2026-03.headline: Studds Q4 FY26 revenue rose 11.9% YoY to INR 167.5 crore; FY27 guidance is 17-18% revenue growth with broadly flat EBITDA margin.
544599|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was INR 167.5 crore (up 11.9% YoY), EBITDA INR 31.3 crore (up 11% YoY, margin 18.7%) and PAT INR 21.1 crore (up 6.1% YoY, margin 12.6%). For FY26, revenue was INR 634.2 crore (up 8.6%), EBITDA INR 122.2 crore (up 16.4%, margin 19.3%) and PAT INR 82.7 crore (up 18.7%). Management took 8-9% price increases from 1 April 2026 to offset raw material inflation, but expects Q1 FY27 gross margin pressure before recovery. Management also announced Bharat Goyal's elevation to CFO effective 1 July 2026, an ESOP plan, and a dividend of INR 3 per share.

financial_highlights.metric: FY26 two-wheeler helmet and boxes volume

financial_highlights.value: INR 3 per share on INR 5 face value (60% payout)

segments.name: STUDDS (domestic mass/core brand)
segments.commentary: Volume grew from 68.7 lakh units in FY24 to 72.6 lakh units in FY26, about 3% CAGR. Management positions it as the scale and stability base.

segments.name: SMK (premium brand)
segments.commentary: Volumes grew at about 52% CAGR. SMK ASP rose from INR 2,359 in FY25 to INR 2,552 in FY26, and SMK sales grew about 30% YoY. Management says SMK EBITDA margin is about 10 points above STUDDS (STUDDS 17%, SMK 27%).

segments.name: Private label
segments.commentary: Volumes grew at about 22% CAGR. The largest white label, O'Neal, saw ASP rise from INR 1,831 to INR 1,918.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Exports were 20% of FY26 revenue versus 16.75% in FY25, and 22.79% in Q4 versus 17% in Q3. Management guides exports to grow 23-24% in FY27 and reach about 30% of revenue in 2-3 years.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at about 17-18%, with EBITDA margins at broadly similar levels to FY26.
Q1 FY27 gross margin expected under pressure from raw material costs; margins to recover in subsequent quarters as material prices ease.

Management does not expect EBITDA margin to reach 22-23% in FY27; it expects that level only after revenue crosses INR 750 crore with operating leverage, and 12 months out margins should be better than FY26.
Advertising and marketing budget for FY27 set at INR 30 crore, across domestic and export, versus about INR 23 crore in FY26.
Normalised inventory days guided at 85-90, versus 91 days currently and 68 days in the prior year.
Expected 2-3 years of 8-9% price increases; a further 2-2.5% or 3-4% increase is possible if raw material costs stay elevated.

Capacity: installed capacity rises from about 9.25 million to over 12 million units (about 33%), with the first 1.5 million units by Q2 FY27 and the second 1.5 million over the following 15-18 months.
capex_capacity: Capacity expansion of 1.5 million units targeted by Q2 FY27, with a second 1.5 million units expected over the following 15-18 months; total installed capacity to rise from about 9.25 million to over 12 million units.
Capacity utilisation FY26: two-wheeler helmets and boxes 89%, EPS 88%, water decals 57%. Q4 FY26 utilisation: helmets and boxes 89%, EPS 91%, water decals 57%.
Capacity figure assumes a 50:50 painted and unpainted mix; unpainted-heavy mix raises effective capacity.
Italy subsidiary being incorporated, with a warehouse in Reggio Emilia via a third-party 3PL. Initial stock of 10,000-15,000 units, about three months' cover, with sales expected from mid-Q2 FY27.
Additional warehouse added in Faridabad in FY26.
Riding jackets and an external Bluetooth communication system for helmets are in advanced prototype; commercial sales expected from H2 FY27.
FY26 capex INR 48 crore.
demand_pricing: Price increases averaging 8-9% across the portfolio and channels from 1 April 2026, with export price increases of about 9-10%. Management says the 8-9% offsets current material costs but not full-year costs if they stay at peak levels.
Raw material prices rose after March and have eased in the last two weeks; management says they remain about 20-25% above the pre-spike level and expects about 2-3 months to return to Nov-Dec levels.
Management reports no volume or demand pressure after the April price increase, and says dealers expected a larger increase.
Unorganised share of the Indian helmet market is estimated at 25-30% (not less than 20%), expected to fall to 10-15% over 2-3 years.
Europe: Italy is the focus market, to be served dealer-direct. Mexico: a 1,200-store retail chain signed; Mexico helmet market about 2.5 million units, with the company below 1% share.
Competition: management says unorganised players may exit under price pressure, and many brands, including Chinese OEM suppliers, have raised prices.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 12 million capacity target conservative if unpainted helmets are produced more?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said capacity is fungible. The 12 million figure assumes a 50:50 painted and unpainted mix, and capacity rises if the unpainted share increases.

qa_highlights.question: What is the raw material inflation and will 8-9% price increases offset it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 8-9% almost offsets current material prices, but not if costs stay at peak. Q1 FY27 margins will be under pressure, and recovery is expected once material prices fall.

qa_highlights.question: Can EBITDA margin reach 22% as revenue crosses INR 750 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said not in FY27 because of Q1 raw material pressure. Operating leverage is expected to lift margins above FY26 levels 12 months out.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin gap between SMK and STUDDS, and between export and domestic?
qa_highlights.answer: SMK EBITDA is about 10 points higher than STUDDS (STUDDS 17%, SMK 27%). Export and domestic margins are roughly similar, with exports mostly SMK, and a gap of about 10 points is cited.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the European subsidiary moved from Spain to Italy?
qa_highlights.answer: The Spanish distributor objected to a direct subsidiary there. Italy has no direct importer, is the largest European market, and is served by a Dutch distributor with small volumes. The warehouse will be in Reggio Emilia.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory days rise from 68 to 91?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the new Faridabad warehouse and higher US inventory with rising US sales. It says 85-90 days is the comfortable range.

risks_watch: Raw material volatility: prices spiked to about 150 (index) before easing to 120-125, and Q1 FY27 gross margin is expected to be under pressure.
Working capital: inventory days rose to 91 from 68, and management targets 85-90 days.
Start-up costs and margin drag from the Italy subsidiary and the Europe 3PL warehouse, and new export markets with their own homologation rules (Brazil, Indonesia, Sri Lanka).
Execution on the Decathlon non-motorised helmet supplies from July 2026 and on the 1.5 million unit capacity addition by Q2 FY27.
Marketing spend to rise to INR 30 crore in FY27, which could weigh on operating margins.
Leadership transition: Bharat Goyal becomes CFO from 1 July 2026.
544599|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth and the SMK and export story, but candid that Q1 FY27 margins will be pressured by raw material costs. Management was direct on the 22% margin question and on the Spain-to-Italy change, and gave some numbers only as ballparks.
key_quotes: So, export and domestic would be quite similar because most of the exports is with SMK.
I don't think 22 %-23% is what I think will happen this year.
So, I don't see any demand pressures as of now.
We have never reduced our prices.

rows.when: Q1 FY27, with recovery later in FY27
rows.why: FY27 EBITDA margin guided broadly similar to FY26's 19.3%, Q1 FY27 gross margin under raw material pressure, and management rules out 22-23% in FY27 until revenue crosses INR 750 crore (FY26 revenue INR 634.2 crore).

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q2 FY27 for first 1.5 million units; second 1.5 million over
rows.why: Installed capacity rising from about 9.25 million to over 12 million units (about 33%), with the first 1.5 million under construction and utilisation at 89% for helmets and boxes.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Revenue guided up 17-18% with 8-9% price increases from April 2026, implying volume growth of roughly 8-10%; no volume pressure reported after the price hike and 1.5 million units of capacity arrive by Q2 FY27.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is 89% for helmets and boxes and 91% for EPS in Q4 FY26, and the second 1.5 million unit tranche is planned 15-18 months out, so a further capex step is probable.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance is new at 17-18% revenue growth with flat margin, and management was candid that Q1 FY27 margins will be pressured by raw materials, which caps the upside case.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Raw material costs remain about 20-25% above pre-spike levels with a 2-3 month normalisation window, and the 8-9% price hike only offsets current costs, not full-year costs if prices stay at peak.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Riding jackets and an external Bluetooth communication system for helmets are in advanced prototype, with commercial sales expected from H2 FY27, and Decathlon non-motorised helmet supplies start July 2026.

rows.why: Exports were 20% of FY26 revenue and 22.79% in Q4 FY26; management guides 23-24% export growth in FY27.

rows.label: Inventory days normalisation
rows.why: Inventory days at 91 versus 68 a year ago, with management targeting 85-90 days, which implies some release of working capital.

tone.note: Management was confident on the SMK premium and export story and on the 1.5M unit capacity by Q2 FY27, but cautious that Q1 FY27 margins will be pressured by raw materials and that the 22% margin is out of reach in FY27; analysts pressed on margin recovery and the 12 million capacity assumption.

544599|2026-06.headline: Studds Q1 FY27 revenue rose 13.7% to INR169.7 crores, but EBITDA margin fell to 11.5% on a styrene-driven raw material spike; management guides 14-15% in Q2.
544599|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 13.7% YoY to INR169.7 crores, with two-wheeler helmet and box volume of 1.95 million units at 81% utilisation. EBITDA was INR19.6 crores (11.5% margin) and PAT INR12.3 crores (7.2% margin), hit by a sharp rise in styrene-based raw material prices (about 600 bps of margin impact) and manpower costs (about 200 bps, from a Haryana minimum wage hike). Management said effective price realisation was about 5% in Q1, with a full ~9% price increase expected from Q2 as older-price orders roll off. Growth initiatives include 1.5 million helmets of new capacity, Decathlon, an Italian subsidiary and new products.

segments.name: Domestic STUDDS (helmets)
segments.commentary: Management cited domestic EBITDA of roughly 16-17% currently, versus about 17-18% in FY26. Q1 price increases were not fully passed through in OEM, CSD/CPC and some export channels.

segments.name: SMK (premium)
segments.commentary: Export EBITDA on SMK was described as about 30-35%. SMK range is INR4,000 to INR15,000 helmets.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: About 21% of Q1 revenue; target is closer to 30%. Export orders executed in Q1 were contracted before the price rise; new orders are booked at revised prices.

segments.name: Bicycle helmets (Decathlon)
segments.commentary: Bicycle helmet ASPs are about 15-20% below motorcycle helmets. Commercial production expected from October 2026, with Decathlon working like an OEM relationship.

segments.name: Bluetooth and riding jackets (new)
segments.commentary: Management expects INR15-20 crores of revenue from these two categories in FY27. Some products are made in-house and some by contract manufacturers.

segments.name: Italian subsidiary
segments.commentary: Dealer-direct entry planned in Italy, Germany and France. Expected losses of about INR2-3 crores in FY27 and about INR2 crores in FY28; revenue guidance EUR100-125k in FY27 and about EUR1 million in FY28. Management said profits start from year 3, with 10-12% EBITDA margin cited.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin expected at 14-15%; normalised 18-20% run rate by Q4 FY27, subject to stable raw material prices.
FY27 revenue growth of mid-teens guided earlier; volume growth now expected at about 10% with 7-8% blended realisation (management said high-teens revenue growth on last call).
Full ~9% price increase (on FY26 base) expected to be reflected from Q2; Q2 realisation expected at 8-9% for OEM/CSD/CPC channels.
Styrene-based raw material cost impact expected to soften to about 300 bps in Q2 from 600 bps in Q1; management expects Q3 and Q4 to improve further.
FY28 standalone guidance: volume growth 13-14% and price realisation 3-4%, implying mid-to-high teens growth (management said this excludes the Italian subsidiary).
At current styrene levels (~INR185 weighted average), PAT margin expected at about 11.5-12%, versus about 13% earlier; management expects a return to FY26 levels by Q4 FY27.
Export mix rising toward 30% could add 200-300 bps to PAT margin, per management's rough estimate.
Total capex of INR76 crores to 30 June 2026 plus INR10 crores of vendor advances; FY27 capex budget INR58 crores (INR7.5 crores spent in Q1); FY28 plan INR31 crores.

financial_highlights.change: volume growth ~8.5% YoY (1.4 lakh units on 17.56 lakh base)

qa_highlights.question: Share of styrene-based raw materials in bill of materials?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said styrene-based direct raw material is about 36% of consumption, with about 15% more indirect (e.g., paint); analyst confirmed 36% direct.

qa_highlights.question: Italy dealer-direct model: capturing distributor margin or absorbed by costs, and steady-state margin differential?
qa_highlights.answer: Entry planned in Italy, Germany and France where there are no strong distributors; no profit in years 1-2, with profits from year 3 at a surplus EBITDA margin of about 10-12%.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of the 600 bps material and 200 bps other-expense margin hit?
qa_highlights.answer: The 200 bps is entirely manpower cost, up after Haryana minimum wage revision effective 1 April (about 35%, unskilled from INR11,000-12,000 to INR15,000-16,000); expected to soften as 9% realisation flows in, but to persist.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 9% price hike on FY26 base? Q1 vs Q2 realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, 9% on March 2026 base; Q1 realised about 5%, Q2 expected 8-9%, and next quarter about 9%, with CSD/CPC and some exports lagging.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 volume growth and realisation split?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 volume about 8.5%; full-year volume closer to 10% and blended realisation 7-8%, with management referring back to high-teens revenue growth guided on last call.

qa_highlights.question: Italy subsidiary losses and revenue for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Losses of about INR2-2.5 crores in FY27 and about INR2 crores in FY28 (corrected from earlier figures); revenue EUR100-125k in FY27 and about EUR1 million in FY28, included at consolidated level.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY28 guidance of 13-14% volume and 3-4% price on a consolidated basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Management clarified it is standalone only, excluding the Italian subsidiary, whose ASP differs; Italy revenue is incremental on top of that.

qa_highlights.question: PAT margin outlook at current styrene levels, and export mix impact?
qa_highlights.answer: At ~INR185 styrene, PAT margin about 11.5-12% versus ~13% earlier; return to FY26 levels by Q4 FY27 expected. Export mix rising to 30% could add 200-300 bps to PAT margin.

capex_capacity: First-phase addition of 1.5 million helmets annual capacity progressing as planned, expected operational from September/October 2026; existing two-wheeler helmet and box utilisation at ~81% in Q1 FY27.
Total capex of about INR76 crores incurred up to 30 June 2026, plus INR10 crores of advances committed to vendors.
FY27 capex budget INR58 crores (described as the complete FY27 budget); about INR7.5 crores spent in Q1 FY27.
FY28 capex plan INR31 crores, which includes starting a second phase of construction (figure restated on call; analyst had cited INR28 crores).

Italian operations to be fully functional in October 2026; Decathlon commercial production from October 2026; Bluetooth mesh product first commercial production expected Q3 FY27; riding jacket commercial availability around Q2 FY27.
demand_pricing: Q1 FY27 effective price realisation about 5%; full ~9% price increase on FY26 base expected to be reflected from Q2, with Q2 realisation of 8-9% in the quarter per management.
Volume growth in Q1 about 8.5% (1.4 lakh units on 17.56 lakh base); management guided FY27 volume growth closer to 10%, with blended realisation of 7-8%.

Styrene-based raw material impact about 600 bps on margin in Q1, expected to ease to about 300 bps in Q2; styrene weighted average ~INR185 currently versus ~INR225 peak and ~INR135 at start of Q4 FY26.

OEM price increases received from all customers except one, with that one expected within a week; manpower cost pass-through expected from OEMs. Management said GT channel price increase was fully passed through without resistance.

Exports about 21% of Q1 revenue, with export orders from before the price rise executed at old prices; new export orders booked at revised prices. Export SMK EBITDA about 30-35%; domestic EBITDA about 16-17% currently vs 17-18% in FY26.
Bicycle helmet (Decathlon) ASPs about 15-20% below motorcycle helmets; Bluetooth and riding jacket revenue expected at INR15-20 crores in FY27.
risks_watch: Styrene price path: management says Q2 already softening and expects Q3-Q4 better, but prices moved from ~INR135 to ~INR225 peak and are at ~INR185; Gulf supply disruption (Hormuz) is the cited driver.
Realisation lag: Q1 realised only ~5% vs ~9% target; CSD/CPC and some export channels slower to pass through; one OEM price hike still pending.
Q2 margin guidance of 14-15% and Q4 return to 18-20% depend on raw material stability; margin recovery timing could slip.
Italy and Decathlon execution: Italy start-up losses, Decathlon commercial production from October 2026, and new-product launches (Bluetooth mesh Q3 FY27, jackets Q2 FY27) all need to hit timelines.

Guidance clarity: FY28 volume/price guidance is standalone; analyst reconciliation of consolidated numbers was not fully resolved on the call, with some figures corrected during Q&A (e.g., Italy losses, EUR1 million vs INR figures).
key_quotes: The important part is what we are doing today. What is important for us is that we have not been sitting back and waiting for the commodity cycle to normalize.
So, we don't expect big losses after that.
Once our Italy operations become fully functional in October 2026, we will be much closer to the customer.
So rather than asking a distributor to forecast demand several months in advance, we can increasingly move towards a more responsive and just-in-time supply model.
544599|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on medium-term recovery and capacity, but cautious on near-term margins, with management repeatedly stressing dependence on raw material prices. Several Q&A figures were corrected on the call (Italy losses, FY28 cost, EUR revenue), which lowers confidence in the precision of the numbers.

rows.why: Q1 EBITDA margin 11.5% with ~600 bps styrene hit easing to ~300 bps in Q2 and full ~9% price increase from Q2 (Q1 realisation only ~5%); management guides 14-15% in Q2 and 18-20% run rate by Q4 FY27, subject to raw material stability.

rows.why: First-phase 1.5 million helmets annual capacity is under construction and progressing as planned for operation from September/October 2026, against existing utilisation of 81%.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade

rows.why: Management expects INR15-20 crores of revenue from Bluetooth and riding jacket categories in FY27, with jackets available around Q2 FY27, Bluetooth mesh first commercial production in Q3 FY27, and Decathlon commercial production from October 2026.

544599|2026-09.headline: Studds Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 18.6% YoY to INR 183.1 crore, but EBITDA fell 23.7% to INR 22.8 crore on raw material inflation.

PAT fell about 28% to INR 14.7 crore (8.1% margin). Management attributed the margin squeeze mainly to styrene-based raw material inflation plus wage increases from April, with a cumulative net price increase of about 9% now in the system. Capacity was expanded with a new plant commencing commercial production on 30 October 2026, and export growth remained strong at about 50% in H1.

segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 volume of 2.04 million units; H1 FY27 volume of 3.99 million units. Management said Q2 volumes were flat, with Q2 domestic volume about 3.5 million and export about 0.4 million units in H1 per the call (figures were disputed/clarified as H1).

segments.name: SMK brand (premium)
segments.commentary: SMK share of sales rose to about 20% in Q2 FY27 from about 13% in Q2 FY26. Management said SMK gross margins are about 70% to 80% higher than Studds, though both brands' margins are currently down on raw material costs.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export revenue was INR 79.4 crore in H1 FY27, up nearly 50% YoY; US is about 10% of business. Growth reported across US, Europe and rest of world; long-term export growth guided at about 20-25%, short-term 30-35%.

segments.name: Accessories (riding jackets, Bluetooth, luggage, locks, gloves, goggles, rainwear)
segments.commentary: Riding jackets under SMK commenced production in September 2026 (target 10,000 units by March 2027, 40,000 units next fiscal), with first-year revenue target of INR 15-20 crore. Bluetooth communication system launch planned November 2026 with capacity above 2 lakh units a year.

segments.name: Water decals / EPS
segments.commentary: Capacity utilisation of 64% for water decals and 88% for EPS in Q2 FY27 per the call.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth guidance of 8% to 10% reiterated; management expects Q4 to be the strongest quarter given new plant ramp-up, with November and December volumes lower as ramp-up continues.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue potential do the new products have, and will they be sold domestically or exported?
qa_highlights.answer: First-year revenue target for jackets is INR 15-20 crore based on 40,000 units. Bluetooth will sell in both domestic and export markets; apparel is focused on India for now. Margins for new products are expected in line with helmets.

qa_highlights.question: Is SMK margin higher than Studds, and by how much?

qa_highlights.question: Why has export growth not translated into sharp margin improvement?

qa_highlights.question: What is the price hike taken and is more needed?

qa_highlights.question: Why were Q2 volumes flat and what is the outlook?

qa_highlights.question: Is there an inorganic growth plan?

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable export growth rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Short-term guidance of 30-35% (slightly ahead currently); medium-term about 30%; long-term about 20-25% over around 5 years. 50% growth is not sustainable over the long term.

qa_highlights.question: What are the biggest execution risks in export markets?

544600|2026-03.headline: Lenskart Q4 FY26 revenue rose 41% YoY to ₹2,516 crore, with reported EBITDA up 61% and pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin at 12.8%.
544600|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the strongest quarter since listing: revenue grew 41% YoY to ₹2,516 crore, PAT reached ₹204 crore, and EBITDA margin expanded 2.7 pp to 21.3%. India and international both grew, with India same-store sales growth at 24% and international revenue up 35.4%. FY26 crossed ₹1,700 crore EBITDA, ₹1,000 crore pre-Ind AS EBITDA and ₹500 crore PAT for the first time. Management kept the steady-state pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin at about 25% and guided FY27 net store additions to roughly FY26 levels (542 in India plus 61 international in FY26).

financial_highlights.change: Q4 from 8.1% YoY; FY26 from 3.6% in FY25

financial_highlights.metric: Net cash (ex IPO-related payables, largely settled in April)
Return on capital employed (ex undeployed IPO proceeds)

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹1,475 crore (+44% YoY) with eyewear units up 24.3% to 7.9 million; product margin held at 64%. Store count 2,609 after 170 net adds in Q4 and 542 in FY26; FY26 pre-Ind AS EBITDA ₹753 crore at 14.3% margin.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹1,054 crore (+35.4% YoY; +25% constant currency) with eyewear units up 29%. Store count 718 after 13 net adds in Q4 and 61 in FY26; FY26 pre-Ind AS EBITDA ₹264 crore at 7% margin. Japan was the strongest market; Middle East had a temporary traffic dip that has recovered to near normal.

guidance_outlook: Net new store additions in FY27 expected to be around FY26 levels (FY26: 542 India, 61 international).
Long-term steady-state pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin unchanged at approximately 25% (India currently 14-15%, about 10 pp runway).
Quarterly margins will vary with store-opening phasing, seasonality and long-term bets; management said it will prioritise long-term value over short-term linearity.
Management urged investors to track trailing 12-month volume growth as the cleanest measure of underlying demand.
Step-up in R&D spend in FY27 for automated eye testing, smart eyewear (B by Lenskart) and AI; FY27 priorities include scaling to 100 million customers.

Hyderabad plant and Thailand JV cited as structural answers to reduce import dependence.
Remote optometry stores rose 3.7x in a year to 623.
India eyewear units reached 29 million in FY26 (18 million two years earlier); long-term store runway of 4,500 stores in India previously articulated, management said more is possible.
demand_pricing: India same-store sales growth 24% in Q4 (broad-based across Metro, Tier 1, Tier 2); same-pincode sales growth 31%. Management declined to split SSSG into value and volume; it rejected an analyst's estimate of ~10% volume SSS as too low.
Eye tests: 6.8 million globally in Q4 (+45% YoY); India eye tests 6 million (+50%); about half of India eye tests were first-time exams. Gold active members 8.8 million (+29.5%).
Product margin in India held at 64% despite rupee depreciation; management said structural margin gains were offset by currency (RMB 11 to 14 cited as an example).
ASP fluctuations are driven by OPP campaigns (New Lens Replacement, Hustlr) and by upgrades to Own days, Meller, progressives.
International ACP reduction ongoing as markets are integrated into central supply chain; operating leverage seen after scale in Singapore, Dubai and now Japan.
Meller sunglasses out of stock in all markets; launched in 1,000+ India stores, Middle East and Southeast Asia, with Japan next.

qa_highlights.question: What geopolitical, raw material, China-sourcing or market risks should investors monitor?
qa_highlights.answer: Freight and raw material have had no meaningful impact so far; currency is the biggest variable. 42% of business is international and vertical integration has offset rupee-import headwinds. No material demand impact seen in India or abroad; Middle East dip was small and brief.

qa_highlights.question: How was the India gross margin held near 64% in a low-ASP quarter, and does SSSG of ~25% with ~15% price imply ~10% volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin gains came from vertical integration and process changes, not price increases; OPP campaigns are paired with upgrades to offset margin. Management said the 10% volume estimate was not correct and that volume SSS is meaningfully higher; it does not disclose value/volume split.

qa_highlights.question: How will employee productivity and cost leverage trend, especially internationally?
qa_highlights.answer: Operating leverage came mainly from SSG and volume growth on a fixed cost base. HQ and tech costs were flat as headcount was not added; AI and remote optometry are expected to add more output per person.

qa_highlights.question: Does Tier 2 strength expand the 4,500-store runway and allow faster expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said more than 4,500 stores are possible; 200+ Tier 2 stores have been added and feed GeoIQ. Metros are also growing (eye tests +45%+) and are the main source of SSG.

qa_highlights.question: How should we think about competition in smart glasses (e.g. Google re-entry)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the category is very early with no clear form-factor winner; it sees Lenskart's role in prescription and distribution of smart glasses and its app/data layer as advantages. Launch focus is on learning, not near-term sales.

qa_highlights.question: How will international margins converge to India's level, and what is the KSA breakeven status?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a quarter for reaching 15% international margin; it cited falling ACP and operating leverage after scale. KSA is about two years old and ahead of where UAE was at the same stage; no breakeven date was given.

qa_highlights.question: Will store expansion focus on saturating existing pincodes or entering new ones, and what about cannibalisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Site selection is bottom-up using mobility data within a 10-minute travel radius, not pincode-level. Management said stores tripled in many cities while revenue doubled, and that much of SSG came from multi-store pincodes.

qa_highlights.question: Is same-day delivery a near-term target and does the store network become an inventory model?
qa_highlights.answer: No delivery target set; same-day is in experiments in Singapore and some Indian markets. Stores are being used as micro-fulfilment nodes for OTC products and at-home frame trials, which management described as a chemist model rather than a warehouse.

qa_highlights.question: What is Meller's traction and scale target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Meller is ahead of plan, sold out across markets, and is being positioned as a Gentle Monster-type brand for Gen Z. No specific scale target was given.

544600|2026-06.headline: Lenskart Q1 FY27 revenue grew 34% YoY and PAT rose 182% to ₹228 crore, with India same-store sales growth at 18.3%.
544600|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue up 34% YoY and PAT up 182% to ₹228 crore, against full-year FY26 PAT of about ₹530 crore. India revenue grew 30.7% to ₹1,531 crore with pre-Ind AS 116 EBITDA margin of 15.4%, while International revenue grew 38% to ₹1,203 crore with pre-Ind AS 116 EBITDA margin of 10.6%. Store network expansion was the fastest in company history at 455 net new stores over nine months, and the company framed its growth around densification and entry into unserved pin codes. Figures are on a proforma basis, which matched reported figures for the quarter.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹1,531 crore (+30.7%); product margin 64.2%; marketing 4.8% of revenue (from 5.7%); SSSG 18.3%, same pin code sales growth 24%; eye tests 63 lakh (+42.7%); eyewear units 82 lakh (+22.8%); 116 net new stores and 50 new cities added.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹1,203 crore (+38%); product margin 77.1%; eyewear units +37.6%, transacting customers +27.8%, eye tests +20.5%, sunglasses units +58.4%; only 16 net new stores added in the quarter.

Management said it expects Y-o-Y margin improvement in International through FY27 but declined to guide the full-year margin against Q1, which benefits from seasonal sunglasses sales.
Management said short-term currency headwinds could persist if the currency weakens further; product margin offset is expected to improve with Hyderabad plant and insourcing.

Manufacturing of branded lenses (Rodenstock, Tokai) in India, with plans to extend to international markets.

qa_highlights.question: Will store expansion from ~2,700 to ~10,000 stores hurt same-store sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said densification has not diluted SSSG; penetration is about 35%, and the company is adding new price bands below ₹1,000 and above ₹10,000. It said eye test volume is the funnel driver and that supply-side engineering is the constraint.

qa_highlights.question: Is gross margin resilience a sign that currency concerns are less elevated?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said a large part of revenue is non-INR, giving a natural hedge; product margin was protected by in-house frame manufacturing, vendor volume discounts and mix, but short-term headwinds could persist if the currency weakens.

qa_highlights.question: What is the biggest long-term constraint to the vision: product, real estate or talent?
qa_highlights.answer: Peyush Bansal said talent, especially engineering talent able to apply data and AI, is the main constraint as the company scales.

qa_highlights.question: Why did SSSG, SPSG and NPS moderate, and has NPS recovered?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the NPS dip to confusion over social media communication about policies, said it has been clarified and NPS is back near earlier levels, and said SSSG rose from 16% a year ago to 18%.

qa_highlights.question: What share of eye test customers buy glasses and how many bring outside prescriptions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a significant majority of eye test customers buy glasses, immediately or within months; first-time customers convert slower. It did not give a percentage for outside prescriptions.

qa_highlights.question: Is the International Q1 margin a fair guide for full-year FY27?

544602|2026-06.headline: Allcargo Global Q1 FY27 revenue rose 5.8% YoY to INR3,522 crores; EBITDA turned positive at INR33 crores versus a INR31 crore loss a year ago.
544602|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue was INR3,522 crores, up 5.8% YoY and 20.8% QoQ, with gross profit of INR733 crores (up 2.5% YoY, 6.5% QoQ). EBITDA was INR33 crores against a loss of INR31 crores in Q1 FY26 and INR17 crores in Q4 FY26. Losses narrowed at EBIT (loss of INR18 crores) and PAT (loss of INR28 crores), and standalone borrowings fell to INR272 crores from INR314 crores at March 31, 2026. Management attributed the volume recovery to sequential trade-lane improvement after inventory corrections, while the Middle East conflict continued to weigh on FCL volumes.

segments.commentary: Volumes up about 1% QoQ and down double digits YoY, weighed by Middle East exposure. FCL market share is under 1%.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the post-COVID 21 to 24 month period was exceptional for FCL margins, and excluding it yield has improved continuously; volumes, not yields, have been the drag. It described the business as shadowing trade conditions rather than cycling.

qa_highlights.question: Why are volumes declining when global trade is broadly flat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said LCL has declined more than the industry on a YoY basis, while FCL decline is higher for Allcargo due to Middle East exposure. No alternative to LCL exists except air for small shipments averaging 3 to 4 cubic metres.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost base and is it flat in USD?

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt composition and net debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt is mainly working capital plus acquisition funding. Consolidated gross debt about INR942 crores and net debt about INR570 crores at June quarter-end.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA and ROCE normalisation path is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: No EBITDA margin guidance, since margins are not a relevant metric in this business. Management said ROCE was historically above 20% and should return there broadly; a 12% to 15% volume increase from current levels is the ballpark needed.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company pursue acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Near term, no; management said the strategy is to grow by investing in people rather than buying businesses, as all key markets and products are already covered.

544603|2026-09.headline: Groww's Q2 FY27 call centred on Cost to Serve rising on AI compute, one-time INR10-13 crore hit, and MTF book adding ~INR600-700 crore a quarter.
544603|2026-09.overview: Management explained that Cost to Serve rose in Q2 due to AI-related costs, higher compute on more trading days, and a one-time INR10-13 crore hit from delayed files on an expiry day. Cost to Grow fell because the IPL branding spend in Q1 did not recur. segments.commentary: Top four Q-commerce companies use the gateway; one of the largest consumer billers signed up, going live in Q3.

Capex described as normalising; management expects steady state across the two years after adjusting for these items.

qa_highlights.question: Why is EBITDA margin tracking below last year and will guidance be revised?

qa_highlights.question: Why did capex and indirect costs rise in H1?

544608|2026-03.headline: Emmvee FY26 revenue rose 116% to INR 5,049 crore and PAT 193% to INR 1,082 crore, with 9.4 GW order book and 6 GW expansion underway.
544608|2026-03.overview: FY26 was the first year as a listed company (IPO Nov 2025, INR 2,900 crore raised), with revenue of INR 5,049 crore, EBITDA of INR 1,734 crore (34% margin) and PAT of INR 1,082 crore (21% margin). Module capacity reached 10.3 GW after two 2.5 GW lines were commissioned (May and Dec 2025), and cell utilisation rose to 69.9% for the year and 79% in Q4. Working capital absorbed cash as inventory built up, while the 6 GW integrated cell and module project at Devanahalli is progressing with IREDA's INR 3,306 crore loan sanctioned. Management stated that FY27 will be a year of execution.

segments.name: Modules
segments.commentary: Installed capacity 10.3 GW at March 31, 2026, 100% TOPCon; module utilisation 43% for FY26, affected by Units 5 and 6 running only part-year. Q4 module production about 953 MW per management in Q&A, and G12R modules now in production.

segments.name: Cells
segments.commentary: Installed capacity 2.94 GW; utilisation 69.9% in FY26 (43.3% in FY25), 79% in Q4 and about 85% in March 2026. Management expects a transition from M10 to G12R cells by end of the current quarter.

guidance_outlook: 6 GW integrated cell and module facility at Devanahalli: module line commissioning expected by end of calendar 2026, cell line by end of FY27.
Post-expansion installed capacity targeted at 16.3 GW modules and 8.9 GW cells by end of FY27.
Ingot and wafer facility of about 9 GW in phases: Phase 1 5 GW, Phase 2 4 GW a year later; first facility planned in FY29. Capex guided at INR 600-700 crore per GW.
Next-quarter DCR mix guided at 30-35% of module sales; by around the beginning of FY28 management expects nearly all sold capacity to be DCR.
Current EBITDA spreads on new orders said to be similar to FY26 levels.
IREDA term loan of INR 3,306 crore at 7.95%; about 75-80% expected to be drawn by March 2027, with 15-20% retention spilling into FY28.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex in cash flow about INR 650 crore; gross block rise of about INR 1,000 crore (adjusted for grant) mainly for Units 5 and 6 modules. Land acquisition of about INR 311 crore for the expansion was expensed this year per the Q&A.
Module line commissioning: 2.5 GW in May 2025 and 2.5 GW in Dec 2025 at Sulibele, Bengaluru.
Land at Devanahalli fully paid and in possession; construction started and module line order finalised.
Management cited that module lines typically reach 65-70% utilisation versus 90-95% for cells, which is why module capacity is sized above cell capacity.
Cell capacity at 2.94 GW already built for G12 and line can switch from M10 to G12R through a kit change.
demand_pricing: DCR module price about INR 21-22/W; non-DCR module about INR 14-15/W. Management says DCR pricing is resilient and has not seen upward pressure despite limited domestic cell capacity.
Customer mix cited: IPPs about 40%, C&I about 30% (from prior analyst framing; not contradicted). Average top-10 customer order size rose to 221 MW from 121 MW.

Demand drivers cited: PM-KUSUM (KUSUM-C) and PM Surya Ghar for DCR; ALMM List-2 for cells expected to phase in, with utility projects bid after August 2025 covered; ALMM for IPP demand expected around FY28 or late 2027.
Exports: zero in FY26 and no export orders in the book; management treats exports as upside.
A customer advance of about INR 320 crore received in FY25 was adjusted this year, lowering the customer advance balance. A 4.5 GW cell order has been advanced in full and supply has started.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital: why did inventory build up, and will it reverse?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the build reflects the ramp-up in Q4 (revenue about INR 1,700 crore, versus about INR 1,000 crore in Q1); CFO said FY26 finished-goods change was INR 636 crore and inventory should be held near current levels, with some reduction possible.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the production-to-revenue gap large (revenue +67% QoQ vs production +30%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said sales differ from production, realisations move with raw-material prices, and EBITDA per watt is the better measure; it does not disclose sales MW.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the 6 GW cell plan 9 GW versus module 7 GW in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said modules run at 65-70% utilisation versus 90-95% for cells, so module capacity is sized higher to match cell output; module is made to order, cell is batch made-to-stock.

qa_highlights.question: What are the timelines and quantum for the wafer/ingot plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Ingot-wafer of about 9 GW in phases, first facility in FY29, capex about INR 600-700 crore per GW.

qa_highlights.question: IREDA loan rate and drawdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Rate 7.95%; nothing drawn yet, first drawdown expected within about a month; 75-80% expected drawn by March 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of a possible ALMM delay to July?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a one-to-two-month shift would not change plans; it sees no change in DCR/non-DCR mix from a few-month delay.

risks_watch: Working capital: inventory and receivables rose; operating cash after working-capital change fell to about INR 200 crore from about INR 625 crore, per analyst calculation.
Module utilisation at 43% for FY26; Q4 module output and the ramp of Units 5 and 6 need to be tracked.
Capex of about INR 4,500-4,800 crore for the 6 GW project plus INR 600-700 crore per GW for ingot-wafer; funding mix (debt/equity) not finalised.
ALMM timing: developers have petitioned for an earlier July deadline; utility bids after August 2025 are covered.
Cell transition from M10 to G12R, targeted by end of the current quarter; ramp risk on cell utilisation.
April cell production on the DCR portal looked lower; management said the portal updates monthly and that production continues normally.
Inter-company eliminations rose sharply in Q4 between the parent and the Emmvee Energy subsidiary; the accounting is not fully detailed.
544608|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on growth, execution and balance sheet, but guarded on pricing and cash flow. Management was direct on capacity and loan terms, but deflected on exact DCR mix (giving a 30-35% range) and on sales volumes, which it does not disclose.
key_quotes: FY26 was a milestone year; FY27 will be the year of execution.
Growth must, therefore, be measured against returns, leverage, execution timelines and customer visibility.
So, we don't have any Mono PERC capacity; all our capacity is TOPCon and latest.
exports are treated as an upside for us rather than the core part of our business in the current scenarios.

544608|2026-06.headline: Emmvee Q1 FY27 revenue rose 51% YoY to INR 1,555 crore, EBITDA margin 35%, PAT INR 380 crore (+103% YoY); order book 9.9 GW.
544608|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was INR 1,555 crore (+51% YoY, down QoQ), with EBITDA of INR 548.1 crore (+56% YoY, -4% QoQ) and EBITDA margin of 35% versus 33% in Q4 FY26. PAT was INR 380.3 crore, helped by finance costs falling to INR 11.1 crore from INR 53.1 crore a year earlier. Module and cell production both hit record quarterly levels, with cell utilisation up to 83%, and order book rose to 9.9 GW after 1,484 MW of inflows. Management reiterated stable EBITDA per watt (module about INR 2.5/W, cell INR 6.0-6.5/W) and a 6 GW TOPCon cell and module expansion on schedule.

segments.commentary: Production 454 MW (vs 360 MW in Q1 FY26, +26% YoY; 428 MW in Q4 FY26). Cell utilisation 83% (vs 68% in Q1 FY26, 79% in Q4 FY26). Merchant cell sales rose sharply QoQ, described as the highest in company history; cell EBITDA about INR 6-6.5/W.

guidance_outlook: Targeting approximately INR 2,400 crore of EBITDA by close of FY27.

6 GW integrated TOPCon cell and module expansion: module line commissioning by December 2026, cell line by March 2027; total project cost about INR 5,500 crore (hard costs about INR 4,600 crore), debt of about INR 3,300 crore tied up at under 8%, about 60% of hard-cost orders placed.
Post-expansion capacity to reach about 16.3 GW modules and 8.9 GW cells by end FY27.

EBITDA per watt expected to stay stable; non-DCR module mix expected to be higher than DCR over next few quarters.
capex_capacity: Current installed capacity: 10.3 GW modules and 2.94 GW TOPCon cells.
Management expects about 7+ GW of orders to be executed over the next 18 months.
Cell peak utilisation seen at about 85-90% and already close to that; module peak utilisation about 65%.
Transition of cell capacity to G12R under way, partially converted; effective cell capacity to rise even if utilisation % is similar.
Module utilisation in base case expected at similar levels (about 45%) in coming quarters.
demand_pricing: Order inflow Q1 FY27 of 1,484 MW; order book 9.9 GW vs 9.4 GW at end FY26; DCR share of order book rising but non-DCR still significant.
Realisation for non-DCR module about 15-16 cents/W in Q4; a small increase of about INR 1/W in DCR realisation this quarter per management.
Sales are priced in USD across rooftop, KUSUM and C&I segments per management, which partly offsets input-cost moves.
C&I order inflows started after 1 June; supply to be expected later in FY27. DCR demand expected to strengthen progressively during FY27 with ALMM List 2 (effective June 2026).

Management said silver paste imports are subject to DGFT pre-approval; approvals received in 3-4 days so far, with about three months of inventory applied for, and no pricing premium versus earlier levels.

qa_highlights.question: EBITDA per watt trend for DCR and non-DCR modules?
qa_highlights.answer: Both DCR and non-DCR EBITDA spreads were in line with Q4 FY26 and are expected to remain stable.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin per watt trend and DCR mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided on EBITDA per watt: about INR 2.5/W for modules and INR 6.0-6.5/W for cells, similar to Q4. DCR share of sales was over 50%, including both modules and cells; future mix to be more non-DCR but DCR inventories will be used.

qa_highlights.question: Why did raw material cost fall 18-19% QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a healthier DCR mix and higher internal cell consumption plus merchant cell sales; said this is mix-dependent and not guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Inventory position at quarter end?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 74.25 crore added to finished goods; management expects the strong order book to liquidate inventory, and raw material stock was deliberately raised due to geopolitical risk.

qa_highlights.question: Is the DCR module shortage in Karnataka real and what about run-rate increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Emmvee is equipped for phased ALMM rollout and ALMM List 3 discussions have begun; it expects cell production run-rate to rise further in coming quarters before new capacity arrives.

qa_highlights.question: Can EBITDA per watt benefit from backward integration and utilisation gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the benefit is visible in absolute EBITDA and mix, not in blended per-watt numbers, because of efficiency gains that offset raw material headwinds.

Silver import licensing via DGFT and commodity-linked input price moves; management says pass-through is handled through value engineering and USD-linked selling prices.

544608|2026-09.headline: H1 FY27 revenue rose 45% YoY to INR3,132 crores and PAT 79% to INR762 crores, with EBITDA margin near 35%.

Finance cost fell to about INR9.5 crores from INR55.2 crores a year earlier after IPO-funded debt repayment. Cell output reached 513 MW at 89% effective utilisation, while module output was 952 MW at about 44% utilisation. Order book stood at about 10.4 GW after record inflows of about 1.5 GW in the quarter, and the 6 GW integrated cell and module expansion remains on schedule (module by December 2026, cell by March 2027).

544609|2026-09.headline: Physicswallah Q2 FY27 revenue rose 18% YoY to INR1,242 crores, a record, with Pre-Ind AS EBITDA of INR233 crores at an 18.8% margin.
544609|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 was the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue at INR1,242 crores (+18% YoY), with online up 26% to INR694 crores and offline up 9% to INR541 crores. Pre-Ind AS EBITDA rose 45% to INR233 crores (18.8% margin, +350 bps), and PAT was INR142 crores versus INR70 crores a year earlier, taking H1 PAT to INR55 crores from a loss. NEET demand, delayed by a month, recovered only partly in Q2, and government-exam enrollments fell 24%, which weighed on offline and subsidiary Xylem. Management kept full-year consolidated revenue guidance of around 30% and said M&A is included in that figure. The company also sold its FinZ loan book and acquired an 11% stake in Sarrthi IAS.

vs INR70 crores in Q2 FY26
vs INR57-59 crores loss in H1 FY26

segments.name: Online

segments.name: Offline
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR541 crores (+9%); H1 collections growth around 11%. Vidyapeeth contributed 66% of H1 offline revenue, with 167 centres against 117 a year ago. Utkarsh Classes was hit by government-exam notification delays.

segments.name: Xylem (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: About 80% of its business depends on NEET, so it was hit hardest by the delayed NEET cycle. Management is working on diversifying its categories.

segments.commentary: Contributed 73.8% of H1 enrollments, up from 64.8%. K-12 collections grew about 49%. Skills and Earners grew 10x. Finance (CA, CS, ACCA, CFA) grew about 30%. Boards and CUET enrollments rose 130%.

segments.name: FinZ (NBFC)
segments.commentary: Sold its entire INR96 crore loan book to Auxilo Finserve on 3 Oct 2026. Student lending moves to third-party NBFCs; FinZ will close subject to RBI approval.

Group Pre-Ind AS EBITDA growth of about 100% targeted for FY27, mostly from online.

M&A contribution to FY27 guidance is expected to be less than 5%; about USD20 million is earmarked for online acquisitions out of the INR1,800 crore IPO proceeds to be deployed over two years.
capex_capacity: Offline centre expansion slowed; plan is about 25-30 Vidyapeeth centres opened per year over the next two to three years, plus government-exam offline centres. Last year about 50 Vidyapeeth centres were opened.

PW Digital University (PWDU) notified in the Punjab Government Gazette effective 29 Oct 2026; admissions expected from July 2027, and a business plan will be shared in the next 3-6 months. Management described it as capital-light.
Sarrthi IAS: acquired 11% for INR71 crores, consummated in Q2; the company says it is now the largest civil services educator in India.

demand_pricing: NEET online collections rose 27% and enrollments over 30% in Q2, but full-cycle online NEET collections are still 7% below last year and enrollments 13% lower. Offline NEET enrollments for the academic year are 8% lower.

Q2 unique enrollments rose 12.9% to 1.5 million; ACPU up 9.2% to INR4,280. Infinity Pro collections rose 32%, lifting share to 35% from 31%.
Offline ARPU growth of about 5-7%, which management attributed to mix shift toward new centres; Vidyapeeth ARPU is 9-10% higher YoY.

NEET is only about 15% of online revenue. Skills enrollments rose 10.3x to 1.69 lakh; CA enrollments rose 19%; NEET PG enrollments rose 35% to 9,500.

qa_highlights.question: Given NEET's partial recovery, how much must collection growth accelerate for the 30% full-year guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 NEET collections and enrollments improved significantly, with some collections spilling into Q3. It relies on mega crash courses, Earners, PW Talk/Books/Pi (INR3-4 million uplift) and newer categories such as CA and CLAT. It stated it is confident of the annual guidance but could not quantify how much of the NEET gap would be covered.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a chance online growth ends above 30% given the H2 crash courses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was too early to say and did not want to guide above 30%. Internal online targets have been exceeded, and K-12 is beating its annual operating plan. The 360-degree tracker product is being extended from JEE to NEET.

qa_highlights.question: Will online EBITDA margins (about 35%) be reinvested in marketing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there are no plans to shift margins into marketing. Online margins may rise in the next two to three years, but spending is currently going into AI tutor development.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any change to consolidated revenue guidance despite the offline shortfall? Is M&A included?
qa_highlights.answer: No change. Online is compensating for offline, and the majority of the offline hit came from NEET and government exams. The guidance includes M&A; the company is in advanced talks on a couple of online assets, and M&A is expected to contribute under 5%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the unit economics and pricing for AI Tuto?
qa_highlights.answer: Price discovery has not happened yet. The indicative price is about 2x online ACPU. Cost is below INR20 per hour of tutoring, and paid monetisation this year will be minimal. The first launch targets grades 6-12 and JEE/NEET.

qa_highlights.question: Will offline break even this year given H1 EBITDA loss of about INR108 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 and Q3 are the strongest offline quarters. H2 expansion costs are much lower because Vidyapeeth openings were slowed. Vidyapeeth is expected to break even or be profitable this year, and subsidiary cost cuts are underway.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee and faculty counts fall sequentially?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to AI efficiencies in content, QC, test-paper making and subjective-answer evaluation. Employee count is about 19,100 and faculty about 7,100.

risks_watch: NEET remains structurally behind: online NEET collections are 7% below last year on a full-cycle basis, and offline NEET enrollments are 8% lower.
Xylem's 80% NEET dependence and Utkarsh's exposure to government-exam notifications both weigh on offline; the timing of the government-exam notifications is outside management's control.
The 30% FY27 revenue guidance depends on H2 collections, crash-course results and M&A (guided at under 5% contribution); the deals are not yet announced.

544610|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 34% to INR 143 crore with 82.5% recurring; FY27 target INR 210 crore, with INR 190 crore visibility cited.
544610|2026-03.overview: Workmates reported FY26 revenue of INR 143 crore (up 34%) and PAT of INR 15.92 crore (up 16%, margin 11.1% vs 13%). Margins compressed: gross margin 32.8% vs 33.9% and EBITDA margin 16.2% vs 17.7%, which management attributes to a Dubai contract exit (about INR 4 crore), a gaming client exit (INR 3.5 crore) and about INR 6 crore of added headcount cost. Management set an FY27 revenue target of INR 210 crore (45%+ growth) and entered FY27 with MRR of INR 13.5 crore per month. This was the company's first earnings call since its BSE SME listing.

financial_highlights.value: INR 218 crore as stated on call (inconsistent with 82.5% recurring share of INR 143 crore revenue)

segments.commentary: Management said 82.5% of FY26 revenue was recurring; contracted recurring base of about INR 40 crore per quarter (about INR 160 crore annualised) for FY27.

segments.commentary: AI services revenue was about INR 2 crore of the INR 143 crore in FY26; AI plus cybersecurity targeted at about 5% of FY27 revenue. Management says AI influences much larger cloud and managed services revenue.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target INR 210 crore (45%+ growth); contracted/visible base INR 190.56 crore, leaving about INR 19-20 crore of new business to win over ~10 months.
H1 FY27 outlook about INR 91.56 crore (about INR 79-80 crore contracted, INR 6.15 crore recurring new, INR 5.82 crore project implementation); H2 estimate about INR 99 crore.
FY27 PAT guided at about INR 24-25 crore on INR 210 crore revenue; management said PAT margin would be similar to or higher than FY26 margin.
Margin recovery levers: higher AI and security mix, billable utilisation from 84% toward 88%, and operating leverage as new hires reach full productivity.
FY27 target excludes any US or UK turnover. AI expected to be a meaningful contributor in FY27 and the primary growth engine from FY28.
capex_capacity: Manpower cost about INR 16.9-17 crore on about 170 employees (about INR 9-10 lakh per head); FY27 existing-staff cost expected to rise to INR 18.5-19 crore with appraisals plus about INR 1.5 crore of new hires.
Three delivery centres (Kolkata, Bhubaneswar, Hyderabad); nine locations in total. 120+ AWS-certified professionals out of 170+ staff.

US billing entity setup initiated; full US office and Singapore expansion contingent on geopolitical situation. Management said a light, fractional-consultant model will be used for global acquisition.
IntelliOps AI operations platform onboarded for more than 60% (later stated 65-70%) of customers; management intends to list it on the AWS marketplace.
demand_pricing: Management described competition as spanning TCS, Infosys and Accenture, Big Four firms, and mid-size cloud peers such as Minfy and Rapyder. Differentiators cited: AWS premier-tier partner status (less than 1% of AWS partners globally), Gen-AI competency, and the highest count of AWS competencies in India.

Pipeline includes Agentic AI platform migration, Gen-AI and data analytics in manufacturing, AI-led transformation for a large insurer, fintech cloud migrations and an NBFC cloud implementation. Management said 7-8 enterprise deals were targeted for closure in Q2.
Enterprise client count rose from 34 to 38; 28 net new clients added; top 20 accounts contributed 73% of revenue; client retention 95%. Management said top-5 concentration has declined.

Management said customers negotiate hard on managed-services and implementation pricing in India, while accepting AWS consumption costs. Hardware prices reportedly doubled or tripled, which management views as a tailwind for cloud migration.

qa_highlights.question: How confident is management of the INR 210 crore FY27 target?
qa_highlights.answer: Anirban Dasgupta said about INR 160 crore is contracted (INR 40 crore per quarter), plus INR 30 crore visibility, giving INR 190.56 crore; the remaining about INR 19 crore must be won over 10 months.

qa_highlights.question: What PAT margin is expected in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Debasish Sarkar said PAT margin would be around the same or higher, equating to about INR 24-25 crore PAT on INR 210 crore revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Will manpower cost rise as revenue scales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the bulk of practice investments are done; existing staff cost goes to about INR 18.5-19 crore with appraisals plus about INR 1.5 crore of new hires. AI tools are expected to let the same headcount deliver more projects.

qa_highlights.question: Is there hardware or GPU cost pass-through risk on annuity contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Anirban Dasgupta said AWS prices have stayed flat or fallen, the platform provides GPU and LLM infrastructure via Bedrock, and there is no cost surprise in existing revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the AI revenue share and is it linked to cloud?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 pure AI services revenue was about INR 2 crore; AI plus cybersecurity targeted at about 5% of FY27 revenue; AI typically pulls through cloud and managed services.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Dubai contract declined?
qa_highlights.answer: Kamal Nath said credit-insurance checks failed for the customer and the replacement entity; the INR 1 crore per month order (about INR 12 crore) was declined on bad-debt risk.

544612|2026-03.headline: FY26 value added revenue rose 12.3% to INR49,180 million with a record 18.8% EBITDA margin; Q4 EBITDA up 17.6% to INR2,573 million.
544612|2026-03.overview: Management reported its best full year yet: FY26 VAR grew 12.3% to INR49,180 million, EBITDA rose 13.5% to INR9,255 million, and EBITDA margin reached a record 18.8% of VAR. Q4 VAR grew 17.5% to INR14,058 million, with EBITDA margin stable at 18.3% despite geopolitical cost pressures. Advanced Ride Technologies drove growth (FY26 up 19.7%), while Clean Air and Powertrain grew only 5.5% for the year. Lifetime order book stood at INR124,000 million at March 31, 2026, with exports and new Clean Air and bearings wins cited as growth drivers.

segments.name: Clean Air and Powertrain Solutions
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR24,296 million, up 5.5% YoY; Q4 INR6,905 million, up 9.9%. Growth tepid due to OEM and within-OEM mix shifts (lower-end SUVs, EV mix at a European OEM), not share loss per management.

segments.name: Advanced Ride Technologies (suspension)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR24,885 million, up 19.7% YoY; Q4 INR7,153 million, up 26%. DCx DaVinci mechanical suspension adopted by a leading Indian OEM for a flagship SUV.

guidance_outlook: Lifetime order book of INR124,000 million gives 100% visibility of FY2028 internal revenue target; management expects double-digit medium-term growth.
Export order book expected to keep growing; current exports are about 5-6% of sales versus a 14-20% share of the order book (as stated).
New West India shock absorber plant (board-approved) expected to take 6-12 months to commission; peak revenue contribution expected mid-2028 to 2029.
Clean Air entry into the largest Indian PV OEM's supplier panel for a Gasoline Particulate Filter; growth expected from late FY27/FY28.
Management expects margins to remain stable going forward.
Addressable Clean Air content from CAFE 3 and BS7 estimated at INR1,300-1,400 crore over the next three to five years.
capex_capacity: Announced capex of about INR1,400 million across the North India Clean Air facility (announced Q3 FY26) and a new greenfield West India Advanced Ride Technologies plant.
FY26 capex was about INR1,150 million.
Bearings business: new plant not yet decided; management is checking whether existing plants can accommodate the new bearings business.
Capex-to-steady-state revenue ratio cited as roughly 1:3.
Localization about 89-90%, management intends to keep it near 90% over the long term.
demand_pricing: Management says the DCx DaVinci suspension has 3-4 OEMs interested, including Indian, Japanese, Korean and European OEMs; it targets about 50% of India's roughly 5-5.5 million PV market.
Conventional mechanical dampers still dominate over 90% of Indian passenger vehicles.
Export drivers cited: technology equalization (BS6.2 with RDE, Euro 6 RDE), China-plus-one sourcing, labour cost advantage and rupee depreciation.

Direct material cost (steel) recovered through quarterly escalator agreements; indirect costs (freight, currency, plastics, rubber, fuel) being recovered through customer negotiations, which management says can be tough.
Management said currency depreciation gives an immediate 15-20% improvement in global competitiveness.

qa_highlights.question: How will exports ramp over the next two to three years, and when will the new plants and bearings orders commission?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports are described as middle-ended, with a critical mass around 2028 and ramp starting 2027-28. The West India plant takes 6-12 months to commission; peak around mid-2028 to 2029. Bearings value not yet disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: What is content per vehicle for commercial vehicle exhaust systems versus passenger vehicles, and how do diesel, petrol, CNG and hybrid differ?
qa_highlights.answer: A commercial exhaust is 3-4x a passenger car system and can reach 10x for tractors with aftertreatment. Diesel carries higher hot-end content. Hybrids can lift content from 1x to 1.5-2x. CNG and hybrid need exhaust systems with no content loss.

qa_highlights.question: Can exports go directly to third-party OEMs or only to Tenneco group entities?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports go both to Tenneco group entities and to third-party OEMs with group permission, which management frames as partnership, not competition.

qa_highlights.question: Why no two-wheeler suspension or Clean Air two-wheeler presence, and is the CV localization point about Clean Air?
qa_highlights.answer: Management avoids low-margin two- and three-wheelers and will enter only with technology differentiation; M&A also being considered. The CV localization reference relates to Clean Air, with localization about 89-90%.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Clean Air growth tepid and what drives the margin expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth was held back by absence from the largest PV OEM and by mix shifts at existing OEMs. Margins attributed to the P3 operating model, standardized Lego-brick product design, and a higher-margin export order book; management expects margins to stay stable.

qa_highlights.question: How do OEMs upgrade from passive to passive-plus or DaVinci suspension, and what is the cost delta?
qa_highlights.answer: Upgrades within mechanical suspension fit the existing packaging envelope with small cost delta. Electronics and software (semi-active CVSA) above about INR35 lakh MSRP need routing and ECU changes, which raise cost substantially.

qa_highlights.question: How are currency movements and indirect cost inflation handled in export contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Currency depreciation is seen as a benefit. Indirect costs (freight, currency, plastics, rubber, LPG, CNG, crude) are being bundled and recovered from customers, with cost-cutting in SG&A and factory efficiency as mitigation.

risks_watch: Clean Air growth lagged the market in FY26 due to OEM mix shifts and absence from the largest PV OEM until FY28.

544613|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 87.5% YoY to Rs 9,008 million, with FY26 EBITDA margin at 18.5% and FY27 revenue guided up 50%.
544613|2026-03.overview: Fujiyama reported a strong March quarter, with revenue of Rs 9,008 million (+87.5% YoY, +53.1% QoQ) and PAT of Rs 1,063 million (11.8% margin). Full-year FY26 revenue was Rs 26,545 million (+72.3%) and PAT Rs 3,041 million (11.5% margin). Capacity expansion continued at Ratlam, with the 2 GW solar panel plant commissioned, though the inverter and battery lines slipped to 2027. A fire at the Bawal lead-acid battery facility (1.3 GW capacity) has suspended operations, with third-party arrangements covering supply. Management guided FY27 revenue up 50% and PAT margin of 11% to 13%.

segments.commentary: Capacity rose from 1,143 MW to 2,180 MW during FY26. Inverter line at Ratlam is expected to be commissioned in Q1 2027.

segments.commentary: Capacity rose from 45 MWh to 545 MWh during FY26. Battery machinery orders are placed, with commissioning expected in Q2 2027.

segments.commentary: Facility with 1.3 GW capacity suspended after a fire; no casualties. Management said it is covered by insurance and third-party capacity is being used.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the increase is mainly raw material for new locations (Dadri, Noida, Ratlam); raw material is above Rs 500 crore of about Rs 900 crore total inventory, and finished goods inventory days are similar to last year. Management expects inventory days to fall once lines ramp up.

qa_highlights.question: Bawal fire: is the facility operational and what is the margin impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Operations are suspended and the cause is under investigation. Management said margin impact is slight, offset by third-party lead-acid capacity bought at good prices, and that the incident will not have a material long-term impact.

qa_highlights.question: BIS seizures: what was affected and what is the penalty exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 10 to 15 of about 500 SKUs, mainly inverters and batteries, are under BIS query. The maximum penalty equals the seizure value, but management expects a lower outcome. It said there is no impact on the Dadri or Ratlam ramp-up or PM Surya Ghar participation.

qa_highlights.question: What are the revenue and margin contributions from the Ratlam and TOPCon cell lines?
qa_highlights.answer: Ratlam peak revenue is about Rs 5,000 crore when fully utilised. The TOPCon cell line adds no revenue, only backward integration and margin benefit. Management said it is passing DCR margin to customers rather than retaining it.

qa_highlights.question: Long-term PAT margin trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided FY27 PAT margin at 11% to 13%, said margins are stable to improving, and cited AI-led opex reduction. It did not give a 36-month target.

544613|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 125.3% YoY to Rs 13,457 mn; EBITDA margin 18.9%, normalized PAT Rs 1,652 mn after Bawal fire exceptional loss of Rs 1,436 mn.
544613|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 125.3% YoY to Rs 13,457 mn and EBITDA rose 140.6% to Rs 2,548 mn, with margin up to 18.9% from 17.7%. A Rs 1,436 mn provisional exceptional loss from the Bawal facility fire brought reported PAT to Rs 578 mn (4.3% margin), while normalized PAT was Rs 1,652 mn (12.3%). Management raised full-year revenue growth guidance to about 70% from 50%, kept the margin guidance at "sustainable to improve," and added distributors, dealers and two states. Ratlam capacity additions (2 GW solar panel, 2 GW power electronics, 2 GW battery due Q2 FY27) and stake increases in Zayo entities were the main capex and integration moves.

financial_highlights.change: expected to be fully recovered via insurance

financial_highlights.metric: Normalized PAT (ex post-tax fire provision Rs 1,074 mn)

segments.name: Residential rooftop / B2C
segments.commentary: Management said about 90% of revenue comes from the B2C channel. Sales are sold as a package of panels, inverters and batteries; no segment-wise revenue split was given.

segments.name: Off-grid vs on-grid vs hybrid
segments.commentary: Management said on-grid growth was the main driver this quarter, enabled by in-house DCR cells; off-grid is still growing but more slowly. No split was disclosed.

segments.name: Tubular batteries
segments.commentary: Tubular battery output (about 10% of revenue) was lost in the Bawal fire; management estimated the gross margin impact at below 0.5% as batteries are now bought from outside vendors.

qa_highlights.answer: Management raised FY27 revenue growth guidance to about 70% from 50%, citing demand and Ratlam capacity, and said it will trail the guidance upward as the year progresses.

qa_highlights.question: Will backward integration lift margins or be passed on to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said DCR cell capacity supports margins but raw material price volatility is a factor, and it will pass on part of the gains; margin guidance remains 'sustainable to improve'.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Bawal fire loss is recoverable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the damaged assets with net carrying value about Rs 143 cr are fully insured, the survey is done, the full loss was booked in Q1, and claim settlement is expected by year end.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Rs 26-30 per watt figure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is an average distributor BOM (roughly Rs 15 panel, Rs 5 inverter, Rs 5 battery), varying with DCR/non-DCR, battery type and system type, with GST included.

qa_highlights.question: Capex funding for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no equity dilution this year; about Rs 200 cr of the Rs 500 cr additional capex will be debt-funded, with Rs 100 cr from IPO proceeds and Rs 200 cr from internal accruals.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the TOPCon line and the lead-acid plant after the fire?
qa_highlights.answer: TOPCon commissioning is targeted within about 9 months. The fire-hit lead-acid plant will not restart until insurance work is done; the company is in talks to lease an operating plant.

544614|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 26% YoY to INR191 crore and adjusted EBITDA margin hit about 19%; SessionM acquisition closed May 1, 2026.

Q4 PAT of INR43 crore included a one-time INR25 crore churn-indemnity income from the Kognitiv acquisition; normalized PAT was INR19.6 crore. FY26 revenue reached INR734 crore (+23%), adjusted EBITDA INR107 crore (+43%, ~14.7% margin) and normalized PAT about INR32 crore. Management also closed the SessionM (Mastercard merchant loyalty) acquisition on May 1, 2026, and cited a $20 million Fortune 500 retail win.

qa_highlights.question: What synergies and revenue visibility come from SessionM?

qa_highlights.question: How do ARR (INR765 crore) and ACV (INR121 crore) link, and what drives the gap?

qa_highlights.question: Why are costs growing near revenue growth when headcount is flat?

544614|2026-06.headline: Capillary Q1 FY27 revenue rose 43% YoY to INR256 crore and adjusted EBITDA to INR44 crore (~17%), with organic growth at 17%.
544614|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR256 crore, up 43% YoY, with two months of SessionM (acquired May 1, 2026) contributing; organic growth was 17% and currency added about 6%. Adjusted EBITDA was INR44 crore (about 17-18% margin) versus INR19 crore a year earlier, and reported PAT was -INR9.5 crore, or INR25 crore normalised after excluding a cyber-fraud loss and a one-time deferred tax charge. ARR reached INR1,026 crore (+34% YoY), and trailing-12-month new ACV excluding one large healthcare win was about INR92 crore (+75%). Management kept FY27 guidance of INR1,065 crore revenue and INR172 crore EBITDA unchanged, saying it expects to beat both.

qa_highlights.answer: No SessionM migrations before end-2026/early 2027; the full base is expected to take 2-3 years. 3-4 of ~45 customers are being fast-tracked; margins will improve through server cost cuts (SessionM server costs are ~50% of revenue vs ~7-9% at Capillary).

qa_highlights.question: Organic vs inorganic growth split and FX effect?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 organic growth was 17%; FX contributed about 6%; the rest is SessionM's two months. Cash is about half USD and half INR, which gives a natural hedge with the US at ~60% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Is the cyber-fraud loss covered by insurance?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, the bank-account fraud at a subsidiary is insured, but the amount and timing of recovery are not yet clear. No customer or employee data was exposed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the organic NRR breakdown and churn?
qa_highlights.answer: Price escalators and overage are 4-5% of NRR; upsell and new cohorts add ~10%; churn is ~5%.

qa_highlights.question: Are the aiRA figures net of cannibalisation and what are the economics?
qa_highlights.answer: ARR is ~USD2.5 million with no cannibalisation so far; gross and contribution margins are above 80%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the SessionM purchase price INR17 crore when the deal was USD20 million?
qa_highlights.answer: The USD20 million enterprise value was adjusted for net debt at closing; the final true-up on April 30 brought the value to about INR17 crore; the entities are debt-free.

544617|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 16% YoY to ₹812 mn, but EBITDA margin fell to 30.3% from 40.5% on a ₹85 mn-per-quarter US near-shore team cost booked in other expenses.
544617|2026-03.overview: Excelsoft reported Q4 FY26 revenue of ₹812 mn (up 16% YoY) and FY26 revenue of ₹2,725 mn (down from the ₹3,333 mn stated for FY25, although management described FY26 growth as 17%). Q4 EBITDA fell 13% YoY to ₹246 mn and PAT fell to ₹166 mn from ₹205 mn, as other expenses rose 76% to ₹209 mn on a 30-person US near-shore consultant team hired from January. Management said the cost is a one-off that will lift margins back to about 30-31%, and it flagged a planned UK awarding-body (AQA) announcement and a renewed acquisition push under new CEO Doreswamy Palaniswamy.
