EBITDA rose 29.78% to INR130.31 million, but margin contracted about 178 bps to 16.24% due to nearshore build-out, international sales hiring, one-time recruitment and AI training costs. PAT rose 57.13% to INR92.28 million, helped by lower interest cost. Management guided FY27 revenue of INR350-360 crore and year-end EBITDA margin of 24-25%.

qa_highlights.question: Why are margins guided at 24-25% when earlier commentary implied 30-31% for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the earlier view excluded sales hiring and internal capability costs. It chose a conservative 24-25% EBITDA target, with possible further AI-related investment, and expects faster top-line growth to offset percentage margin pressure.

qa_highlights.question: Are the one-time costs confined to FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth of 30%-plus needs investment, and further spend may be required, so it would not commit to margin recovery beyond 25%.

qa_highlights.answer: Q1 is typically 20-22% of annual revenue. Management guided INR350-360 crore, and said INR400 crore was not committed.

qa_highlights.question: How much AQA revenue is booked and what is the scale?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR2.5 crore booked in Q1 with billing started; INR12-15 crore expected in FY27. Four-year visibility is roughly USD17 million, with upside.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Three targets: one US and two India. Non-binding offers issued for two; one is in final negotiation stage, with outcome expected in a couple of weeks.

qa_highlights.question: Will nearshore expansion compromise margins?

qa_highlights.question: Why did PAT exceed EBIT by so much?

544619|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 27.9% to INR642.3 crores and PAT to INR174.3 crores, but EBITDA margin fell to 34.6% and working capital days rose to 213.
544619|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue from operations grew 27.9% YoY to INR642.3 crores, with EBITDA up 16.8% to INR221.9 crores and PAT up to INR174.3 crores from INR138.7 crores. Q4 FY26 revenue grew 15.7% to INR182.3 crores, with EBITDA of INR62.6 crores at a 34.3% margin. Specialty ingredients grew 62% to INR280 crores and rose to 44% of revenue, while pharma, food and nutrition grew 10%. Working capital days increased from 184 to 213 on higher raw material and finished goods inventory, and management targets 150-160 days within FY27.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume growth exceeded 20% with a mix shift; the phosphate price pass-through started in Q1. Margin was diluted by glycinate and gluconate running on a small temporary line, and by hiring for the greenfield plant. Management expects about 15% EBITDA growth in FY27 and FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise sharply in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited about INR3 crores CSR spend, about INR1.5 crores of LPG premium costs in March, and about INR2 crores of air freight to the largest customer. These are expected to fall in Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How much battery material volume is expected in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is commercially making battery-grade iron phosphate in the existing pharma facility (5,000-7,000 MT capacity), with about half for commercial orders. It agreed that about 2,500 MT of sales in FY27 is a fair assumption.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex and revenue economics for battery materials?
qa_highlights.answer: The INR600 crores covers 100,000 MT including land and Phase 2 infrastructure, so it is not INR300 crores per 25,000 MT. Revenue potential at full capacity is INR1,600-1,800 crores.

qa_highlights.question: What is the non-battery revenue potential and margin path?
qa_highlights.answer: Without incremental capex, the existing portfolio can scale to INR1,000-1,200 crores. Margin should recover toward the historical 24-25% (per the management answer), and bisglycinate should add higher-margin revenue from FY28.

qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify margins or a realisation premium for battery materials and new molecules, citing confidentiality. It did say bisglycinate realisation is about four times the current portfolio, and that competition is mainly with a US market leader on performance rather than price.

544619|2026-06.headline: Sudeep Pharma Q1 FY27 revenue rose 27% YoY to INR158.3 crore, with EBITDA margin at 34.7% despite an LPG-driven specialty slowdown.
544619|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations grew 27% YoY to INR158.3 crore and EBITDA rose 25% to INR54.9 crore, with margin at 34.7%. PAT increased to INR40.6 crore (PAT margin 25.6%). Pharma, food and nutrition (PFN) grew 31% (management also cited 30% in Q&A), mainly on volume from phosphates. Specialty ingredients grew 19% after LPG shortages in April and first half of May cut utilisation, and NSS (European subsidiary) was weak due to energy costs at a major infant formula customer in Ireland. Management said specialty and PFN momentum should continue into Q2, with price pass-through on phosphates mainly landing in Q2.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Greenfield Nandesari FDA approval expected in Q1 FY27 with supplies from Q3 FY27, and Bisglycinate has two large North American customers approved; Phase 2 HPMC/PVP excipients are not expected this financial year.

rows.label: Two binding SAM off-take agreements
rows.why: Two binding off-takes are expected later in CY2026 and gate the 100 to 200 KTPA scale-up, with 8 customers already qualified and 2 MOUs with South Korean cathode makers signed in Q1.

rows.why: Q1 Absorbis sales already exceed full FY26 sales and two large North American customers are approved, though deliveries are behind schedule and management expects a top 2-3 PFN product within 2-3 years.

544619|2026-09.headline: Sudeep Pharma Q2 FY27 revenue rose 21% YoY to INR196.7 crore with EBITDA margin of 37.2%, a record quarter despite Fortified Rice pause.
544619|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 was the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue and EBITDA, with revenue up 21% YoY and 24% QoQ, and EBITDA margin up about 310 bps YoY to 37.2%. Pharma Food Nutrition (PFN) drove growth, rising 57% YoY, while Specialty Ingredients fell 25% YoY after the Government's Fortified Rice programme paused. PAT grew only 11% YoY to INR51.8 crore because of lower other income, a higher effective tax rate of 27%, and new greenfield depreciation. Management guided to positive YoY growth in Specialty Ingredients in Q3 and Q4 and kept the Dahej battery-materials start date of April 2027.

segments.name: Specialty Ingredients

Specialty margin expected to recover toward pre-Q2 levels in Q3 and Q4, per management.

Magnesium bisglycinate targeted to become a top-3 PFN revenue contributor within 2-3 years, with potential of at least INR100 crore.
Margins expected to be sustained at current levels, but greenfield operating costs and battery costs will start hitting the P&L as commissioning nears.
Binding offtake details for the battery business expected in the next call or within two months.

Specialty Ingredients utilisation around 40-45% in FY26, expected to recover to about 40-45% by Q4 FY27.

Dahej battery plant: Phase 1 of 25,000 tpa commercial operations from April 2027; scale-up to 100,000 tpa and then 200,000 tpa. Management referred to about INR600 crore capex for the first 100,000 tpa.
FY27 capex about INR77 crore, mainly battery project at Dahej and greenfield completion. Battery inventory is being built up ahead of commissioning.
demand_pricing: Phosphoric acid prices rose about 40% vs Q4 FY26 by Q1 FY27 and strengthened further; pass-through was executed and Q1 inventory built ahead of price increases supported Q2 and October-November.

Export share about 65% of revenue (exports up 24% YoY), domestic about 35%.

qa_highlights.question: What is Specialty Ingredients underlying growth excluding Fortified Rice, and what growth is expected in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Fortified Rice was about 20-25% of segment revenue (INR40-50 crore in FY26). Premix was hit by product mix change even though volumes grew. Non-Fortified Rice premix contracts for Q3 and Q4 are expected to largely offset the loss.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the Specialty margin fall while PFN margins rose sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to operating leverage: premix, a large contributor, had limited revenue, and NSS was a drag. Q3 and Q4 contracts are expected to carry better margins than the Fortified Rice business they replace.

qa_highlights.question: Is the PFN growth from volume or pricing, and what is the PFN volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth came mainly from phosphates (up about 70-80%) and magnesium bisglycinate, which received the maximum capacity allocation in the existing setup. PFN volume grew about 30-35% in Q2 and about 19% in H1.

qa_highlights.question: How will bisglycinate be distributed across customers, and how much of Nandesari capacity can go to it?
qa_highlights.answer: About 50% of bisglycinate volume will go to larger customers, including two of the largest US tolling manufacturers, and 50% to mid/small customers, to avoid concentration. About 70-80% of the 40% of capacity allocated to other products would go to bisglycinate; the remaining 60% of the greenfield is mainly phosphates and is not easily fungible.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Phase 1 battery capacity is covered by binding offtake agreements?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give volume detail today, saying the company would break it out by customer and volume at the next call or within two months. Binding commitments are targeted for Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the battery pricing premium and return profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Pricing is set at a slight premium to China, driven by US 45X PFE-compliant supply rules, and capped by competitiveness. Management targets asset turns of about 3x and ROCE similar to the core business, and will not guide EBITDA margin for the battery business.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Phase 1 plant approval needed for Korean customers, and how long does validation take?
qa_highlights.answer: Plant approval for the Dahej site is expected to take 3-6 months because product and process approval is already in place. Management assumes about half a year of FY28 for commercial supply and revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the NSS revenue and margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 is expected to be flat. FY28 growth should be similar to the core business, and the NSS target EBITDA margin is close to 30% after supply chain changes.

544626|2026-03.headline: Exato Technologies FY26 revenue rose about 35% to Rs 168 crore and PAT about 67% to Rs 16.09 crore, with management guiding 50-60% growth for FY27.
544626|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue from operations grew about 35% to Rs 168 crore and PAT grew about 67% to Rs 16.09 crore, with PAT margin up from 7.77% to 9.58%. Q4 EBITDA margin fell, which management attributed to heavy investment in US and Australia hiring, travel, events and leadership additions. Management said the order book closed at about Rs 600 crore (up from about Rs 520 crore in December), and it is pivoting toward international markets, AI-as-a-service, ERP and an infrastructure (hardware) line. Q4 showed a sharp rise in purchase of software and hardware, which analysts questioned as margin-diluting.

segments.commentary: Management expects this to contribute 30-35% of revenue within 2-3 years and cited larger deals in pipeline; it was earlier a Cisco/HP business, now being rebuilt as a dedicated vertical.

Management expects BPO/KPO and healthcare to remain the core verticals; BFSI (insurance) is a focus.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI infrastructure deals and customers spending IT budgets in Q4 drove higher resale purchases; these are sold to customers, so they cannot be capitalised. Hardware margins are lower on transactional deals, and a dedicated infrastructure vertical with OEMs (HP, Cisco) is intended to improve margins.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY26 revenue and PAT guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided 50-60% growth in both revenue and PAT, calling it the minimum, driven by international geographies, bigger deal sizes and hybrid delivery.

qa_highlights.question: What share of revenue is from exports, and how does margin differ?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports were about 28-30% of FY26 revenue per management; target 50-55% in two years. Gross margin is 22-24% domestic and 30-35% international.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Rs 380 crore unexecuted order book will bill in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: About 30-35% of the Rs 380 crore will be billed in FY27, with the rest over 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan and timeline to grow from 150 to 500-600 customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Target set at 3-4 years, supported by an inside sales team of about 20 people, a US senior hire from Tata Communications, and a planned event with about 2,500 customer database contacts.

qa_highlights.question: What are the customer and order book breakup, and is the 60% international target on track?
qa_highlights.answer: About 75% of the Rs 600 crore order book is BPO/KPO, 20% BFSI, 5% other. Management said 50-60% international revenue is a 2-3 year target, with US, Singapore and Australia push; FY26 international share was about 24% per the management's own statement on the call.

IP/ExatoIQ revenue: start is expected this month or next, with two deals said to be near signing; margin guidance of 40-50% and customer names not yet disclosed.

key_quotes: Our expectation is that revenue will grow at least 60 to 70% , or even more than that, and profitability will also be growing more than 70 to 80%.

Rather than commenting specifically on this, because I cannot comment too much on ongoing matters, being a listed company, the way I am looking at it is that the company we want to acquire should have something we want to build.
So, approximately 30 and 30, or 25? Our focus is going to be CX; that is what creates the differentiation for us.

544631|2026-03.headline: Creative Newtech FY26 consolidated total income rose 50.85% to INR2,717.51 crores, with PAT of INR70.29 crores, while Q4 receivables built up to about 20% of turnover.
544631|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 consolidated total income of INR2,717.51 crores (up 50.85%), EBITDA of INR104 crores (up 41.7%, margin 3.83%) and PAT of INR70.29 crores (up 32.35%, margin 2.59%). Q4 FY26 total income was INR740.44 crores with EBITDA of INR29.39 crores and PAT of INR17.79 crores. Brand business (Honeywell, CyberPower and audio/air purifier lines) reached INR369.61 crores, 14.1% of revenue, against guidance of INR350-360 crores. Management flagged the Middle East war and container freight costs (Red Sea route cost up from about $1,500-1,700 to $7,500-8,000 per container) as headwinds to Middle East brand sales, and memory, storage and CPU costs up 30-40%.

segments.name: Own brand (Vertual, launched May 2026)
segments.commentary: New in-house brand with air purifier and similar Honeywell categories, to launch first online in the US (Amazon warehouses already stocked) and in India, with material available from 22-23 May 2026. guidance_outlook: Internal target of at least 25-30% annual revenue growth and 30% absolute profit growth over the next 5-6 years; management says growth rate is ambitious but achievable for about 3-4 years.
Brand business targeted to grow 50-60% a year; Honeywell alone at least 40-50%; Honeywell brand expected to grow about 50% in FY27.
Brand business EBITDA expected at about 13% now, aiming for 17-18% at INR1,000 crore scale; long-run EBIT target 18-19% above INR1,000 crores.
Vision of a 50:50 market entry to brand split by 2030; aspiration to reach 3-4 brands near term and 6-7 long term, with 2-3 brands above INR1,000 crores.
Plan to separate brand and market entry businesses in 2-3 years, with a demerger process that could start after about 15 months; no plan in the next 15 months.
Middle East brand sales could fall to about 50% of current levels if shipments stay disrupted; management says price hikes and consumer sentiment may hit margins in FY27.
capex_capacity: Intangible assets rose to INR406 crores on ERP migration (Microsoft Business Central) with CRM and supply chain modules, new servers and software licences.
New distribution centre opened in Noida; new offices and set-up teams in Delhi and other locations for new businesses.
Working capital expected to be funded through debt and internal accruals for the next 15 months; equity raise only for an acquisition of about 30% of company size or a brand purchase.
Management is actively looking to acquire a surveillance/AI brand with a legacy, team and sales; expects a small acquired business (INR5 crore) could scale to INR10 crores in a year.
Brand business inventory: company holds 30-40 days of inventory to secure supply and hedge price increases; partners hold 45-60 days stock in Middle East.
demand_pricing: Management says price escalation is possible but demand should hold for 3-4 years, supported by India demographics, government push on AI, digital infrastructure and Make-in-India.

Higher Q4 gross and EBITDA margins attributed to Make-in-India surveillance and AI customers (PSU or government end-users) served via smaller vendors; management expects this margin mix to flow to the bottom line over time.
Raw material costs for memory, storage and CPUs up 30-40%; management says costs are being passed on but customers are beginning to feel the pressure and consumption may fall.

Brand categories: audio market about INR25,000 crores (India and abroad), air purifiers about INR3,000 crores in India, data-centre cables about INR4,000 crores in India; US air purifier market about INR28,000 crores, with about INR8,000 crores sold on Amazon.

Honeywell air purifier and accessories ambition is to be number 1 or 2 in India; air purifier currently close to number 2. Quick commerce grew over 100% across India, UAE and Saudi Arabia; 1 product sold every 60 seconds online in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Would demerging the higher-return Honeywell brand business unlock value?
qa_highlights.answer: Management plans separate brand and market entry businesses within 2-3 years, but there is no plan for the next 15 months; a demerger process is about 12-15 months and would start once the brand reaches about INR1,000 crores.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the Middle East war on the business?
qa_highlights.answer: Freight on Red Sea routes rose from about $1,500-1,700 to $7,500-8,000 per container; short-term impact is manageable given 45-60 days of partner stock, but a prolonged disruption could halve Middle East brand business.

qa_highlights.question: Why were Q4 gross and EBITDA margins high?
qa_highlights.answer: Make-in-India surveillance and AI customers, served through smaller vendors, carry higher margins, and the mix is expected to scale as government demand for AI, IoT and data centres grows.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivables rise to about 20% of turnover and how will they normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 turnover roughly doubled to INR721 crores from INR393 crores; extended credit for new AI, surveillance and data centre lines is expected to normalise receivables back toward 13-14% of turnover.

qa_highlights.question: Why did finance costs stay low despite higher short-term debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt excluding MSME supply-chain finance rose only to INR83.72 crores from INR69.53 crores; the rest is about INR171 crores of government TReDS-type MSME payment finance at around 8-9% that started in the last two quarters, so only about 8 months of interest was incurred.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Honeywell licence be renewed and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Licence expires March 2027; management is very confident of renewal, citing Honeywell's 22-23 year average licences and its split into five companies, with two separated and two more by July-August 2026.

Input cost inflation of 30-40% in memory, storage and CPUs, with customers starting to resist price hikes and consumption possibly falling.
Receivables at about 20% of turnover (INR565 crores) versus 13.4% last year; management targets return to 13-14% and inventory is also rising.
Honeywell licence renewal due March 2027; a new licence and trademark terms will need to be confirmed.
Working capital and MSME supply-chain finance (about INR171 crores) rising; watch debt levels and interest costs in coming quarters.
Acquisition plans in surveillance/AI brands and the own-brand launch (Vertual) add execution and funding risk; watch marketing spend of INR10-12 crores.

544631|2026-09.headline: Creative Newtech Q2 FY27 EBITDA rose 50.70% YoY to INR40.11 crores on total income growth of 14.43%, with H1 PAT up 35.49% to INR39.47 crores.
544631|2026-09.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 total income of INR754.8 crores (+14.43% YoY), EBITDA of INR40.11 crores with margin up to 5.31% from 4.04%, and PAT of INR25.94 crores (+36.88%). H1 FY27 EBITDA grew 55.78% to INR65.01 crores on total income growth of 16.55%, and operating cash flow reached INR351.24 crores. Management highlighted a won BSNL BharatNet Middle Mile advance work order (INR3,194.83 crores), the pending Infinova India acquisition, and the WOZOYO consumer brand launch. Brand business share of revenue rose from 14% in FY26 to 17% in H1 and 19% in Q2.

segments.name: Brand business (Honeywell, WOZOYO, CyberPowerPC)

segments.name: Market entry / distribution business
segments.commentary: Management said gross profit percentage in this business rose ~200 bps and consolidated GP rose ~350 bps, with the business moving toward higher-margin technology and digital infrastructure work.

segments.name: WOZOYO (Hong Kong subsidiary Secure Connection Limited)
segments.commentary: Launched in the US end-July 2026; ~$2.2 million (~INR20 crores) sold in first three months through end-September. FY27 target of INR45-50 crores across India and US; India launch of air purifiers for Diwali.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at roughly 20% (per Chairman, 'roughly give and take'), versus 14% in Q2 and 16.55% in H1 total income.
BSNL BharatNet project: INR150-200 crores revenue expected in Q4 FY27 and INR500-600 crores in FY28; capex ~INR1,700 crores over ~3.5 years; net profit ~6-7% of billed value.
Brand business: ~INR475-500 crores revenue for Honeywell plus WOZOYO in FY27; WOZOYO INR100-150 crores next year; targeted INR2,400 crores brand revenue by FY29.

Infinova: acquisition completion targeted before 15 November 2026 (possibly ~15 days more for share transfer); STQC-led sales reflection expected around January-February 2027; first-year target INR75-80 crores.
Working capital days expected to normalise to 52-55 days long term (CFO).
Management said to model 8% PAT as a conservative brand-business assumption.

Infinova India acquisition: six agreements being signed; completion expected before 15 November 2026; Infinova has a small factory and assembly unit.
Company-run data centre for SNOC, ~INR50 crores capex, built for government prequalification.
Super Micro tie-up for AI servers/GPU and HPC; a large deal under discussion (not confirmed).
First AVGC lab set up at Karnavati University, Ahmedabad (CyberPowerPC-linked).
Management said it may raise equity only for a larger acquisition; currently banks supportive and cash flows good.
demand_pricing: WOZOYO US: ~50% of sales spent on Amazon Marketing Services currently, expected to fall to 12-14% after ~$1 million in sales; return rate ~3.5-4% vs 8-9% typical; Amazon Choice for docking stations.
WOZOYO brand marketing budget INR20-22 crores from balance sheet; ~INR12 crores spent on brand to date.
Management expects strong air purifier season in India due to weather and AQI conditions.

Management estimates India air purifier market at INR2,000 crores (CAGR ~24%), US air purifier market at ~INR28,000-30,000 crores; India electronic essentials ~INR10,000 crores; India surveillance ~INR30,000 crores with one large competitor at INR5,000-5,500 crores.
Management says the company will not agree to consignment or sale-or-return terms with online platforms.

qa_highlights.question: What WOZOYO product categories and channels show traction, and what KPIs will be tracked?
qa_highlights.answer: Air purifiers and docking stations lead; US channels are Amazon, TikTok and Walmart/Best Buy. KPIs are returns (3-3.5% now vs 8-9% typical), reviews and Vine program; India launch via Blinkit, Swiggy and Amazon with FY27 WOZOYO target of INR45-50 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline and capability rationale for the Infinova acquisition?
qa_highlights.answer: Completion targeted before 15 November 2026. Infinova is a high-end camera maker serving smart cities, borders and airports, with STQC certification planned to meet government requirements; sales impact expected from January-February 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Brand spend and margin trajectory for FY28-FY29 and the INR2,400 crores FY29 goal?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said brand share rose to 19% in Q2 and is targeted at ~40% by FY29, with PAT of 10-11%. Chairman said the INR2,400 crores target rests on WOZOYO, Honeywell, Infinova and CyberPowerPC plus a possible fifth brand, and suggested 8% PAT as a conservative assumption.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 45 working-capital-day level sustainable, and what is the BSNL revenue timing?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said 45 days benefited from vendor negotiations and debtor days were 75 in Q1 falling to 65; long-term normal is 52-55 days. BSNL revenue of INR150-200 crores is expected in Q4 FY27 and INR500-600 crores in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Current brand PAT, and does PAT grow with revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said brand PAT is ~11-12% currently. Chairman said that at larger scale (INR1,000-1,200 crores per brand) margins would be 8-10%, as current spending is below what the company would want to deploy in brand building.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 revenue growth of ~20% achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said roughly yes, about 20% for the full year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q2 sales strength shifted by Diwali timing, and is NWC of 45 days steady state?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said Diwali shifted about a month earlier this year, moving some sales into Q2 with Q3 also expected to be strong. CFO said 45 days is not sustainable and 52-55 days is the expected range.

544632|2026-03.headline: Meesho says logistics disruption in Q2–Q3 FY26 is behind it; Q4 contribution margin exit rate of 4% is the new baseline.
544632|2026-03.overview: Management described Q4 FY26 as a strong quarter, with contribution margin up about 170 bps QoQ, of which roughly 110 bps came from lower logistics cost. The 145 bps one-time logistics headwind was concentrated in Q2 and Q3 FY26 and attributed to short-term capacity building during 3PL consolidation around May 2025. Ad revenue as a percentage of NMV rose QoQ, while reported revenue per order looked flat partly due to accounting changes (first-order discounts now netted against revenue) and a higher prepaid mix. Management gave no EBITDA break-even or FCF timing guidance; it pointed to LTM FCF as the guiding metric, and Q4 cash balance fell about INR300 crore, which management partly attributed to tax payments expected to be recovered.

544632|2026-09.headline: Meesho Q2 FY27 contribution margin rose to about 6%, driven mainly by logistics efficiencies, with management reinvesting part of the gain into pricing.

Adjusted EBITDA margin was about minus 1% of NMV, with a quarterly FCF print helped by a roughly INR523 crore working capital release tied to festive-season timing shifting into September. Festive season sales were described as better than expectations, with traffic at all-time highs, though seller-side supply disruptions from crude and Middle East volatility were flagged.

544634|2026-03.headline: Aequs FY26 revenue rose 33% to INR12,304 million with a record Q4 of INR3,671 million; FY27 guides 45-50% consolidated growth and consumer EBITDA breakeven by Q4 FY27.
544634|2026-03.overview: FY26 consolidated revenue grew 33% to INR12,304 million and EBITDA grew 43% to INR1,545 million (13% margin), but full-year PAT was a loss of INR1,133 million. Q4 was the highest-ever quarter at INR3,671 million revenue, yet EBITDA margin fell to 9% as consumer electronics capacity, commissioned in Q3, carried full depreciation and fixed costs at about 23% utilisation. Aerospace carried the year (revenue INR10,464 million, EBITDA margin about 27%), while consumer EBITDA loss widened to INR783 million. Management also announced two state MoUs for about INR4,756 crores of multi-year capex, the CFO's exit at end-June 2026, and the loss of Hasbro volumes offset by a Mattel long-term agreement.

segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR10,464 million (+27%), EBITDA INR2,813 million (+76%); Q4 revenue INR3,040 million (+29%), EBITDA INR1,010 million. Portfolio grew to 5,654 SKUs (+26% YoY, 433 added in Q4); order book USD 889 million.

segments.name: Consumer
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR1,840 million (+84%), EBITDA loss INR783 million. Capacity utilisation at 23%, targeted at 40-50% by FY27 year-end; FY27 consumer revenue growth guided at 125-150%.

Consumer EBITDA breakeven targeted by Q4 FY27; long-term consumer EBITDA goal of about 20%, with 18-20% expected at roughly 75-80% utilisation.
Consolidated PAT expected to reach breakeven by H1 FY28; depreciation keeps PAT negative for much of FY27.
FY27 capex of about INR500 crores in consumer and about INR160 crores in aerospace; PLI eligibility begins in FY27 (none booked in FY26). Interest expense expected to fall versus FY26.
Consumer gross block about INR830 crores; asset turn expected near 1.5x at peak; INR2,000 crore consumer turnover on about INR1,330 crore gross block was indicated as closer to FY29.

Fleet of 434 CNC machines and 179 moulding machines at FY26 close.

MoU with Karnataka (Mar 2026): INR2,856 crores over five years across Belagavi (aerospace precision) and Hubballi (consumer capacity).

Consumer capacity utilisation at 23%; management said the customer relationship requires scaling and that alternates would be sought otherwise.
demand_pricing: Hasbro informed Aequs it has revised its manufacturing and sourcing strategy and will stop raising purchase orders; management said overall consumer growth will not be impacted.
Long-term agreement signed with Mattel; management expects Mattel volumes to absorb the Hasbro capacity impact.
Aerospace order book USD 889 million, roughly 8-9x FY26 aerospace revenue per analyst framing; management is moving into engine and landing gear components, with engine revenue starting FY28.
About 93-94% of revenue is USD-linked including deemed exports.
Aluminium/steel and titanium lead times cited at 65-75 weeks and 52 weeks respectively; buffer stock raised to about 125% of quarterly needs from about 70%.
Plastics prices rose in the quarter but are passed through to consumer customers under back-to-back agreements.

qa_highlights.answer: Aerospace capex about INR160 crores and consumer about INR500 crores for FY27. Mattel LTA signed. No PLI income booked in FY26; FY27 is the first eligible year.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the West Asia crisis on margins and working capital?
qa_highlights.answer: Management saw no significant margin impact in Q4; the working capital build reflects inventory held 4-6 weeks ahead, expected for about two more quarters. Air freight is up 6-8 days and sea freight 5-6 weeks.

qa_highlights.question: Reconciling FY26 aerospace 27% margin with 20% FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: The 27% is segment EBITDA including other income and before unallocated corporate costs; the like-for-like operating margin is about 20%.

qa_highlights.question: Why add consumer capex with utilisation at 23%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the customer wants a meaningful share of India requirements; the capex is customer-driven and the asset base will ramp, with utilisation targeted at 40-50%.

qa_highlights.question: Consumer revenue potential from INR500 crore capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided utilisation to 50% and consumer growth of about 125% this year; no revenue figure was given for the capex.

qa_highlights.question: Long-term aerospace growth beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a multi-year opportunity at 20-plus% growth and said the engine component contribution starts in FY28, with FY27 growth predominantly from aerostructures.

qa_highlights.question: Depreciation and interest run-rate for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 depreciation was about INR45-46 crores, plus additions from capex; interest expense expected to decline versus FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Consumer margin path and steady-state utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins are driven by utilisation; 18-20% margins are expected around 75-80% utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Consumer funding for the planned capex?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex to be funded by borrowings and some internal accruals; a breakdown was deferred offline.
